title: Lead Éclairage / Lighting Lead - TV Featurette
description:
NOTRE HISTOIRE

Depuis plus de 35 ans, Bardel Entertainment ne cesse de grandir et d’évoluer, tout en restant fidèle à ses racines créatives et à l’art de l’animation. Notre quête d’idées nouvelles, de techniques innovantes et de technologies de pointe est guidée par la conviction qu’ensemble, grâce à la créativité et à la collaboration, tout est possible ! Si vous souhaitez faire partie d’un environnement qui vous encourage à expérimenter, apprendre et contribuer à des projets passionnants, rejoignez-nous.

OUR STORY

For more than 35 years, Bardel Entertainment has been growing and evolving, yet at our core, we remain grounded in the creative roots of the craft of animation. Our pursuit of fresh ideas, techniques, and technologies is driven by the belief that together, through creativity and collaboration, we can accomplish anything! If you want to be part of an environment that empowers you to experiment, learn, and contribute to exciting projects, come and join us.

Le Lead du Lighting est responsable de diriger les équipes de lighting et de compositing afin de délivrer le look souhaité et la qualité visuelle d'un long métrage d'animation. Ce rôle assure la continuité de la vision artistique tout au long de la production, tout en gérant les défis techniques et de production.

Responsabilités:

  • Superviser l'équipe de lighting afin d’atteindre le style visuel souhaité pour le long métrage d’animation, en respectant la direction artistique du projet.
  • Assurer et maintenir la qualité, la cohérence et la continuité de l’éclairage à travers tous les plans du film.
  • Collaborer étroitement avec le Superviseur CG pour évaluer la faisabilité technique des designs d’éclairage, en proposant des solutions adaptées aux contraintes de production, tout en respectant la vision du réalisateur.
  • Participer à la répartition des tâches en concertation avec le Réalisateur et le Superviseur CG, en tenant compte des compétences et des forces de chaque artiste afin d’optimiser le flux de travail.
  • Revoir régulièrement le travail des artistes lighting, fournir des retours constructifs, et valider les plans avant soumission au Réalisateur.
  • Guider et encadrer l’équipe lighting pour atteindre le look souhaité, en équilibrant les exigences artistiques avec les contraintes de production (temps, budget, ressources).
  • Collaborer avec les départements connexes (compositing, FX, surfacing, layout, etc.) pour assurer une intégration harmonieuse de l’éclairage dans les plans finaux.
  • Identifier et résoudre les défis techniques et créatifs liés à l’éclairage, en garantissant des résultats de haute qualité au service de la narration et de l’émotion.
  • Garantir la continuité visuelle des séquences, en veillant à la cohérence du style d’éclairage sur l’ensemble du film.
  • Travailler avec la gestion de production pour s’assurer du respect des délais et du budget, et proposer des ajustements si nécessaire pour maintenir les objectifs de production.
  • Développer et superviser le pipeline de lighting : méthodologies, outils, planning, ressources et assignations.
  • Maintenir une documentation claire et à jour pour l’équipe lighting et les autres départements concernés.
  • Assurer une communication fluide au sein de l’équipe et avec les autres départements impliqués dans la production.
  • Participer activement à l’amélioration continue des procédures, outils et workflows pour optimiser l’efficacité et la qualité du département lighting.
  • Fournir des retours réguliers sur les performances des artistes lighting et les accompagner dans leur développement.
  • Participer au processus de recrutement des artistes lighting, en collaboration avec les ressources humaines et la production.

The Lighting Lead is responsible for leading the lighting and compositing teams to deliver the desired look and visual quality of an animated feature film. The role ensures the continuity of artistic vision throughout the production, while also managing technical and production challenges.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Lead the lighting and compositing teams to deliver the expected and desired visual style of the feature film.
  • Ensure and maintain the quality and consistency of lighting and compositing across all shots in the film.
  • Collaborate with the CG Supervisor to assess the technical feasibility of designs, suggesting production-friendly solutions to uphold the director's vision while considering the technical constraints of the project.
  • Consult with the Director and CG Supervisor to assign tasks to artists based on their individual skills, strengths, and experience, ensuring optimal workflow and creativity.
  • Review the work of artists regularly, providing feedback and approving shots for submission to the Director.
  • Direct and guide the lighting and compositing teams to achieve the desired look, balancing artistic requirements with productivity and budget constraints, in close collaboration with production management.
  • Oversee the compositing process, ensuring that all visual elements (lighting, effects, and CG assets) are seamlessly integrated and meet the artistic and technical standards of the film.
  • Solve complex technical and creative challenges in lighting and compositing, ensuring high-quality outputs that enhance storytelling and emotion.
  • Manage shot continuity and maintain consistency in look across sequences, ensuring that the film's visual language is preserved.
  • Work with production management to ensure the team stays on schedule and within budget, making adjustments as necessary to meet deadlines.
  • Develop and oversee the Lighting & compositing workflow, resource requirements, methodologies, tools, schedules, and work assignments.
  • Maintain up-to-date documentation for the team and other supervisors.
  • Keep the team informed of project-related updates and developments.
  • Enhance procedures and tools for production optimization.
  • Serve as the primary liaison for interdepartmental communication.
  • Provide constructive feedback to each artist regarding their performance.
  • Actively engage in the process of selecting new artists.

Requirements

Qualités recherchées :

  • Au moins 5 ans d'expérience dans le domaine de la production et connaissance approfondie des différentes plateformes logicielles.
  • Au moins 3 ans d'expérience dans un rôle de leadership, sur un projet entièrement animé ou hybride.
  • Expérience de la production dans Katana, Blender, Renderman et de la composition dans Nuke.
  • Solide compréhension des techniques et principes traditionnels d'éclairage et de composition.
  • Solide expérience technique et capacité à appréhender rapidement de nouveaux programmes et systèmes.
  • Haut degré d'autodirection et forte éthique de travail.
  • Connaissance d'UNIX et des scripts shell.
  • Capacité à planifier et à exécuter des scènes d'éclairage 3D complexes, notamment en travaillant avec des calques et des passes, en effectuant des compositions complexes et en optimisant les scènes et les rendus.
  • Solides compétences en matière de communication (écrite, verbale et interpersonnelle).
  • Solide compréhension artistique de l'éclairage et de la composition. Une liste des tâches effectuées pour chaque prise de vue doit être fournie.

What you’ll bring:

  • 5+ years production experience with strong working knowledge of various software platforms.
  • 3+ experience in a leadership role on a fully animated or hybrid features.
  • Production experience in Katana, Blender, Renderman and compositing in Nuke is a requirement.
  • Strong understanding of traditional lighting and compositing techniques and principles.
  • Solid technical background with ability to grasp new programs and systems quickly.
  • High degree of self-direction and strong work ethic.
  • Knowledge of UNIX and shell scripts.
  • Ability to plan and execute complex 3D lighting scenes including working with layers and passes, doing complex comps and optimizing scenes and renders.
  • Strong communication skills (written, verbal and interpersonal).
  • Demo reel should display a firm artistic understanding of Light and Composition. A shot breakdown listing jobs performed for each shot is required.

title: 2D Character Layout Artist (Anime Series)
description:
OUR STORY


For more than 35 years, Bardel Entertainment has been growing and evolving, yet at our core, we remain grounded in the creative roots of the craft of animation. Our pursuit of fresh ideas, techniques, and technologies is driven by the belief that together, through creativity and collaboration, we can accomplish anything! If you want to be part of an environment that empowers you to experiment, learn, and contribute to exciting projects, come and join us.

Role Overview:

The Character Layout Artist bridges Storyboard and Animation. You will take storyboard panels and animatics and turn them into clear, well-staged scenes by positioning characters, setting poses, and establishing how characters interact with the environment and camera.

You’ll work closely with Animation Supervisor and Directors, BG, and Animation teams to make sure the story, dialogue, and intended performance are clearly communicated before a scene moves into full animation.

Location: Vancouver, BC

Duration: Late September (3 week contract with potential for extension)

What You’ll Do

  • Translate storyboards and animatics into character layouts.
  • Stage and position characters within each scene.
  • Create clear poses that communicate the action, emotion, and intent of the scene.
  • Establish character placement, screen direction, eyelines, and interaction with props and environments.
  • Block key character movements and poses to support dialogue and performance.
  • Work with camera and composition to ensure characters are staged effectively.
  • Maintain character proportions, scale, and continuity between scenes.
  • Identify and resolve staging or continuity issues before animation.
  • Work with Animation Directors, and Supervisors to address notes and make revisions.
  • Follow production schedules, pipelines, and file standards.

Requirements

What You’ll Bring:

  • Experience in character layout in 2D traditional animation production.
  • Strong understanding of character posing, staging, composition, and visual storytelling.
  • Ability to interpret storyboards, animatics, and dialogue.
  • Good understanding of animation principles and how layout supports animation.
  • Strong attention to character proportions, positioning, and continuity.
  • Ability to work efficiently within production deadlines.

Benefits

title: Production & Quality Specialist (Seed)
description:
We are looking for a Finished Goods Production & Quality Specialist to join our Operations / Supply Chain team and help manage the day-to-day execution of our seed packet production program.

This role sits at the intersection of production, quality, inventory, logistics, and replenishment. You will work closely with copackers, suppliers, warehouses, 3PLs, and internal teams to ensure the right products are produced in the right quantities, meet quality and packaging specifications, and are available when and where they are needed.

You will own the operational follow-through of production POs from creation through receipt, maintain visibility to finished-goods inventory across our network, coordinate production and logistics, and identify supply or service risks before they impact customers.

The role also has significant responsibility for e-commerce and Amazon replenishment, including Amazon FBA inventory and the availability of seed packets needed for Amazon bundle production.

Quality is a key part of the role. You will monitor finished packets against established specifications, investigate quality issues, coordinate corrective actions with production partners, and ensure issues are documented and resolved.

We are looking for someone who is highly organized, analytical, detail-oriented, and comfortable taking ownership. You should enjoy working with data, solving operational problems, communicating with external partners, and driving issues through to completion.

This is a hands-on role with the opportunity to make a measurable impact on production performance, quality, inventory accuracy, customer service, and operating cost as we continue to scale our seed business.

Requirements

2–5 years of experience in supply chain, production planning, procurement, logistics, inventory, quality, or a related field.

Experience working with suppliers, manufacturers, copackers, warehouses, or 3PLs.

Experience managing purchase orders, production schedules, inventory, replenishment, or logistics.

Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills with the ability to analyze and work with operational data.

Experience with an ERP system; NetSuite experience is a plus.

Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and follow issues through to completion.

Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with internal teams and external production partners.

Comfortable identifying problems, investigating root causes, and driving corrective actions.

Ability to work in a fast-paced environment where priorities and production requirements can change quickly.

Experience with e-commerce, Amazon, CPG, agriculture, seed, food, or manufacturing is preferred but not required.

How to Apply & To be Considered

Please submit your resume and a brief note on what draws you to this role and how your experience maps to it. In the header of your note, make sure to include "I am the next Seed Specialist at Back to the Roots!"

title: ATUM Team Talent
description:
Why We Exist:

ATUM exists to support courageous founders who turn differentiating tech into world-changing companies that solve critical challenges in Energy, Medtech and Advanced Manufacturing. We bring capital, operational muscle and partners from academia, industry, VC, and government who co-invest in every build.

ATUM build ventures from scratch by helping researchers, corporates and founders turn breakthrough research into venture-scale companies, backing them with capital, corporate networks, and the operational guidance to navigate everything from technical validation and grants to go-to-market and growth.

The Opportunity:

We’re building a pool of exceptional talent across disciplines to support ATUM's activities. Whether your strength lies in technical due diligence, deep-tech commercialisation or operational scaling, we always want to hear from you.

You may be considered for opportunities in:

  • Venture Building: suited to dynamic and entrepreneurial individuals with experience in science and/or engineering. This team bring in experience the venture building process, from technology due diligence to go-to-market commercialisation, focusing on building investible ventures for external founders to scale. Prior experience as a Founder, or as part of an early stage startup team, is highly sought after.
  • Market Expansion: suited to engaging, entrepreneurial individuals with experience running innovation programmes, including evaluating and assessing deep-tech innovations, engaging mentors and entrepreneurs-in-residence, and scoping problem/interest areas with corporates. Familiarity with both corporate R&D and startup ecosystems is extremely valuable.
  • Platform Operations: suited to those with skill sets that can be utilised to unlock ATUM's team, and ATUM's activities, to their full potential. This covers specialists in finance & investments, operations, marketing, talent & HR. Exposure to the world of entrepreneurship, either from inside a startup or as part of a VC or Venture Building team lends itself to quick ramp up in our environment.

Requirements

Values Alignment

Say what you do and do what you say

✅ What We Do:

  • Transparent decision-making – Keep stakeholders informed and explain the “why” behind decisions.
  • Own up to mistakes – If something goes wrong, acknowledge it, fix it, and learn from it.
  • Open communication – Share feedback honestly and constructively, even when it’s difficult.
  • Tough love when needed – We challenge each other to improve, always with the intent of helping the team grow.

❌ What We Don’t Do:

  • Hide information or blame others when things go wrong instead of taking responsibility.
  • Avoid difficult conversations to keep the peace at the cost of progress.
  • Give vague or sugar-coated feedback that doesn’t help others improve.

Figure it out… And make it happen

✅ What We Do:

  • Find solutions, not excuses – When facing a roadblock, look for alternatives and propose solutions.
  • Share ideas and approaches – If you find a better way to do something, spread the knowledge.
  • Celebrate progress – Small wins add up, and recognizing them keeps us motivated.

❌ What We Don’t Do:

  • Wait for someone else to solve the problem instead of taking initiative.
  • Stick to “the way it’s always been done” without questioning if there’s a better way.
  • Ignore small achievements and only focus on final results.

Raise the bar - every time.

✅ What We Do:

  • Always improve – Continuously refine skills, workflows, and approaches.
  • Deliver work that exceeds expectations – Aim for impact, not just completion.
  • Set new standards – Raise the bar for yourself and others.

❌ What We Don’t Do:

  • Settle for “good enough” when we know it can be better.
  • Repeat mistakes without learning from them.
  • Avoid feedback or growth opportunities because they feel uncomfortable.

Benefits

What We Offer:

  • Exposure to cutting-edge research, industry leaders and venture ecosystems
  • The opportunity to shape the direction of new ventures and emerging markets
  • Collaboration with a powerful cross-functional team of scientists, technologists, builders, operators and investors
  • Flexible engagement pathways, from full-time roles on our team, to Entrepreneur-In-Residence positions
  • A high-energy environment where collaboration and collective success sits at the core of all that we do

ATUM is an equal opportunity employer and partner, whether you are exploring joining our team, our Venture Build Programme, or one of our Portfolio Companies. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and identities, and our selection decisions are guided by our core values. If our mission resonates with you, we encourage you to apply.

title: M26196 Research Associate in Corporate Sustainability (Locally Recruited)
description:
CIMMYT is a cutting-edge, non-profit, international organization dedicated to solving tomorrow’s problems today. It is entrusted with fostering improved quantity, quality, and dependability of production systems and basic cereals such as maize, wheat, triticale, sorghum, millets, and associated crops through applied agricultural science, particularly in the Global South, through building strong partnerships. This combination enhances the livelihood trajectories and resilience of millions of resource-poor farmers, while working towards a more productive, inclusive, and resilient agrifood system within planetary boundaries. CIMMYT is a core CGIAR Research Center, a global research partnership for a food-secure future, dedicated to reducing poverty, enhancing food and nutrition security, and improving natural resources. For more information, visit

Cimmyt is looking for a Research Associate who can lead the research and analysis agenda on Corporate Sustainability, Responsible Sourcing, and Regenerative Agriculture, contributing to CIMMYT’s positioning as the leading technical partner for the global agri-food industry. The position serves as a critical bridge between research and implementation and seeks to design, pilot, and scale strategies and tools for regenerative agriculture, decarbonization, and responsible sourcing. The incumbent will be responsible for aligning international reporting frameworks with operational supply models, generating the scientific evidence and scalability mechanisms necessary for CIMMYT to help companies meet their corporate sustainability goals across the various geographic regions of operation.

Key Responsibilities and Activities

Standardization and Harmonization of Sustainability Frameworks

• Analyze international frameworks (GRI, SAI Platform, ISSB/CDSB), national regulatory frameworks, and global corporate priorities to consolidate a system of key performance indicators (KPIs) that integrate metrics on soil health, water efficiency, carbon intensity, productivity, market access, community development, and gender equity.

• Collaborate in the design and implementation of Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) protocols (scalable MRV systems), ensuring the development of replicable methodologies and resources that enable the model to be scaled up to various partners in the agro-industrial sector.

• Design and propose innovative business models and monetization schemes linked to regenerative agriculture (Business Modeling and Monetization of Ecosystem Services for farmers, rural businesses, aggregators, and leading agri-food companies), with the aim of diversifying funding sources and strengthening CIMMYT INC.’s strategy.

• Develop mechanisms to implement strategies that improve engagement within Mexico’s responsible supply ecosystem and that incorporate incentives related to traceability, natural capital assessment, carbon markets, digital traceability, data wallets, and agricultural contracts linked to sustainability performance.

• Propose and develop impact assessment frameworks based on standardized metrics to accurately quantify the social and environmental returns of CIMMYT’s interventions with the private sector (Impact Assessment and Standardized Metrics).

• Systematize lessons learned and produce high-quality technical documents (methodological guides, white papers, scientific articles) that document the impacts of responsible sourcing and regenerative agriculture initiatives, adaptable to various contexts in North America and the Global South.

• Develop high-quality technical briefs and investment proposals for fundraising and identifying joint projects with the private sector in the areas of responsible sourcing and regenerative agriculture.

• Identify and manage collaboration opportunities with key stakeholders in the decarbonization, water neutrality, and biodiversity agendas to expand the institution’s portfolio of strategic projects.

• Provide specialized technical assistance and training programs for supplier companies to mitigate sustainability risks and close operational gaps in the supply chain.

• Lead the preparation of performance reports and technical documents for executive committees and decision-makers in the agri-food sector.

Requirements

Education: Master’s degree in Agricultural Economics, Sustainability, Agribusiness, Environmental Sciences, or related fields. A Ph.D. in business administration is desirable.

• Experience (at least 4 years): Previous experience in strategic consulting, value chain analysis, or sustainability project management with multinational companies.

• Technical Skills: Proficiency in statistical/econometric software (R, Stata), in-depth knowledge of ESG reporting standards, and technical fluency in English and Spanish.

Benefits

CIMMYT offers an attractive remuneration package and support for continuous professional development. In addition to the provisions of the Mexican Labor Law our package of benefits includes year-end bonus (40 days), vacation premium (56%), life and medical insurance, supermarket coupons, savings fund, social Mexican benefits (IMSS, SAR / Infonavit).

Candidates must apply here

Please note only short-listed candidates will be contacted.

Foreign national candidates must have legal documents to work in Mexico.

This position will remain open until filled.

Using tumblers, dryers, and finishing equipment, you'll help ensure every part meets customer expectations while maintaining accurate production records and keeping materials organized. This is a great opportunity for someone who takes pride in quality work, pays attention to details, and enjoys seeing the finished results of their efforts.

Shifts Available

  • Shift 16: 3:00pm - 1:00am, Monday - Friday (+$1.25/hour shift differential)

Starting rate of pay:

  • $19.80 per hour base rate. Candidates with relevant experience may be eligible for base pay up to $20.80 per hour.

Key Responsibilities

  • Operate tumblers and dryers to deburr, finish, and dry parts according to specifications
  • Load and unload parts while adjusting machine settings to achieve consistent results
  • Inspect parts before and after processing to verify quality standards are met
  • Move parts through the finishing process and prepare them for the next operation
  • Utilize computer systems to record production, manage inventory, and track job activity
  • Maintain organization of bins, boxes, and materials for each job

Requirements

  • 6–12 months of relevant manufacturing or production experience preferred
  • Basic math skills for weights, counts, and production tracking
  • Basic understanding of measuring tools such as calipers or micrometers
  • Strong attention to detail

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to stand and move throughout the shift in a production environment
  • Frequent handling of parts, bins, and materials
  • Ability to lift and move materials as needed
  • Repetitive motion involving loading, unloading, and inspecting parts
  • Required PPE: eye protection, hearing protection, MET guard safety shoes

Benefits

  • Annual pay-for-performance increases
  • Paid holidays and paid time off
  • Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance
  • FSA/HSA options
  • Employer-paid life and disability coverage
  • 401(k) with company match
  • 24/7 on-site fitness center
  • Temperature-controlled facility

Clow Stamping Company is committed to providing equal employment opportunities for all employees and applicants. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, marital status, pregnancy, familial status, disability, genetic information, labor organization membership, public assistance status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Applicants and employees are evaluated based on their conduct, experience, and performance, in accordance with Company policies.

title: Software Engineer

“I wanted to create a company that I would have wanted to work at when I was an engineer.” — Mark Griffis, President

Along with our mission-driven team’s deep expertise in a wide range of development languages, we employ a disciplined agile approach to define goals upfront, keep organizational value at the forefront, and set the pace for rapid, iterative innovation that transforms organizations. We call this the Art of the Possible.

  • Embody integrity

  • Stay hungry
  • Remain grounded
  • Create impact
  • Challenge with respect

We’ve built our culture around creativity, continuous learning, and our shared values. If that sounds like something you’d like to be a part of, then join us today!

title: Backend Software Engineer - Web/ML Dev Ops
description:
Company Description

Chooch helps build and run Computer Vision AI applications that make cameras intelligent—enhancing productivity and revenue while reducing operational costs. Chooch has been named a leading computer vision platform by IDC.

Role Description

We’re looking for a Backend Software Engineer (US-based) to join our team in a full-time, remote role. You’ll build and own the backend systems that power our Computer Vision AI platform and analytics products—including APIs, data services, model-serving integrations, and the infrastructure that enables reliable deployments for healthcare, manufacturing, and retail customers.

This role involves frequent collaboration with technical and non-technical stakeholders and close partnership with Solutions Engineering and ML teams. You’ll have significant opportunity to lead technical initiatives, improve platform reliability and scalability, and provide product feedback grounded in real-world deployments.

Key Responsibilities

Backend Systems & API Development

  • Design, build, and maintain scalable backend services that support CV/LLM workflows, analytics, and customer-facing applications.
  • Develop and evolve REST/GraphQL APIs, internal service interfaces, and event-driven integrations.
  • Implement authentication/authorization patterns and ensure secure service-to-service communication.

Data Platforms & Analytics Enablement

  • Build and maintain the data layer (storage, indexing, retrieval) that supports analytics, reporting, and search across CV outputs.
  • Implement streaming and batch pipelines for ingesting camera/edge events and transforming model results into customer-ready insights.
  • Define data contracts, schemas, and quality checks to keep downstream systems sane (because data loves chaos).

Model Integration & Serving Collaboration

  • Partner with ML engineers to productionize model inference: deployment patterns, versioning, monitoring, and rollback strategies.
  • Integrate CV and LLM services into backend workflows with an emphasis on latency, throughput, and observability.
  • Support experimentation while ensuring production systems remain stable and maintainable.

Reliability, Performance, and Observability

  • Own service health via metrics, logs, tracing, alerting, and incident response practices.
  • Optimize system performance across API latency, queue backlogs, database efficiency, and inference throughput.
  • Improve platform robustness through testing strategy, CI/CD, and infrastructure-as-code collaboration.

Cross-Functional Delivery & Customer Impact

  • Work closely with Solutions Engineering to translate customer requirements into scalable backend solutions.
  • Troubleshoot complex issues in production deployments (you won’t be alone, but you will be the calm voice in the room).
  • Contribute to technical roadmaps and platform standards as we scale across customers and industries.

On-Site Travel and Field Testing (Occasional)

  • Some deployments are live with major Fortune 500 customers; occasional travel may be required to validate performance, gather requirements, and ensure systems operate reliably in real-world environments.

Requirements

  • Must-have
    • Strong backend engineering experience building and maintaining production services and APIs.
    • Proficiency in Python (writing clean, testable, maintainable code).
    • Solid understanding of relational databases and SQL (preferably PostgreSQL), including schema design and query optimization.
    • Comfort operating in a Linux environment: command line, debugging, log analysis, and basic networking concepts.
    • Experience with modern software development practices: code reviews, testing, CI/CD, and shipping iteratively.
    • Proficiency with Git and collaborative workflows (feature branches, PRs, conflict resolution).
    • Strong problem-solving skills with a track record of diagnosing and resolving complex issues in production.
    • Clear communication skills and ability to collaborate with cross-functional partners (Solutions, ML, Product, customers).
  • Nice-to-have
    • Experience integrating or supporting ML/CV systems in production (model serving, inference pipelines, monitoring).
    • Working familiarity with computer vision / image processing libraries (e.g., OpenCV) to understand inputs/outputs and troubleshoot issues.

title: Production Analyst (Soil)
description:
About Back to the Roots

Back to the Roots is America's #1 organic gardening company, dedicated to reconnecting families to where their food comes from through fun, simple, and educational gardening products. We're committed to sustainability, innovation, and making organic gardening accessible to everyone — and we're growing fast.

About the Role

The Soil Production Analyst is a critical hire for our Operations team. As we scale our soil network & contract manufacturing sites to support significant retail growth, we need someone who owns the analytical backbone of our soil production.

This person will own the numbers, the schedule, and the plan. You will translate the demand signal into a production schedule, maintain real-time inventory visibility across all soil sites, and flag risks before they become fires. You are the connective tissue between what we're selling, what we're making, and where it needs to be.

You have a passion for analytical rigor, love building systems that scale, and are energized by turning complex data into clear decisions. You work best when you own something fully — and you take pride in getting the details right.

This role is fully remote. If you happen to be based in the SF Bay Area, we get together for a weekly company lunches at our Oakland headquarters — so come hungry. But we're looking for the best person for the job, wherever they are.

What You'll Own

Production Schedule & Demand Alignment

  • Build and maintain the master production schedule across all soil contract manufacturing sites, sequencing production runs to match demand, inventory targets, and retailer windows.
  • Translate the demand signal — from sales forecasts, retailer commitments, and historical data — into a clear production plan that co-man team can execute against.
  • Identify and flag supply risks early: material shortages, capacity constraints, lead time gaps, and seasonal timing conflicts before they impact the business.
  • Work closely with the Soil Procurement & Production team to align production sequencing with procurement timelines and co-man capacity.

Inventory Management & Visibility

  • Maintain real-time inventory accuracy across all soil co-man sites and distribution locations, ensuring consistency between physical stock and NetSuite.
  • Work on end-of-month inventory verification and reconciliation — catching discrepancies before they become accounting or fulfillment problems.
  • Monitor safety stock levels for key inputs and finished goods, alerting the team to shortfalls before they impact production or retailer commitments.
  • Manage and track inventory transfers between manufacturing sites, inventory locations, and fulfillment centers with full documentation.

Purchase Order & Production Tracking

  • Be adjacent to purchase orders for raw materials and packaging across soil co-man sites — end to end from issuance through receipt.
  • Collect and audit daily and weekly production reports from manufacturing partners; update NetSuite to reflect real-time finished goods and raw material levels.
  • Track status of deliveries, costs, and production output; resolve and communicate material shortages with clear escalation to the right stakeholders.

Analysis, Reporting & Continuous Improvement

  • Build and maintain performance dashboards tracking key metrics: fill rate, inventory turn, production accuracy, and COGS inputs — giving the team the visibility to make faster, better decisions.
  • Analyze production and supply data to identify cost savings, process inefficiencies, and network optimization opportunities.
  • Work with the Director of Operations to develop internal tools and processes that make the production planning function sustainable and scalable as we grow to more sites.
  • Support the improving our soil network — modeling network scenarios, freight costs, and inventory positioning across manufacturing and distribution tiers.

Requirements

What We're Looking For

  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Business, Operations, or a related field — or equivalent hands-on experience.
  • 2–4 years of experience in production planning, operations analysis, or supply chain coordination, ideally in a manufacturing, CPG, or co-man environment.
  • High proficiency in Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel — pivot tables, VLOOKUPs, scenario modeling, large data sets. You are faster and more accurate than the average analyst.
  • Experience with NetSuite or another ERP system strongly preferred; you know how to keep systems clean and up to date.
  • Strong analytical instincts — you read between the numbers, anticipate issues before they surface, and translate data into a clear action plan.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and follow-through. You do not let things fall through the cracks.
  • Clear communicator — written and verbal — with internal teams and external manufacturing partners.
  • Comfortable in a fast-paced, lean team environment where you own your work and figure things out.
  • Experience in lawn & garden, soil, agriculture, or a category with multi-site co-manufacturing is a plus.
  • Familiarity with Google Suite (Gmail, Sheets, Docs, Drive).

What Success Looks Like

  • Soil production planning is seamless — because this role owns it.
  • We enter peak season with a clear, sequenced production plan across all sites, and the team is executing against it — not scrambling.
  • Inventory discrepancies are caught before month-end, not discovered after.
  • Supply risks are flagged two to three weeks before they become problems.
  • The team has real-time visibility into production status without needing to chase down updates.

How to Apply & To be Considered

Please submit your resume and a brief note on what draws you to this role and how your experience maps to it. In the header of your note, make sure to include "I am the next Production Analyst at Back to the Roots!"

Benefits

  • Unlimited Vacation and Sick Days
  • Commuter pre-tax mass-transit and parking
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan
  • Personal Cell Phone Reimbursement
  • Company laptop

title: Programme Manager, Europe (AI Climate Governance)
description:
Programme Manager, Europe (AI Climate Governance)

This role is to work on our new AI & Climate Governance programme

  • Reports to: Head of Business & Investor Engagement
  • Preferred timezone: Europe, within CET +/-2.
  • Deadline: Saturday 19 September
  • Contract: Full-time (40 hours)
  • Duration 12 months, with possibility of extension subject to funding

About Climate Catalyst

Climate Catalyst works across Europe, India and Indonesia to accelerate the decarbonisation of heavy emitting industries. A non-profit and strategic convenor, we:

  • Work with diverse stakeholders to identify critical policy gaps where the potential for collaboration is high and align around a shared vision and goals.
  • Build diverse coalitions of existing and new actors across civil society and the private sector to break down silos and build the strategic power of the collective.
  • Co-create strategies tailored to the specific challenge ahead and the national and regional context we’re working.
  • Utilise our expertise in research development, creative communications and policy and business advocacy to deliver shared goals and secure policy and financial shifts towards a net zero future.


We work to secure a just, equitable and prosperous future where global temperature rise is limited to 1.5°C, taking into account the systemic impact heavy emitting sectors have on nature, land use and human health. To date, we’ve sparked collective action towards driving steel decarbonisation in India and Indonesia and building a sustainable aviation sector in Europe. We continue to look for opportunities to scale our impact via new programmes in Europe, India, Indonesia and elsewhere.

About The Role

The Programme Manager will form part of our European programme team, working closely to deliver impactful strategies that target emissions reductions from heavy emitting industries in Europe. This role will focus mainly on the issue of AI and climate governance - where experience is preferable but not required - and take the lead on delivering EU-targeted activities and outputs for this programme. This role is initially set as a 12-month, full-time contract, with potential to extend, and will report to our Head of Business & Investor Engagement.

What you will do

  • Identify policy opportunities and contribute to determining strategic policy positions and recommendations for decision-makers and those who influence them.
  • Build knowledge in the field of climate governance and AI, with a specific focus on policy mechanisms such as the Cloud and AI Development Act, and the EU Tech Sovereignty Package alongside other relevant files relevant to AI and climate.
  • Synthesise AI-relevant policies and research developments and design into public facing briefings for key stakeholders (policy makers, CSOs and the private sector).
  • Work with NGO partner organisations to develop policy positions and execute advocacy activities on climate & AI, and to ensure effective engagement of the private sector across different stages of our programme.
  • Conduct stakeholder mapping, research, and analysis to identify strategies and tactics to effectively engage key stakeholders, particularly business and investors, in support of our policy objectives.
  • Strengthen and build relationships of trust with key businesses and investors, business NGOs, trade associations and other private sector actors.
  • Keep track of climate policy, technology, and economic trends pertaining to the private sector internationally and their role in AI, and specifically in Europe.
  • Engage subject-matter experts, consultants, and researchers as necessary to support our strategies.
  • Produce private sector-orientated outreach and policy advocacy materials, including memos, brief reports, letters of commitments, talking points, and more.
  • Produce and scope terms of reference for targeted research on AI and Climate governance which will shed light on trade offs and influence our target audience.
  • Represent Climate Catalyst at relevant events and forums organised by partners and businesses associations.

Requirements

What You Would Bring

  1. At least five years of experience working on EU policy making processes, including advocacy on emerging issues in the field of technology or AI and climate and the Brussels and/or member state levels.
  2. Demonstrated experience and skills in engaging policymakers and civil society in policy advocacy activities relating to climate change issues. Experience engaging private sector organisations is valued, but not essential.
  3. Experience of working in multi-disciplinary teams to deliver on organisation-wide strategies.
  4. Knowledge and understanding of the key issues pertaining to AI and climate, or other industrial decarbonisation policies, and topics pertinent to Europe.
  5. Strong initiative and an ability to work both autonomously as well as within a team.
  6. Strong interpersonal and communication skills including the ability to distil complex issues for a lay audience.
  7. Ability to establish and maintain strong working relationships with the network of civil society organisations and progressive business and investors.
  8. Awareness of the potentially diverse opinions and voices of Climate Catalyst’s partners and ensure they are taken into account in our policy positions and recommendations.
  9. Ability to adapt and respond positively in circumstances where priorities need to shift quickly, and be open to working on different issues over time.
  10. Humble, with low ego and ready to roll up your sleeves.
  11. Committed to our values of courage, collaboration, diversity and learning.

Benefits

Additional Information

  • This role is fully-remote, with a stipend available for use of co-working spaces. You must have a right to work in the European country you reside in.
  • Our working language is English. Fluency in an additional European language is highly valued but not required.
  • This position requires travel. We anticipate at least two international work trips during the contract period. It will also likely require travel to EU Institutions in Brussels, as well as to events and meetings with European partners.
  • You will be part of the European team, and report into the Head of Business and Investor Engagement.

Compensation + Benefits

  • The starting salary for this role is EUR 64,400. Compensation is adjusted based on the employee’s location and aligned to equivalent local salary bands.
  • Benefits include: health insurance, stipends for wellness and phone/Wi-Fi, professional development, co-working space coverage, generous pension contribution and more. For more information about working with us at Climate Catalyst, visit our website at .

Diversity at Climate Catalyst

Climate Catalyst aims to design inclusive strategies to meet our objectives. We recognise that the only way to deliver on this is to build a diverse team composed of individuals with varying backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We encourage applicants from historically marginalised and currently underrepresented groups in the climate movement to apply.

Equal Employment Opportunities

Climate Catalyst is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable employment opportunity laws prohibiting discrimination. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, national origin, citizenship status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other basis protected by applicable law.

How to Apply

To apply, please upload a cover letter of no more than one page outlining interest in the role and your CV to this application page. We will not consider applications that have been AI-generated and may utilise AI detection tools during this recruitment process.

title: Artiste Compositing / Compositing Artist - Feature Animation
description:
NOTRE HISTOIRE

Depuis plus de 35 ans, Bardel Entertainment est le chef de file de l'industrie de l'animation grâce à son engagement inébranlable en matière de qualité, de créativité et d'innovation. Nous sommes un studio internationalement reconnu, lauréat d'un Emmy Award® - dans deux villes canadiennes de premier plan, Vancouver et Montreal - et la force créatrice derrière des succès d'audience tels que Le Prince Dragon, Rick and Morty, Teen Titans Go ! et Diary of a Wimpy Kid.

OUR STORY

For more than 35 years, Bardel Entertainment has led the animation industry through unwavering commitment to quality, creativity, and innovation. We are an internationally recognized, Emmy Award®-winning studio – in two prominent Canadian cities, Vancouver and Montreal – and the creative force behind top audience hits such as The Dragon Prince, Rick and Morty, Teen Titans Go!, and Diary of a Wimpy Kid.

Requirements

En tant qu'artiste Compositing, vous jouerez un rôle crucial dans la mise en vie de nos univers animés. L'artiste Compositing est responsable de l'intégration des éléments 3D rendus, des effets spéciaux et d'autres éléments pour créer les plans finaux parfaitement réalisés de notre long métrage d'animation. Cela inclut de garantir la cohérence visuelle, de respecter l'intention artistique et de résoudre les défis techniques pour produire des images de haute qualité.

Ce que vous ferez :

    • Combiner plusieurs couches d'animation, d'effets visuels, de passes d'éclairage et d'éléments d'arrière-plan pour créer une image cohérente.
    • Équilibrer les couleurs, la lumière et la profondeur afin d'assurer la cohérence visuelle entre les plans et les séquences.
    • Résoudre les problèmes techniques tels que les incohérences des contours, le flou de mouvement et le nettoyage des artefacts.
    • Collaborer avec les départements tels que l'éclairage, les effets et le rendu pour identifier et résoudre les défis spécifiques à chaque plan.
    • Utiliser des logiciels de compositing pour ajouter de la profondeur, de l'atmosphère et des améliorations comme les effets de lentille, l'étalonnage des couleurs et le flou de mouvement.
    • Apporter des ajustements créatifs pour s'assurer que la vision du réalisateur est réalisée dans chaque plan.
    • Travailler en étroite collaboration avec le Superviseur Compositing et les autres membres de l'équipe pour s'aligner sur la direction artistique et les normes techniques.
    • Fournir des retours aux départements en amont (par exemple, modélisation, éclairage, FX) pour améliorer l'efficacité du flux de travail.
    • Organiser et gérer tous les actifs de compositing, y compris les conventions de nommage des fichiers et leur archivage approprié.
    • Maintenir des normes élevées en matière d'organisation des fichiers et de gestion des versions.

Ce que vous apporterez :

    • Plus de 5 ans d'expérience en tant qu'Artiste Compositing dans l'industrie de l'animation, idéalement sur des longs métrages entièrement animés ou hybrides.
    • Maîtrise des logiciels 3D standards de l'industrie (par ex. : Maya, Houdini).
    • Compétence dans l'utilisation de Katana, y compris le travail avec des modèles dans un pipeline de production.
    • Solide compréhension de la théorie des couleurs, de la composition et des principes de la cinématographie.
    • Connaissance approfondie des langages d’ombrage (par ex. : RenderMan, Arnold).
    • Familiarité avec les logiciels de compositing (par ex. : Nuke).
    • Excellentes compétences en résolution de problèmes et capacité à travailler efficacement sous des délais serrés.
    • Excellentes compétences en communication et en travail d'équipe.
    • Une passion pour la narration et un sens artistique développé.
    • Capacité à guider et à soutenir les artistes compositing juniors et d'autres membres de l'équipe, en favorisant un environnement d'apprentissage collaboratif.

Emplacement: Montréal, Québéc

___________________________________________________________________________________________

As a Compositing Artist, you will play a crucial role in bringing our animated worlds to life. The compositing artist is responsible for integrating 3D rendered assets, special effects, and other elements to create the final polished shots for our animated feature. This includes ensuring visual consistency, maintaining artistic intent, and resolving technical challenges to produce high-quality imagery.

What you’ll be doing:

    • Combine multiple layers of animation, visual effects, lighting passes, and background elements into a cohesive image.
    • Balance color, light, and depth to ensure visual consistency across shots and sequences.
    • Address technical issues such as edge inconsistencies, motion blur, and artifact cleanup.
    • Collaborate with departments like lighting, effects, and rendering to troubleshoot and resolve shot-specific challenges.
    • Use compositing software to add depth, atmosphere, and enhancements such as lens flares, color grading, and motion blur.
    • Apply creative adjustments to ensure the director’s vision is achieved in every shot.
    • Work closely with the Compositing Supervisor, and other team members to align on the creative direction and technical standards.
    • Provide feedback to upstream departments (e.g., modeling, lighting, FX) to improve workflow efficiency.
    • Organize and manage all compositing assets, including file naming conventions and ensuring proper archiving.
    • Maintain high standards for file organization and version control.

What you’ll bring:

    • 5+ years experience as a Compositing Artist in the animation industry, ideally on fully animated or hybrid features.
    • Proficiency in industry-standard 3D software (e.g., Maya, Houdini).
    • Proficiency using Katana including working with templates in a pipeline.
    • Strong understanding of colour theory, composition, and cinematography principles.
    • Strong knowledge of shading languages (e.g., RenderMan, Arnold).
    • Familiarity with compositing software (e.g., Nuke).
    • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work efficiently under tight deadlines.

Location: Montreal, Quebec

Duration: August - November 2026

Benefits

Échelle de salaires : $1,700 - 2,000 CAD par semaine

L'échelle de salaires indiquée reflète nos attentes actuelles pour ces postes à la date de publication de cette annonce. Votre offre de salaire finale prendra en compte plusieurs facteurs clés, y compris votre formation, vos qualifications, certifications, expérience, compétences, localisation géographique, ainsi que les besoins et exigences de l'entreprise.

Un environnement de travail flexible, une assurance santé et bien-être étendue dès le premier jour, et un programme de contrepartie pour les REER ne sont que quelques-uns des avantages offerts. Pour plus de détails, consultez notre site web.

Si cela vous semble correspondre, qu'attendez-vous ? Envoyez-nous votre candidature !

Pay Range: $1,700 - 2,000 CAD per week

This salary range provided reflects our current expectations for these roles as of this posting’s date. Your final salary offer will consider various key factors, including your education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographical location, as well as the needs and requirements of the business.

Flexible work environment, Extended Health and Wellness from day 1, RRSP matching are just some of the benefits. For more details, check out our website.

If this seems like a good fit, what are you waiting for, get your application in!

The QA engineer reviews requirement specifications and design documents, to better understand the features and specifications for the efficient design of test cases to address the full spectrum of the requirements and quality. Key Responsibilities

  • Participate in requirement reviews in order to write test procedures and test cases

  • Setup, integrate and develop highly efficient and reliable test infrastructure
  • Design and develop tools and scripts for product and solution automation test
  • Investigate and evaluate new techniques and tools for continuous improvement
  • Ensure test plans align with the development schedule and project milestones
  • Prepare test reports on test results and problems and provide initial issue analysis
  • Analyze reported issues to generate quality reports, and contribute to defect prevention
  • Support development teams to verify and/or reproduce reported issues
  • Participate in the continuous improvement of test processes and methodologies
  • Setup and configure necessary hardware and operating environments for specialized and daily test cases
  • Maintain of test equipment and the test library environment
  • Participate in development of test tools and test scripts
  • Interact with software developers and other QA engineers to ensure the deliverables fully address the needs

Requirements

Required Skills and Experiences:

  • Minimum two years of experience in testing Android code
  • Minimum two years of experience in mobile or automotive industry
  • Understanding and experience of different automation framework
  • Experience in automation tools like Jenkins, Selenium, Appium and others is a plus
  • Experience with Android automation test tools such as UiAutomator, Monkey&MonkeyRunner or Robotium
  • Development or scripting skills in common language such as JAVA, Python, Perl, C++ or shell
  • Ability to anticipate problems and issues, and then recommend solutions to the problems
  • Experience in mobile application automation is highly preferred
  • Solid knowledge of software quality assurance methodologies and tools

title: Senior Optical Engineer
description:
This role is with Nexascan, a startup supported by ATUM.

Prototype-to-Product Leadership

- Lead the transition of optical systems from lab-stage prototypes to field-ready commercial products. You will solve critical challenges related to miniaturization, ruggedization, and thermal stability in constrained environments.

End-to-End Optical Design

- Use Zemax or Code V to simulate and optimize complex optical paths, ensuring high signal-to-noise ratios for speckle pattern interferometry and defect detection.

Active Sensing Integration

- Pioneer the calculation of optical and acoustic energy propagation to enhance system reliability. You will design customized illumination protocols (active excitation) to maximize defect contrast on difficult surfaces.

- Pioneer the calculation of Acoustic Wave Power to enhance performance and reliability.

- Multi-Physics Synchronization: Experience integrating optical systems with dynamic mechanisms (e.g., PZT phase shifters) and synchronizing high-speed imaging with external triggers from multi-element NDT sensors to boost system speed and sensitivity.

- Opto-Mechanical Collaboration: Collaborate with the FEM, mechanical and firmware team to ensure optical measurements (displacement gradients) are formatted for direct simulation validation.

Technical Strategy

- Document design history files and present technical milestones to stakeholders and investors, helping to shape the company's IP strategy.

Requirements

Education

Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Optical Engineering, Physics, or a related field.

Experience

Minimum of 7 years in optical engineering, with a strong preference for candidates who have taken a product from proof-of-concept to manufacturing.

Technical Proficiency

Expert mastery of optical design software (Zemax, Code V, or equivalent). Experience with laser speckle interferometry, shearography, or coherent imaging systems is required.

Analytical Skills

Strong ability to model physical interactions (light-matter interaction) and solve complex noise/contrast problems in active sensing systems.

Cross-Disciplinary Knowledge

Familiarity with Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) principles. Understanding of how acoustic or mechanical waves propagate through materials (e.g. beam spread, refraction) is a plus, but not required.

title: FBS Personal Lines Hub Leader.
description:
FBS – Farmer Business Services is part of Farmers operations with the purpose of building a global approach to identifying, recruiting, hiring, and retaining top talent. By combining international reach with US expertise, we build diverse and high-performing teams that are equipped to thrive in today’s competitive marketplace.

We believe that the foundation of every successful business lies in having the right people with the right skills. That is where we come in—helping Farmers build a winning team that delivers consistent and sustainable results.

Since we don’t have a local legal entity, we’ve partnered with Capgemini, which acts as the Employer of Record. Capgemini is responsible for managing local payroll and benefits.

What to expect on your journey with us:

Key Responsibilities:

Data Governance & Analytics

Digital Transformation

Requirements

title: Lead Data Platform Engineer
description:
About us

We are a leading consultancy with a purpose to make an enduring impact on health and healthcare. We work with leaders and frontline teams to improve health, transform healthcare, drive adoption of innovation and create value through investment.

Our consultancy serves the entire healthcare sector, from payors and providers of care, to life science companies, health tech and sector suppliers and health investors. We provide end-to-end services, from strategy through implementation, accelerated by data, digital and AI.

We shape opinion through evidence-based thought leadership on key issues affecting health. With unmatched ability to access and use health data, our consultants are a driving force for delivering positive and meaningful change.

About the role

The Lead Platform Engineer is the senior technical lead for CF’s data platform, combining design authority over platform architecture, helping to mentor and direct the data engineering team and managing delivery of platform and data engineering workstreams.

The role sits within CF’s unified data function (Data Innovation and Data Ops), which is led by the Director of Data, Analytics and Intelligence, as the most senior role within the function’s Data Ops team. Within the team this role sits alongside the Lead Data Scientist(s).

Operating with delegated design authority from the Director of Data, Analytics and Intelligence, the Lead Platform Engineer translates the company’s strategic architectural direction into detailed technical designs, implementation patterns and platform standards, enabling the engineering team to execute against them.

They bring deep technical expertise, experience and knowledge to support the Director in delivery and the strategic architecture, technology strategy, vendor relationships, commercial targets and regulatory frameworks within which the Lead Platform Engineer operates.

They help to coach and manage the data engineer(s) within the Data Operations team. They own the day to day management of the platform and lead data engineering and infrastructure workstreams. They own the platform, infrastructure and data engineering capability that underpins it. The Lead Platform Engineer works collaboratively with the Lead Data Scientist(s), who manage the data science consulting track and direct delivery for the client-facing technical consulting team.

The Lead Platform Engineer contributes to CF’s commercial activities in a focused way: providing technical expertise to support partnership opportunities with platform vendors such as Databricks and with data and research organisations and contributing technical input to proposals where platform architecture or infrastructure design is relevant.

Responsibilities

Platform architecture and design

  • Produce detailed technical designs for CF’s cloud infrastructure (OCI, Databricks) and NHS data pipelines, working within the strategic architecture set by the Director
  • Define integration patterns, data flow designs and component specifications that the data engineering team implements
  • Make implementation-level technology decisions (tooling, frameworks, configuration approaches) within the Director’s strategic technology selections
  • Design scalable, secure platform architectures that support CF’s multi-region operations (UK, Middle East, EU) and comply with NHS IG, ISO 27001 and GDPR requirements
  • Own and maintain platform design documentation, reference architectures and decision records
  • Evaluate emerging platform technologies and make recommendations to the Director on adoption, with supporting technical assessment

Delivery management

  • Own day-to-day delivery management of platform and data engineering workstreams in line with the unified function’s strategy and priorities
  • Develop and maintain technical workplans for platform initiatives, coordinating with the Director and Lead Data Scientist(s) on sequencing and dependencies
  • Manage the data engineering team’s capacity across concurrent workstreams, balancing platform development, Data Operations support and client delivery contributions
  • Coordinate QA and testing for platform components, ensuring work meets quality standards before release
  • Identify and escalate delivery risks, resource constraints and scope changes to the Director with sufficient lead time
  • Ensure platform workstreams are delivered to agreed timelines and within resource constraints

Technical standards and quality

  • Define and maintain engineering standards, design patterns and reference implementations for the data platform
  • Conduct architectural review of platform changes before they enter development, ensuring design coherence and technical soundness
  • Contribute to the build quality assurance process for platform components, embedding quality gates in delivery
  • Design the security architecture for platform components in line with the Director’s IG framework and ISO 27001 requirements
  • Identify and communicate technical risks and architectural trade-offs, with clear recommendations

Commercial and partnership contribution

  • Provide technical expertise to support partnership opportunities with platform vendors such as Databricks, contributing design knowledge and technical credibility to commercial discussions led by the Director and Partners
  • Support the Director in technical discussions with data and research organisations where platform architecture or data infrastructure expertise is required
  • Contribute to the technical sections of proposals and client-facing materials where platform architecture, infrastructure design or data engineering capability is relevant
  • Develop an understanding of CF’s growth ambitions and the data platform’s role in enabling them
  • Ensure every contact with external stakeholders (technology partners, data organisations, potential recruits) supports the CF brand and aligns with CF values

Collaboration and technical advisory

  • Work closely with the Lead Data Scientist(s) to ensure the platform and infrastructure serves client-facing data science delivery
  • Advise data scientists, consulting teams and Data Operations colleagues on platform capabilities, constraints and best-practice usage
  • Provide technical input to the Director on infrastructure implications of new data products, client requirements and commercial initiatives

Team apprenticeship, mentorship and capability building

  • Mentor and help to scope and support the work of data engineers within the Data Operations team; this includes objective setting, feeding in on performance and development and providing technical day-to-day support
  • Act as a technical reference point for the engineering team on platform architecture, cloud infrastructure and system design
  • Develop and deliver internal learning content on platform architecture, design patterns and infrastructure best practice
  • Mentor engineers on architectural thinking, helping the team develop design capability over time
  • Support the Director in defining the technical career track and progression requirements for data engineering roles
  • Contribute to CF’s technical learning programme as faculty where platform and infrastructure topics are relevant

Requirements

The requirements of the role include:

  • Around 4 years of experience in data or platform engineering, preferably including senior or lead responsibility for a production data platform
  • Deep expertise in cloud platform design and secure data architecture, including identity and access management, network design and access control; Databricks and OCI, or comparable platforms
  • Strong Python and SQL, and experience building and monitoring production pipelines using PySpark or Spark
  • Experience with infrastructure as code, CI/CD and a Git and GitHub workflow
  • A track record of setting engineering standards and design patterns, conducting architectural review, and producing design documentation that others build from
  • Experience owning delivery of technical workstreams: technical workplanning, capacity management, QA and early escalation of risk
  • Experience mentoring or managing engineers, including objective setting and development
  • Experience designing to regulated data requirements such as NHS IG, ISO 27001 and GDPR, or comparable frameworks
  • A clear communicator who can explain design decisions and trade-offs to technical and non-technical audiences
  • Comfortable acting as the technical authority for platform and infrastructure decisions, and as the reference point the engineering team comes to
  • Confident in commercial and partner-facing technical discussions, including vendor conversations and the technical sections of proposals

Desirable

  • Experience with NHS or other routine healthcare data at patient level
  • Unity Catalog, Delta Lake and medallion structure, bronze to silver to gold
  • Exposure to dbt and dimensional modelling
  • Experience contributing to vendor or partner relationships, such as with Databricks
  • Experience designing for multi-region operations (UK, Middle East, EU)

Flexible working

We follow a hybrid working model that balances in person connections and remote work to drive exceptional client impact. We enjoy working in person together with clients and colleagues and work where clients need us to be.

In supporting flexibility and remote working, team members can work from home one day per week as standard. Additionally, we offer 44 remote working days per year which can be used to top up your working from home days and enable you to work from home up to two days per week-subject to client needs. Alternatively, you could use your allowance in blocks to manage school holidays or other commitments. Our core in person working hours are from 10am until 4pm allowing you that extra flexibility to manage your schedule in a way that works for you.

Our commitment to Diversity & Inclusion

We are committed to building an inclusive and supportive culture where diversity thrives, and all our people can excel. We only recruit, promote and reward our people based on their skills and contribution, without regard to gender, race, disability, religion, nationality, ethnicity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, or other characteristics.

We are Disability Confident Accredited, and we want you to feel comfortable and able to perform at your best in the recruitment process. If you require any reasonable adjustments for any part of the recruitment process, please let us know.

Benefits

  • Holiday entitlement: 25 days/year for staff and 30 days/year for leadership, increasing by 1 day for every year of service up to a maximum of 35 days of holiday per year
  • We contribute 7% of your salary into your pension, while you contribute 3% (or more if you like)
  • Access to a flexible benefits programme giving you the chance to increase pension contributions, gain access to a cash plan or benefit from a ClassPass subscription
  • Annual leave purchase: employees with less than 35 days annual leave entitlement are able to purchase additional annual leave days
  • Income protection: in the event of long-term incapacity and a qualifying claim, 75% of salary will be paid
  • Enhanced sick pay benefit beyond Statutory Sick Pay for up to a total 12 weeks in any 12-month period
  • Life insurance covering four times your basic salary in a tax-free lump sum payable to your beneficiaries in the event of your death whilst in service
  • Enhanced family leave policies: additional pay for parents who have a baby or adopt
  • Access to an interest-free loan of up to £10,000
  • Access to an interest-free season ticket loan, repayable by 12 monthly instalments
  • Workplace nursery scheme: access to a scheme to help working parents save tax and NI on the cost of the nursery care
  • Flexible working policy: including the ability to work from home up to two days per week, with 44 remote working days per year
  • An employee assistance and wellness programme: including access to telephone counselling, life coaching, interactive tools online and digital content downloadable from Lifeworks
  • Seasonal flu jabs: provided by Boots annually
  • Eye care tests: vouchers and discounts at Vision Express
  • Ride to work scheme, saving up to 42% on bikes and cycling accessories at Evans Cycles
  • Membership to the Health Service Journal (HSJ)

title: Professional Development Specialist
description:
Child Start's Professional Development Specialist is passionate about strengthening the quality of early childhood education by empowering educators, child care providers, parents, and caregivers with the knowledge and resources they need to help young children thrive. This position promotes best practices in child development and developmentally appropriate learning experiences that support the healthy, safe, and successful growth of children.

The Specialist researches, designs, and delivers engaging professional development opportunities that equip early childhood professionals with practical skills and current industry knowledge. They also provide consultation and guidance to child care centers, family child care providers, preschools, and families, helping address a variety of child development and early education concerns through collaborative, solution-focused support.

As a trusted resource and advocate for quality early care and education, this role builds strong community partnerships, encourages continuous learning, and helps improve outcomes for children and families. If you are committed to professional growth, enjoy sharing your expertise, and want to make a meaningful difference in the lives of young children, we invite you to join our team.

  • Provide technical assistance and coaching to child care providers, educators, parents and other caregivers as follow up to professional development sessions around child development issues and developmentally appropriate practices that promotes healthy, safe, optimal learning experiences for young children.
  • Offer KDHE approved in-service and pre-service professional development opportunities, for child care providers and teachers.

  • Participate in collaboration meetings to coordinate planning and delivery of professional development opportunities with other identified recipients.

Requirements

  • A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in child development, early childhood education or a closely related field. At least three years of experience working with young children with a minimum of one year in a child care setting. Experience working with adults (e.g. training, coaching, mentioning or leading and providing support to caregivers/teachers.
  • Requires one to three years of related experience. Requires a working knowledge of standard practices and procedures.
  • Maintain a strong working knowledge of the child care licensing regulations.
  • Complete the Cape Trainer approval process.
  • Be knowledgeable about the core competencies, the CDA process and accreditation systems for both center and home-based programs.

  • Proficient using Microsoft Word, Excel, including creating and editing documents, and spreadsheets.

  • Ability to work with a diverse client population.
  • Requires good interpersonal, communication, and teamwork skills.
  • Holds a valid Driver's License.
  • Ability to complete projects in a timely manner and to multi-task.
  • Bilingual candidates preferred.

Benefits

Child Start's Professional Development Specialist is $19.00 per hour, 20 hours per week, 52 weeks per year.

Child Start offers competitive salary and benefits, including Medical/Dental/Vision plans, company-paid Short-Term and Long-Term Disability coverage, 403(b) retirement plan, 9 paid holidays each year, and much more!

Must have legal authorization to work permanently in the United States for any employer without requiring a visa transfer or visa sponsorship.

In compliance with KDHE requirements, Child Start will request proof of measles (MMR) vaccination or documented immunity during the employment process.

Must be able to commute daily to Wichita, KS.

title: Data Analyst
location: Tel Aviv-Yafo, Tel Aviv District, Israel
description:
At Autofleet, we're transforming the way fleets operate by leveraging data, automation, and AI to power smarter mobility. As a Data Analyst, you'll play a key role in shaping product strategy and business decisions by turning complex data into actionable insights. You'll partner with Product, Engineering, and customer-facing teams to build scalable analytics solutions, define success metrics, and uncover opportunities that drive impact across our platform

What you’ll do:

    • Own the product analytics domain for key Autofleet products and strategic initiatives, with a focus on user behavior and product engagement.
    • Design, build, and own our product analytics infrastructure (event tracking, taxonomy, instrumentation) from the ground up, primarily using Mixpanel.
    • Define and maintain a clean, scalable event-tracking taxonomy in partnership with Engineering and Product.
    • Analyze large-scale product and behavioral datasets to identify trends, opportunities, and business insights.
    • Design, build, and maintain dashboards and reporting solutions using Mixpanel and other modern BI tools.
    • Develop automated data pipelines and analytical workflows using Python and Airflow.
    • Partner closely with Product Managers to define KPIs and metrics (activation, retention, funnels, engagement), measure success, and support product decision-making.
    • Work with customer-facing teams to provide insights and occasionally participate in customer discussions and presentations.
    • Build internal tools and processes that improve data accessibility and operational efficiency.
    • Translate complex data findings into clear recommendations for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Requirements

    • 5+ years of experience in Product Analytics, Data Analytics, Analytics Engineering, or a similar analytical role, with a track record of owning product analytics end to end.
    • Hands-on experience building product analytics infrastructure from scratch, including event tracking design and taxonomy — Mixpanel experience required.
    • 4+ years of hands-on Python experience in a professional environment.
    • Strong SQL skills and experience working with large-scale datasets.
    • Experience building and maintaining workflows using Apache Airflow.
    • Experience using AI-assisted coding tools such as Claude Code as part of your day-to-day workflow.
    • Experience with BI and visualization platforms such as Looker, Tableau, Power BI, or similar.

    • Excellent communication skills and ability to present findings to diverse audiences.
    • Professional working proficiency in English, both written and spoken.
