title: Head of IT
description:
About us

We are a leading consultancy with a purpose to make an enduring impact on health and healthcare. We work with leaders and frontline teams to improve health, transform healthcare, drive adoption of innovation and create value through investment.

Our consultancy serves the entire healthcare sector, from payors and providers of care, to life science companies, health tech and sector suppliers and health investors. We provide end-to-end services, from strategy through implementation, accelerated by data, digital and AI.

We shape opinion through evidence-based thought leadership on key issues affecting health. With unmatched ability to access and use health data, our consultants are a driving force for delivering positive and meaningful change.

Our strategic intent

We are focused on building the leading consulting company dedicated to health. We serve the entire healthcare sector, including healthcare systems (providers, payors and regulators), life sciences (pharmaceuticals, biotech, devices and diagnostics), health technology, health investors, and the wider supplier landscape.

We provide end-to-end services, from strategy through implementation, supporting organisations to improve population health and healthcare outcomes. Our work spans strategy and transformation, finance and performance improvement, and delivery accelerated by data, digital and AI. We help clients understand their ambitions, identify opportunities to create value, apply innovation in practice, and deliver sustainable, measurable change.

Our consulting is accelerated by data. With an unmatched ability to access and use health data, we are recognised for our expertise in its safe and responsible application, improving health and healthcare delivery, supporting adoption of innovation, generating evidence, and informing decision-making. Our engineering and data science capabilities underpin our consulting and are also deployed directly with clients, often as part of multidisciplinary teams.

We are building a community of expert consultants who want to operate at the leading edge of the profession and who share a passion for health. Through structured career development from Analyst to Partner, underpinned by apprenticeship, mentorship and formal training, we are cultivating the leaders of the future and supporting individuals to develop distinctive expertise that creates value for our clients.

Role summary

Reporting directly to the Chief Operating and Commercial Officer (COCO), this role holds end-to-end ownership of CF’s internal technology, with the authority to define our tech stack, set security standards, control software and IT spend, and hold suppliers to account. It operates across all of CF’s geographies, currently the UK, Ireland and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA), with further geographies anticipated as the company grows.

This is a role for someone who is both strategic and hands-on. You will set the technology direction and also build the automations, integrations and internal tooling that make CF more efficient. You will manage our outsourced IT support, with the potential to build a small internal capability over time as we bring more work in-house.

It is a rare opportunity to define an organisation’s technology from the ground up, in a firm where data, digital and AI are central to how we serve and innovate with our clients.

Responsibilities

The role’s responsibilities are organised into the following key areas:

Technology strategy and planning

  • Own CF’s internal technology strategy, assessing the technology needs of the business across all geographies to enhance effectiveness and efficiency and create an excellent working environment for our people
  • Build and maintain a clear, complete view of CF’s tech stack: what we use, who owns it, what it costs, where it duplicates, and where it should be rationalised or replaced
  • Vet and approve new tools and software, acting as the internal decision-maker on technology choices and preventing uncontrolled adoption and duplicate spend
  • Keep abreast of developments in workplace technology and assess the adaptations CF should be making
  • Collaborate in the business planning process, setting and managing IT budgets each year, taking account of corporate strategy, business goals, the needs of staff, licences, software, security and audit requirements
  • Define and serve as business owner of our suite of internal productivity tools
  • Set annual goals and quarterly OKRs for internal technology, with clear measures of service quality, security and value for money

Information security, resilience and assurance

  • Own IT security for CF, moving us from a reactive to a proactive position: multi-factor authentication, patching, endpoint protection, access reviews, joiner-mover-leaver controls and identity and password management
  • Own the security roadmap and the risk decisions within it
  • Own backup and disaster recovery arrangements, ensuring they are documented, tested and understood, not assumed
  • Own the company contingency plan and cybersecurity policy, and coordinate CF’s technical response in the event of an incident, providing operational leadership alongside the COCO
  • Review security reports from our IT provider and act on issues with urgency, escalating appropriately
  • Own the ISO audit process for CF, ensuring we continue to meet the requirements of ISO 27001 and other relevant standards, that our accreditations are maintained, and that evidence and documentation are audit-ready
  • Lead security awareness and good practice across CF, so that our people understand their part in keeping client and company information safe
  • Identify and obtain accreditations that would further strengthen CF’s operations and our reputation with clients and employees

Managing outsourced IT support and suppliers

  • Own the relationship with CF’s outsourced IT support provider, setting the scope of service, agreeing service levels and holding them to account on responsiveness and quality
  • Review IT service support requirements, procure and manage contracts for support, ensuring high standards for employees and excellent value for money for the company
  • Act as the internal technical counterpart to our provider, taking on the complex work that sits beyond straightforward user support, and judging what should be outsourced and what should be brought in-house over time
  • Manage relationships with technology suppliers and licence providers, negotiating value for money and maintaining a clear record of contracts, renewals and ownership
  • Manage phone and network provider contracts and costs, adjusting arrangements for specific business needs

Systems, automation and AI enablement

  • Own the administration and configuration of CF’s internal platforms and productivity tools, including Microsoft 365, Teams and SharePoint
  • Own oversight of SharePoint, including its structure, permissions and continuous improvement, so that information is easy to find, properly governed and meets the confidentiality and information governance standards we work to, collaborating with the Operations and People teams on the content held within it
  • Identify and build automations and integrations that remove manual effort across corporate functions, acting as CF’s internal systems engineer
  • Ensure our core business systems work well together and work with the data operations team to ensure that the data flowing between them is reliable
  • Be an expert, discerning user of AI tools and help colleagues use them well, with clear judgement about where AI adds value and where it does not
  • Ensure AI and other tools are deployed securely and in line with our information governance obligations
  • Work in close partnership with the Data Operations team, who own data analytics, data science, engineering and product development, Databricks, and data protection, maintaining clear boundaries and strong collaboration between internal technology and client-facing data capability

End-user technology and equipment

  • Establish effective management of CF’s equipment, ensuring the timely issuance of equipment to new joiners and the return of equipment from leavers, and maintaining an accurate inventory
  • Purchase all IT equipment, working with our Apple Account Manager to secure the most cost-effective plans and to remediate any issues that arise
  • Manage the resale or donation of used equipment to employees leaving the business or to not-for-profit organisations
  • Support effective remote working across internet accessibility, technology and equipment, and maintain the technology elements of CF’s home working offer
  • Keep abreast of the environments our client delivery teams work in and make sure the technology supports them wherever they are based
  • Ensure that our pool of trusted associates have secure and reliable equipment and systems and access

Stakeholder engagement and communication

  • Serve as the point of contact for the Leadership Team on all internal technology matters, translating technical issues into plain language and clear choices
  • Use corporate systems and forums to engage with all staff on how well our technology works, and proactively communicate planned changes and any disruption they may cause
  • Gather and act on feedback, making sure people understand the relationship between what they raise and what changes
  • Collaborate with teams across the business, including the Operations, People, Finance, Data Operations and CEO’s office teams

Requirements

Mandatory

  • Typically at least 8 years experience in senior technology roles
  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft 365 administration, including identity and access management, device management, and SharePoint structure and permissions
  • Demonstrable, hands-on ownership of information security
  • Experience of owning or leading an information security or quality accreditation process, such as ISO 27001, including preparing for and running audits
  • Ability to build automation and integrations, using scripting, workflow or low-code tools and APIs
  • A confident, fluent user of AI tools, with sound judgement about where they add value and where they do not
  • Ability to explain technical issues in plain language and to influence senior, non-technical stakeholders
  • Excellent organisation and prioritisation skills, comfortable working autonomously as the only internal technology specialist and balancing competing demands
  • Strong problem solving skills and the ability to learn new things quickly

Desirable

  • Experience with genuine end-to-end ownership of an organisation’s internal IT
  • Experience of Apple and macOS device management
  • Experience managing outsourced IT providers
  • Experience setting and controlling IT budgets, procuring technology and negotiating contracts
  • Knowledge of Cyber Essentials, ISO 14001 or other standards relevant to a professional services firm
  • Experience of SharePoint information architecture, or of knowledge and information management more broadly
  • Experience operating across international geographies
  • Experience within a professional services or consultancy environment

Flexible working

This role can work from home one day per week as standard. Office hours are flexible within our core hours of 10am–4pm.

Our commitment to Diversity & Inclusion

We are committed to building an inclusive and supportive culture where diversity thrives, and all our people can excel. We only recruit, promote and reward our people based on their skills and contribution, without regard to gender, race, disability, religion, nationality, ethnicity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, or other characteristics.

We are Disability Confident Accredited, and we want you to feel comfortable and able to perform at your best in the recruitment process, if you require any reasonable adjustments for any part of the recruitment process, please let us know.

Benefits

      • We offer a competitive and flexible reward package designed to support you at work and beyond it. You will benefit from a generous holiday allowance that grows with your career (minimum of 25 days), a strong employer pension contribution, and the freedom to tailor benefits to suit your lifestyle, from wellbeing and fitness to financial protection.
      • We are committed to supporting life’s important moments, with enhanced family leave, income and life protection, and access to practical benefits that make everyday life easier, such as interest-free loans and travel support.
      • Your wellbeing matters to us. You will have access to a comprehensive wellbeing and employee assistance programme, preventative health benefits, and initiatives that support an active, balanced way of working.
      • Above all, we invest in our people; offering flexibility, security, and benefits that grow with you, so you can do your best work while building a sustainable and rewarding career.

title: M26243 Senior Internal Auditor (Locally Recruited)
description:
CIMMYT is a cutting-edge, non-profit, international organization dedicated to solving tomorrow’s problems today. It is entrusted with fostering improved quantity, quality, and dependability of production systems and basic cereals such as maize, wheat, triticale, sorghum, millets, and associated crops through applied agricultural science, particularly in the Global South, through building strong partnerships. CiIMMYT is looking for a strong Internal Audit professional who can independently lead end-to-end audit engagements—from planning and fieldwork to reporting and follow-up—ensuring a risk-based approach and full alignment with Global Internal Audit Standards.

This role is quite strategic. You would partner closely with the Head of Internal Audit to continuously refine the organization’s risk-based audit plan, contributing to enterprise-wide risk assessments across areas like operations, finance, compliance, IT, governance, and research programs.

Key Responsibilities:

· Independently lead and deliver end-to-end internal audit engagements (planning, fieldwork, execution, reporting, and followup) in accordance with the Global Internal Audit Standards (GIAS), ensuring high-quality, risk-based audit outcomes.

· Support the Head of Internal Audit in developing, maintaining, and continuously updating CIMMYT’s rolling risk-based internal audit plan, including performing enterprise-wide risk assessments across operational, financial, compliance, IT, governance, and research/program areas.

· Conduct risk assessments and advisory reviews to identify emerging risks, control weaknesses, governance gaps, and opportunities to strengthen organizational effectiveness.

· Prepare clear, concise, and impactful audit reports, including practical, risk-focused, and implementable recommendations tailored for senior management and governance bodies.

· Manage a structured process for tracking, validating, and reporting implementation of agreed management action plans, including assessing adequacy of remediation, escalating delays or ineffective responses where necessary, and formally validating closure.

· Support governance reporting, including preparation of periodic reports, dashboards, and presentations to the Leadership Team (LT), Director General (DG), Audit & Finance Committee, and Board, as required.

· Provide independent advisory support to management on governance, enterprise risk management, internal controls, and process improvement initiatives, while maintaining independence and objectivity.

· Leverage data analytics and technology-enabled audit techniques, where appropriate, to enhance audit effectiveness, risk identification, and insight generation.

· Ensure audit work is properly documented and fully compliant with GIAS, internal methodologies, and quality assurance requirements, maintaining complete and defensible audit files.

· Build strong, professional relationships with geographically dispersed stakeholders, constructively challenging management where appropriate while maintaining independence, objectivity, and sound professional judgment.

· Provide guidance, coaching, and quality support to junior internal audit staff, peers, interns, or secondees, as applicable, contributing to capability development, knowledge sharing, and consistent delivery of high-quality audit work across the function.

· Coordinate and oversee co-sourced or outsourced internal audit engagements, as applicable, including supporting scope definition, reviewing deliverables, ensuring alignment with GIAS and CIMMYT expectations, and maintaining overall quality and continuity of assurance outcomes.

Requirements

· 7–10 years of progressive internal audit experience, with demonstrated ability to independently manage full audit cycles in complex, international, or matrixed organizations.

· Demonstrated ability to operate with a high degree of autonomy in a lean or resource-constrained environment, effectively managing competing priorities and independently driving audit engagements with limited supervision.

· Strong knowledge of the Global Internal Audit Standards (GIAS) and risk-based auditing methodologies, with sound understanding of governance, enterprise risk management, and internal control frameworks.

· Proven experience in developing risk-based audit plans and conducting comprehensive risk assessments across operational, financial, compliance, IT, governance, and project/program environments.

· Excellent analytical, critical thinking, and report-writing skills, with the ability to communicate complex issues clearly, concisely, and persuasively to senior stakeholders.

· Ability to exercise sound professional judgment and translate complex or ambiguous issues into practical, risk-based, and implementable recommendations.

· Demonstrated confidence and professional credibility in engaging senior and geographically dispersed stakeholders, constructively challenging management where required while maintaining strong working relationships and independence.

· Comfortable operating in a dynamic and evolving environment, with the ability to navigate ambiguity, shifting priorities, and emerging risks pragmatically.

· Strong interpersonal and relationship management skills, with the ability to build trust, engage constructively with diverse stakeholders, and influence positive change while maintaining independence and objectivity.

· Professional proficiency in English is required

· Professional certification (CIA, CPA, ACCA, or equivalent) strongly preferred, with a high level of professional integrity and sound judgment.

· Practical experience using audit tool and data analytics to enhance audit effectiveness (e.g.,Power BI, ACL/IDEA, Excel analytics, SQL, data visualization tools, or similar) would be an advantage.

· Familiarity with grant-funded environments, restricted funding, project governance, research institutions, nonprofit/international development settings, and international operations would be an advantage.

Benefits

CIMMYT offers an attractive remuneration package and support for continuous professional development. In addition to the provisions of the Mexican Labor Law our package of benefits includes year-end bonus (40 days), vacation premium (56%), life and medical insurance, supermarket coupons, savings fund, social Mexican benefits (IMSS, SAR / Infonavit).

Please note only short-listed candidates will be contacted.

Foreign national candidates must have legal documents to work in Mexico.

This position will remain open until filled.

CIMMYT is an equal opportunity employer. It fosters a multicultural work environment that values gender equality, teamwork, and respect for diversity.

title: DevOps Engineer (Transcribe)
description:
Assurity Trusted Solutions (ATS) is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Government Technology Agency (GovTech). As a Trusted Partner over the last decade, ATS offers a comprehensive suite of products and services ranging from infrastructure and operational services, authentication services, governance and assurance services as well as managed processes. In a dynamic digital and cyber landscape, where trust & collaboration are key, ATS continues to drive mutually beneficial business outcomes through collaboration with GovTech, government agencies and commercial partners to mitigate cyber risks and bolster security postures.

Who we are
Transcribe is a speech-to-text-to-insights platform. We have (1) Transcribe Workspace, a web application that serves over 5000 monthly active users, assisting them to transform their conversations into insights, and (2) Transcribe API, a solution that embeds speech-to-text and text analytics solutions into agency systems.

What the role is
You will work on both small and large scale projects, building and maintaining the infrastructure behind them. We are fully aligned with the Government’s cloud-first policy and you will bring capability to help us realize this. The role includes:

  • Managing the development, deployment, orchestration and maintenance of data pipelines for our Data Science products
  • Providing DevOps architecture implementation and operational support
  • Implementing and integration cybersecurity tools and processes
  • Developing and managing processes, automation, best practices, documentation

What it is like working here
We build products that serve a variety of agency users, who use them to solve highly meaningful problems pertinent to our society, from transportation, to education, to healthcare. The public sector is full of opportunities where even the simplest software can have a big impact on people’s lives. We are here to improve how we live as a society through what we can offer as a government.

  • Rapid Prototyping - Instead of spending too much time debating ideas we prefer testing them. This identifies potential problems quickly, and more importantly, conveys what is possible to others easily.
  • Reliable Productization - To scale an idea, a prototype or a Minimum Viable Product to a software product, we scrutinize and commit to its usability, reliability, scalability and maintainability.
  • Ownership - In addition to technical responsibilities, this means having ideas on how things should be done and taking responsibility for seeing them through. Building something that you believe in is the best way to build something good.
  • Continuous Learning - Working on new ideas often means not fully understanding what you are working on. Taking time to learn new architectures, frameworks, technologies, and even languages is not just encouraged but essential.

As we often deal with big data and computing requirements, you are also able to take a long-term strategic view of the platforms you work on, and help provide this perspective to the team. To do so, you will:

  • Effectively prioritize and execute tasks in a high-pressure environment
  • Develop and maintain internal engineering productivity tools and environments
  • Perform independent research into product and environment issues as required
  • Monitoring automation to effectively detect/predict/prevent issues in the environment and code base
  • Future-proofing the technical environments and ensuring extreme high levels of automation, availability, scalability and resilience
  • Have knowledge in and/or continuously learn lots of different open source technologies and configurations

Requirements

The customers for our products are normally agency users, which means that breadth of knowledge in government IT infrastructure and experience in government networks will help. Since our direction is cloud-first, you will likely have some experience in patch/update scheduling, and knowledge of security incident response procedures. A disciplined approach and strong problem-solving instincts are fundamental to succeed. Your aptitude for completing the tasks and attitude to continuous learning are more valued than any formal certification.

To succeed, you will need to possess some of the following:

  • Excellent problem solving and methodical troubleshooting skills
  • Strong programming skills e.g. Bash, Python, Go, Javascript
  • Experience in web frameworks and microservice architecture
  • Strong understanding of networking concepts
  • Experience with infrastructure tools e.g. Docker, Kubernetes, Prometheus, Alertmanager, Grafana, Cloud computing (AWS)
  • On-prem deployment, networking and infrastructure experience would be advantageous
  • Experience with use, setup and administration of services e.g. Elasticsearch, Openshift, MongoDB, Postgres, Nginx
  • Terraform experience would be a plus
  • Breadth of knowledge - OS, networking, automation (CICD), cybersecurity concepts, public key infrastructure, cloud computing, web and API development, distributed systems, Linux

Join us and discover a meaningful and exciting career with Assurity Trusted Solutions!

The remuneration package will commensurate with your qualifications and experience. Interested applicants, please click "Apply Now".

We thank you for your interest and please note that only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

By submitting your application, you agree that your personal data may be collected, used and disclosed by Assurity Trusted Solutions Pte. Ltd. (ATS), GovTech and their service providers and agents in accordance with ATS’s privacy statement which can be found at: or such other successor site.

Benefits

Our employee benefits are based on a total rewards approach, offering a holistic and market-competitive suite of perks. These include leave benefits to meet your work-life needs and employee wellness programmes.

We champion flexible work arrangements (subject to your job role) and trust that you will manage your own time to deliver your best, wherever you are, and whatever works best for you.

title: Employee Engagement Specialist
description:
Job Purpose

Contributes to fostering a motivating work environment and culture across the Bank and its overseas branches, encouraging employee engagement, creativity, and initiative. This is achieved through participation in the development of employee programs and social engagement activities, as well as collaboration with relevant stakeholders to enhance the employee experience in accessing and utilizing services provided by various Human Resources functions. These efforts aim to strengthen employee commitment, satisfaction, and sense of belonging across the Bank and its overseas branches.

Key Responsibilities

  • Implements the work plans of the Employee Engagement and Belonging Unit in alignment with the overall Human Resources strategy. Continuously reviews and updates these plans in response to changing circumstances, requirements, and developments, as well as the recommendations of the direct supervisor.
  • Participates in developing multiple communication channels to ensure transparent sharing of information, news, and events with Bank employees. This includes, but is not limited to, the Bank’s strategy, objectives, achievements, survey results, and other relevant information, in coordination with the direct supervisor.
  • Conducts employee meetings and organizes meetings, conferences, and other engagement sessions on a regular basis, in coordination with the direct supervisor, to facilitate direct and transparent communication with employees, provide them with the necessary information, and obtain their feedback through open dialogue, Q&A sessions, closed-group meetings, brainstorming sessions, and other appropriate engagement techniques.
  • Prepares and issues periodic employee newsletters in coordination with the direct supervisor.
  • Measures, analyzes, and prepares periodic reports related to employee engagement and belonging by utilizing appropriate data collection and analysis methods and tools, including statistical surveys, employee satisfaction surveys, eNPS, and other modern measurement techniques. Ensures that the results are linked to overall organizational performance in coordination with the direct supervisor and develops and updates the relevant reporting dashboards accordingly.
  • Participates regularly in reviewing established Human Resources policies, procedures, and systems, and collaborates with relevant stakeholders across HR functions to enhance them in a manner that improves the employee experience and sense of belonging and increases employee satisfaction with HR services.
  • Proposes and develops programs aimed at enhancing employee engagement and sense of belonging, in coordination with the direct supervisor.
  • Implements work plans designed to foster a positive, engaging, and motivating work culture and environment that supports increased productivity. This includes developing, updating, and promoting positive organizational programs, values, and desired behavioral practices across the organization, documenting recommendations and submitting them to the direct supervisor.
  • Participates in developing an organization-wide Employee Value Proposition (EVP) that reflects the Bank’s culture and the benefits and value offered to employees.
  • Organizes campaigns, events, and interactive engagement activities, in coordination with the direct supervisor, aimed at encouraging and reinforcing positive employee values and behaviors and creating a healthy work environment that supports the achievement of organizational objectives and enhances productivity.
  • Conducts exit interviews, analyzes the underlying reasons and findings, develops relevant recommendations, and submits them to the direct supervisor in a manner that supports the Bank in identifying and addressing workplace-related issues and improving employee retention rates.
  • Follows up on the implementation of onboarding programs for new employees and ensures their effective integration and adaptation into the work environment, thereby enabling them to meet their assigned objectives and perform their responsibilities with the required level of effectiveness and efficiency.
  • Serves as a primary or alternate member of the duly established Business Continuity Plan and Emergency Response Teams and performs all duties assigned under the plan to minimize the impact of crises and ensure the restoration of operations as quickly as possible.

Requirements

Skills and Competencies

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Management Sciences, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 5 years of relevant professional experience.
  • Proficiency in the English language, both written and spoken.
  • Thorough knowledge of Human Resources systems, policies, and procedures.
  • Good knowledge of internal and external regulations, procedures, and their updates governing the work.
  • Proficiency in computer applications and the ability to work effectively with various systems and applications.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Strong negotiation and persuasion skills.
  • Strong analytical skills.
  • Ability to work effectively as part of a team.
  • Strong planning and organizational skills.

Kaya by Chemin Sdn Bhd is a community of high-performing data annotators helping build the next generation of AI. Join us to work on impactful AI projects, develop your skills, and become part of a growing global community.

About the Role

We're looking for Audio Transcription Reviewers to join our AI language project and help ensure the quality of Cantonese-English transcriptions.

In this role, you'll be part of our Quality Control (QC) team, reviewing completed audio transcriptions to ensure they are accurate, complete, and follow project guidelines before they are delivered to the client.

This project features authentic Hong Kong Cantonese-English conversations, so we're primarily looking for candidates who are fluent in Cantonese and familiar with the Hong Kong accent. While some recordings include healthcare-related conversations and English medical terminology, a healthcare background or familiarity with medical terminology is an advantage, but not required.

If you're detail-oriented, enjoy reviewing language data, and want to contribute to building better AI language technologies, we'd love to hear from you.

Requirements

Project Details

  • Project Duration: Approximately 2 months
  • Project Period: July – September 2026
  • Working Hours: Flexible
  • Estimated Workload: Approximately 2 hours per batch
  • Onboarding Training: Mandatory (during office hours, GMT+8)

What You'll Be Doing

  • Review completed Cantonese-English audio transcriptions for accuracy and completeness
  • Verify audio segmentation and speaker labels
  • Identify and correct transcription, segmentation, and formatting errors
  • Ensure healthcare terminology is transcribed accurately where applicable
  • Follow project guidelines to maintain consistent quality standards
  • Escalate unclear or complex cases when necessary
  • Communicate with the Project Manager for clarification
  • Complete assigned batches within the project timeline

Compensation

  • Quality Control (QC): Earn up to USD 8 for approximately 2 hours of work
    • Execution Details:
    • Audio Length: 1–9 seconds
    • Average Handling time: 1-3 minutes/task

Language Skills

  • Fluent in spoken Cantonese and able to read and write Traditional Chinese
  • Familiar with the Hong Kong Cantonese accent
  • Comfortable reviewing Cantonese-English conversations containing code-switching and occasional English medical terminology
  • Fluent in English for project communication and understanding project guidelines

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience reviewing transcriptions, subtitles, or language-related content
  • Healthcare background or familiarity with medical terminology is an advantage
  • Previous experience in transcription, quality control, data annotation, localization, or AI language projects is a plus

Other Requirements

  • Strong attention to detail with the ability to identify transcription and segmentation errors
  • Familiar with using a Cantonese Jyutping keyboard

  • Access to a laptop or desktop computer, headset, and a stable internet connection

title: Software Engineer with Clearance
description:
What is Aviture?

Aviture is a full-service technology consulting firm with expertise in software solutions for both commercial and government organizations.

We believe software doesn’t mean anything unless it solves a problem, so we create technology to enable users, open possibilities, and create meaningful impact.

“I wanted to create a company that I would have wanted to work at when I was an engineer.” — Mark Griffis, President

We are headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska, with remote employees across the nation: Las Vegas, Washington D.C., Austin, Dallas, Portland, Green Bay, Kansas City, Madison, Minneapolis, and Orlando, just to name a few.

What is Aviture’s Art of the Possible?

Along with our mission-driven team’s deep expertise in a wide range of development languages, we employ a disciplined agile approach to define goals upfront, keep organizational value at the forefront, and set the pace for rapid, iterative innovation that transforms organizations. We call this the Art of the Possible.

The solutions we’ve created have:

  • Saved lives in the California wildfires and southern U.S. flooding
  • Provided security for the 2020 Presidential Inauguration, Super Bowl, and post-attack Boston Marathon
  • Enabled augmented-reality training environments for surgeons
  • Increased transparency and promoted patient wellness in hospitals and senior care facilities
  • Combined computer vision and robotics to automate dangerous manual labor tasks
  • And much more!

Why You’ll Want to Live Aviturian

Aviturians create technology that makes a meaningful difference in someone’s life. We’re a team made up of designers, engineers, developers, and inventors who believe technology’s purpose is to empower users to change the world. Here are the values that guide us:

  • Embody integrity
  • Seek ownership
  • Stay hungry
  • Remain grounded
  • Create impact
  • Challenge with respect

We’ve built our culture around creativity, continuous learning, and our shared values. If that sounds like something you’d like to be a part of, then join us today!

Software Engineer

Aviture is hiring a Software Engineer. Aviturians understand how technology can change the world and have the technical skills to make those visions a reality. Aviturians are always eager to learn, share, collaborate, grow, and innovate. (We also share a good meme or thirty.)

We’re looking for a rockstar Software Engineer who will…

  • Work with a cross-functional team to design, develop, test and deploy innovative solutions to a wide range of complex business problems.
  • Actively participate in all aspects of our agile development process.
  • Utilize effective debugging techniques to identify and resolve software defects.
  • Continuously keep themselves up to date on changes in technology, with an emphasis on the tech stacks being used by your team.

Sound like you? Apply today:

Requirements

  • BS degree in Software Engineering related degree, similar technical field of study or equivalent practical experience.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Able to respectfully challenge the status quo.
  • Experience developing and maintaining large-scale applications using one or more general purpose programming languages, such as:
    • Python, Java, C#/.NET, Go, JavaScript, TypeScript
  • Experience with one or more modern frontend technologies is a plus: ReactJS, AngularJS, VueJS, etc.
  • Able to work both autonomously, as well as collaboratively among a team of your peers.
  • Excellent grasp of computer science concepts, proven ability to solve complex technical problems.
  • Experience using common design patterns in the software industry.
  • High personal standards for code quality, maintainability, and performance.
  • This position will require the employee to have a Secret level Government clearance or the ability to obtain one.
  • This position will require the employee to work in person at an off-site location.

Benefits

  • PPO or a High Deductible Health Plan, HSA eligible plan, Dental, Vision, and Supplemental Life.
  • Generous paid time off that starts accruing on day one.
  • Hybrid work environment with quarterly Castaway Week events in the Omaha HQ Office, all expenses paid, from across the country to participate in team-building, collaboration, and fun events.
  • Company vacations!!! Previous destinations have included Napa Valley, Cancun, Cabo San Lucas and Aspen.
  • Matching 401k with 100% vesting in six months.
  • Pick your preferred workstation! Mac? PC? We’ll support you with the tech you need to do your best work.
  • Get paid to go to national and international conferences and training, so that you can stay up to date with the latest innovations.
  • Flexible work schedules: Work the times that fits your schedule, with all meetings required to be scheduled between 9 am and 3 pm CST.
  • Free lunch every Friday and recurring team events for you and your family to enjoy.
  • Incentive and bonus pay.
  • Opportunities for connection and growth through peer coaching, recurring Lightning Talks to share things we’re passionate about, and a bi-weekly company-wide All Hands.

title: Governance and Compliance Administrator (Part-time)
description:

At CIMSPA, we're on a mission to support, develop and enable the professionals and organisations that power the UK's sport and physical activity sector. As the professional development body for the sector, we're creating a workforce that inspires more people to become active and live healthier lives.

We're looking for an organised, detail-focused and personable Governance & Compliance Administrator to join our Governance and Compliance team. This is an exciting opportunity for someone who enjoys bringing order to complex processes, managing sensitive information with professionalism and supporting high standards of governance and accountability.

What you'll be doing

In this varied and rewarding role, you'll be at the heart of our governance and compliance activity, supporting complaints management, governance processes and safeguarding responsibilities across the organisation.

You'll:

  • Act as the first point of contact for complaints and concerns received by CIMSPA.
  • Coordinate and administer complaints, disciplinary hearings and appeals.
  • Support board, committee and panel meetings, including agendas, papers, minutes and action tracking.
  • Maintain accurate governance records, reports and documentation.
  • Help monitor governance activities and support assurance reporting.
  • Provide professional support and guidance to colleagues, members and stakeholders.
  • Act as CIMSPA's Deputy Safeguarding Lead, supporting safeguarding administration and processes.

This role offers excellent variety and the opportunity to work with senior leaders, board members, committees and external stakeholders while contributing to the smooth and effective operation of a national professional body.

What we're looking for

You'll be someone who thrives on organisation, accuracy and collaboration. You'll be confident managing multiple priorities and handling sensitive matters with discretion and professionalism.

We're particularly interested in candidates who have:

  • Experience in administration within governance, complaints, regulatory, committee or professional environments.
  • Excellent organisational and record-management skills.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder relationship skills.
  • Experience coordinating meetings and preparing documentation.
  • The ability to manage confidential information with integrity.
  • A keen eye for detail and a commitment to high-quality work.

Experience supporting boards, committees, complaints investigations, appeals processes or safeguarding activities would be advantageous.

Why join CIMSPA?

We believe people do their best work when they feel supported, trusted and valued. That's why we've built a culture where everyone has a voice and the opportunity to grow.

At CIMSPA, you'll join a passionate, inclusive and ambitious team dedicated to supporting the people who make sport and physical activity happen across the UK. If you're looking for a role where your organisational skills, professionalism and commitment to excellence can make a genuine impact, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Classroom Aide
description:
Support providing a warm, safe, constructive and non-threatening environment with age-appropriate activities for Head Start 0-5 children. Assist the teacher with necessary classroom record-keeping tasks. Assist with food service as assigned.

Supports staff during staff breaks and in the absence of the classroom teacher.

  • Observes children upon arrival; reports any unusual circumstances (bruises, inappropriate dress, signs of illness, etc.) and document in writing to EC Manager.
  • Helps prepare classroom materials for scheduled activities.
  • Support screenings that are completed in first 45 days and as scheduled in developmental, speech and behavior.
  • Support infants feeding on demand with food/bottles. Holds infants while feeding.
  • Take lead to set up for meals, snacks. Supervise lunches, snacks and breakfasts. Assist with clean up following meals. Eat with children in a family-style setting if age appropriate.
  • Assist with children’s attendance & completes CACFP paperwork.
  • Inventories food and requests supplies as needed.
  • Complete Summer food services for children.
  • Assists with fluoride administration and record which children have received fluoride.
  • Follows CACFP, KDHE licensing standard and Head Start Performance Standards at all times.
  • Support and encourage families to be actively involved in the program and assist them in finding ways to volunteer.
  • Supports coordination of progress of each child to share with parents and assist with developing an individual plan together for their child.
  • Supports home visits and/or school conferences.

Requirements

Requires:

  • High School Diploma or equivalent, willing to begin an education plan to obtain a CDA credential or an Associate's degree in Early Childhood Education.
  • A love for teaching and the ability to build a trusting relationship with students, teachers and parents.
  • The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 30 pounds for various classroom and event needs.

Prefer:

  • Child Development Associate (CDA) or Associate's degree in Early Childhood Education or related field.




Benefits

Child Start's Classroom Aide position is $13.88 per hour.

Child Start offers competitive salary and benefits, including Medical/Dental/Vision plans, company-paid Short-Term and Long-Term Disability coverage, 403(b) retirement plan, 9 paid holidays each year, and much more!

Must have legal authorization to work permanently in the United States for any employer without requiring a visa transfer or visa sponsorship.

In compliance with KDHE requirements, Child Start will request proof of measles (MMR) vaccination or documented immunity during the employment process.

This is not a remote position, must be able to commute daily to Wichita, KS.

title: M26332 Program Manager - Genetics Resources Program (Locally Recruited)
description:

This combination enhances the livelihood trajectories and resilience of millions of resource-poor farmers, while working towards a more productive, inclusive, and resilient agrifood system within planetary boundaries. CIMMYT is a core CGIAR Research Center, a global research partnership for a food-secure future, dedicated to reducing poverty, enhancing food and nutrition security, and improving natural resources. For more information, visit

o Resources Management (Human, Financial)

o Coordinate with the assigned DFS point(s) of contact for Grant Management and Resource Mobilization

- Critical and Creative Thinking

- Teamwork

- Client Orientation

- Problem Solving and Decision-Making

- Negotiation and Conflict Resolution

- Proactivity

- Team Leadership

- Risk management

- Certificated project manager and 10+ years demonstrated experience with project or program management.

title: System Engineer (Nutanix and Red Hat)
description:
Assurity Trusted Solutions is a wholly-owned subsidiary of GovTech, providing infrastructure, operational, governance, assurance, and cybersecurity services that support government and commercial organizations. Working at the intersection of technology, reliability, and security, the team helps build and operate platforms that enable critical services to run effectively and securely.

As a System Engineer dedicated to Day 2 Operations, you will focus on maintaining, optimizing, and ensuring the absolute stability of our enterprise hybrid infrastructure. This role is well suited to someone who excels at the "post-deployment" lifecycle—keeping business-critical Nutanix hyperconverged infrastructure (HCI) systems and Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) platforms secure, performant, resilient, and continuously automated.

Responsibilities

  • Day 2 Operations & Lifecycle Management: Own the monitoring, proactive health-checking, performance tuning, and capacity management of enterprise Nutanix HCI clusters (AOS/AHV) and RHEL environments.
  • Patching & Compliance: Manage routine and emergency patching, kernel upgrades, and firmware updates across Nutanix blocks and RHEL estates while adhering strictly to government security baselines and minimizing system downtime.
  • Infrastructure Automation: Write and maintain Ansible playbooks and Bash scripts to automate repetitive system administration tasks, configurations, and configuration drift management.
  • Incident & Problem Management: Serve as the technical escalation point for complex infrastructure incidents, conducting deep-dive root cause analysis (RCA) and implementing permanent fixes.
  • Backup & Disaster Recovery: Regularly manage, validate, and test disaster recovery (DR) procedures and backup replication policies across our production nodes.
  • Collaboration: Work closely with application developers, security operators, and infrastructure architects to ensure platform changes cleanly align with Day 2 operational stability.

Requirements

  • 3-5 years of hands-on experience in enterprise systems engineering, with a heavy emphasis on production infrastructure operations (Day 2 support).
  • Strong competency managing Nutanix environments, including Nutanix AHV/ESXi, Prism Central, and lifecycle management (LCM).
  • Deep expertise in Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) administration, covering storage management (LVM), performance tuning, security hardening, and OS troubleshooting.
  • Hands-on experience with Ansible for system automation, configuration management, and patching workflows.
  • Solid understanding of core enterprise infrastructure concepts: networking (VLANs, routing), storage protocols, and security principles.
  • Familiarity with enterprise monitoring pipelines (e.g., Nutanix Pulse, Prometheus/Grafana, or Syslog).
  • Nutanix Certified Professional (NCP) or Red Hat Certified System Administrator / Engineer (RHCSA / RHCE).
  • Experience operating infrastructure within a highly regulated environment or Singapore public sector context.
  • Basic exposure to container platforms like Red Hat OpenShift or vanilla Kubernetes.
  • Willingness to participate in a scheduled on-call rotation for high-severity production incident resolution.

Benefits

  • We promote a learning culture and encourage you to grow and learn with training budgets and certification sponsorships.
  • Annual Leave Benefits with additional perks such as Family Care and Birthday Leave.
  • Contract Staff enjoys the same comprehensive benefits as Permanent Employees.

High Leverage

Design a daily-use product placed directly in the hands of the world’s most ambitious individuals and organizations - empowering them to compound their time, relationships, and global impact.

Cutting-Edge AI

Work hands-on with a next-generation AI system redefining lifestyle management at the highest level, spanning context, recommendation, orchestration, and execution. Opportunity

Play a foundational role in building the future of high-performance lifestyle management - a $100bn opportunity at the intersection of technology, luxury, and longevity.

  • International terms knowledge.
  • Contract management experience.

In addition to the provisions of the Mexican Labor Law our package of benefits includes year-end bonus (40 days), vacation premium (56%), life and medical insurance, supermarket coupons, savings fund, social Mexican benefits (IMSS, SAR / Infonavit).

title: Head of DNA Data Governance
description:
The Head of Data Governance is responsible for defining and leading the organization’s enterprise-wide Data Governance framework, ensuring that data is managed as a strategic asset. This role drives the vision, strategy, and execution of data governance initiatives, including data quality, ownership, stewardship, metadata management, and compliance.

Main Accountabilities

  • Defines, owns, and implements the Enterprise Data Governance Strategy, ensuring alignment with the organization’s overall data and digital strategy.
  • Establishes and oversees data governance policies, standards, and operating models, including frameworks for data quality, metadata, and master data management.
  • Ensures the effective design and governance of data architecture and data zones within the organization’s data platforms, driving standardization and reusability.

  • Acts as the Product Owner for data-related transformation inititiaves that involve ingesting new sources of data or improving the quality of existing data.

Requirements

Education, Experience and Technical Skills

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Management, or related field
  • Master’s degree in Data Management, or other related field.
  • Minimum 8–10 years of experience in data governance, data management, or data architecture roles, including at least 3 years in a leadership or management capacity.
  • Proven track record in developing and implementing enterprise data governance frameworks and strategies.
  • Strong understanding of data modeling practices, metadata management, master data management (MDM), and data quality frameworks.
  • Experience with data governance and modeling tools (e.g., Informatica Axon, Collibra, Erwin, Alation, etc.).
  • Familiarity with regulatory and compliance requirements related to data (e.g., GDPR, BCBS 239, DORA).
  • Strong business acumen in financial services, risk management, and data-driven decision-making.
  • Technical fluency with relational databases, SQL, and data integration concepts; knowledge of Python, Spark, or data pipeline orchestration is a plus.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, able to articulate data governance concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Collaborative mindset with a focus on building a data-driven culture.

Competencies

  • High attention to detail and accuracy, with results orientation
  • Strong numerical and analytical skills
  • Time management skills and ability to multi-task and prioritize work
  • Organizing skills with a pro-active attitude

Benefits

  • Flexible Work Model: Our hybrid approach offers a level of remote work flexibility that supports work-life balance while preserving strong collaboration and team spirit.

title: Founding Head of Growth
description:
Clients Blackbox is a specialized Meta advertising agency that works exclusively with Registered Investment Advisors (RIAs) and independent financial advisory firms. We build and manage Facebook advertising funnels that generate qualified, booked appointments for our clients. We serve one vertical and we do it at a level no generalist agency can match.

You will own both sales and marketing for the company. This is a hands on, individual contributor role where you run our sales process from first conversation to signed contract while also building and executing our internal marketing strategy.

On the sales side, you will take all introductory and discovery calls with inbound prospects, run strategy and pitch presentations, manage the full pipeline from first touch to close, handle objections, follow ups, proposals, and contract negotiations, and build and maintain a sales playbook, objection library, and follow up sequences.

On the marketing side, you will own and operate our internal Meta advertising campaigns, develop and execute our broader marketing strategy including content, brand positioning, and demand generation, elevate the company brand to attract larger and more established clients, and create or direct the creation of marketing assets such as ads, landing pages, case studies, and social content. This role has a clear trajectory toward leading a sales and marketing function. As the company grows and you demonstrate results, there is an opportunity to build a team underneath you and evolve the role into a broader leadership position.

Compensation: $85,000 base salary plus performance based commission on closed business, paid quarterly. OTE is approximately $150,000 per year. Commission structure details will be shared with qualified candidates during the interview process.

Applications without a Loom video will not be considered.

title: Director Community Development Underwriting
location: New York, New York, United States
description:
About the Organization

The Momentus Capital branded family of organizations - which includes Capital Impact Partners and CDC Small Business Finance and Momentus Securities (an SEC-registered broker-dealer, MSRB-registered municipal advisor, a FINRA-approved municipal advisor and municipal securities broker-dealer, FINRA/SIPC member)- are transforming how capital and investments flow into communities to provide people access to the capital and opportunities they deserve.

We are working to reinvent traditional financial systems and advance locally-led solutions that create economic mobility and generational wealth. Through our continuum of financial, knowledge, and social capital, we offer a comprehensive package of loan products, impact investment opportunities, training and business advising programs, and technology solutions.

Our holistic and streamlined approach offers comprehensive solutions for small business entrepreneurs, real estate developers, community-based organizations, and local leaders at every stage of growth, from inception to expansion. When these leaders have the opportunity to succeed, their communities, their residents – and our country – thrive.

Position Summary

The Director Community Development Underwriting is responsible for overseeing loan underwriting functions and for the full lifecycle of new originations and guiding the restructuring and workout analysis for existing borrowers in alignment with the organizational risk appetite. The Director of Community Development Underwriting reports to the Head of Small Business and Community Development Credit within the Risk Team. This position manages a team of commercial underwriters to support Community Development Lending (CDL) originations and supports existing borrowers in the portfolio.

Requirements

Essential Responsibilities

Loan Origination Production

● Lead a team of underwriters to underwrite complex transactions by ensuring comprehensive analysis, eligibility and conformance with underwriting and credit guidelines such as assessment of historical and projected financial performance, cash flow, debt service, repayment and takeout analysis, sponsor/management capacity, leverage, liquidity, collateral, guarantor analysis, sensitivity and stress testing analysis, evaluating industry, funding sources and market conditions, repayment sources and key credit and underwriting risks from screening to closing.

● Exercise sound independent judgement in evaluating transaction structure, risk/return considerations, policy exceptions, mitigants and overall creditworthiness and provide clear recommendations regarding approval, modification, escalation, or decline.

● Recommend appropriate strategies and guidance in collaboration with credit on risk mitigants, covenants, reserves, conditions and other structural guidance, including delivering advanced level underwriting judgements on transactions requiring escalation due to complexity, policy exceptions or other material considerations.

● Serve as the primary interface for the underwriting processes, actively participate in deal discussions by providing recommendations and technical structuring guidance, attend and deliver guidance during pipeline meetings, co-lead credit office hours, manage internal workflow and due diligence with the teams to close loans.

Leadership and Planning

● Provide input to the CDL Origination and the Credit, Risk teams with strategic and tactical planning in conjunction with organizational goals/objectives and new opportunities.

● Collaborate with internal stakeholders, including CDL loan originations, credit, portfolio and special assets to recommend training topics, conduct training where applicable and attend organized trainings for shared learning, discussing lessons learned and growing knowledge on key topics, including attending conferences/trainings.

● Conduct regular 1:1 meetings with direct reports to manage all aspects of building and lead a highly effective team. Oversee and manage staff development activities; coaching, training, monitor team performance by goal setting, assessing performance and communicating performance objectives.

● Responsible for hirings, and completion of justification for backfill and providing input on staffing needs for workforce development and planning.

● Partner with the portfolio and special assets teams, and other departments to improve handoffs and coordination, training on new products, and the release of policies and procedures to ensure alignment.

● Participate in meetings with CDL originations and other stakeholders to represent underwriting functions.

● Ensure good communication and sharing of information within the CDL loan origination team and other stakeholders.

● Collaborate with external partners such as peer CDFIs on industry updates and best practices to incorporate in the CDL processes and procedures.

Lifecycle Credit Underwriting, Origination and Portfolio and Workout Management

● Responsible for quality of underwriting of work products by the underwriting team and other members of the CDL originations teams during structuring such as eligibility, compliance with policies and procedures, including external guarantees, credit enhancements, and other lending tools by identifying strengths, weaknesses, recommend strategies and mitigants to minimize underwriting and credit exceptions to manage credit and underwriting risks.

● Deliver technical support and oversee the financial analysis for (historical, projections, collateral value, guarantor capacity for existing and distressed borrowers to develop and evaluate downside, stress, and exit, and recovery scenarios, including estimated loss exposure, recovery timing, collateral disposition, and other potential strategies in collaboration with other stakeholders to senior management for consideration.

● Review post-closing amendment memos, assess the quality of the financial analysis and other supporting documentation to ensure thorough underwriting to stabilize borrower performance and reduce the frequency of future extensions and modifications.

● Challenge assumptions and identify emerging risks in underwriting analyses, financial projections, valuations, borrower business plans and proposed transaction structures. Review and challenge the proposed workout strategies prepared by designated staff to ensure supporting financial and credit analysis is sufficient to support organizational decision making.

● Collaborate with stakeholders such as credit, originations, portfolio management and special assets teams to deliver technical underwriting guidance, including identifying early warning indicators and recommending strategies to improve borrower performance, address covenant compliance, strengthen liquidity, preserve collateral value, and evaluate alternative repayment options.

● Maintain compliance with appropriate application of credit and underwriting guidelines as well as other supplementary policies and procedures during the analysis and address escalations to appropriate party.

● Apply experience with distressed and underperforming credits to new originations by identifying potential risks in transaction assumptions, borrower projections, repayment and takeout strategies, collateral support, and proposed structures and recommend appropriate risk mitigants to strengthen credit quality.

● Use portfolio performance, delinquency trends, modifications, restructuring and charge offs and workout outcomes to identify underwriting trends, incorporate lessons learned into underwriting guidelines, and transaction structuring.

● Attend special assets and other portfolio risk meetings by delivering technical guidance and recommending strategies to support decision making and mitigating organizational financial exposure. Oversight of the underwriting checklist to ensure underwriting tasks completed by underwriters and loan officers, monitoring progress against the closing deadline and ensuring pipeline loans are actively managed in accordance with the underwriting guidelines.

● Review credit memos and credit analysis to ensure thorough and complete underwriting prior to submission to appropriate party. Provide frequent input to the lending team assigned to the transaction in structuring the transaction.

● Provide underwriting support and or backup as a reviewer and co-approver for credit and amendment memos for Commercial Real Estate (CRE) loans to ensure compliance with guidelines and policies.

● Ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulatory changes, and internal policies within the organization.

Underwriting Process Management and Data Integrity

● Partner with technology on system design/automation, as well working with the operations excellence team on template design/updates, process mapping, testing, and to improve processes.

● Assign and manage workload team in conjunction with Credit, CDL Originations management and other stakeholders as appropriate for new origination as well as supporting existing borrowers in the portfolio

● Provide guidance to originations and other teams such input on templates, forms and other documents that capture underwriting requirements.

● Ensure team is meeting all established service level agreements and deadlines to manage the underwriting process to support CDL originations with loan closings, including portfolio and special assets portfolios

● Serve as lead to update and maintain updates to the underwriting guidelines for approval to Credit and Risk, continuous review of procedures, processes, and guidelines with a keen focus on process improvement and efficiency.

● Support credit and risk with special projects, including using portfolio performance to identify emerging risks, recurring underwriting exceptions, process gaps, and opportunity to improve loan quality.

● Support the Credit and Risk team with input on credit guidelines and other policies and procedures.

● Support Head of Small Business and Community Development with other functions as identified, including serving as backup for other members of the Credit team.

● Leverage workload management tools/reports for appropriate coaching to CDL for production & quality metrics.

● Provide input to stakeholders with developing new lending products, drafting guidelines and other materials to grow impact and loan production.

● Understand and support data integrity in accordance with organizational policies.

This job description outlines the primary responsibilities and essential functions of the role; however, additional duties may be assigned as needed to support business operations.

Professional Skills, Education and Experience

● Bachelor’s degree or advanced degree in business or public administration, finance or related field preferred. Education level will be considered on a holistic basis considering both education and work experience.

● 10 years of advanced commercial and community development lending underwriting and/or lending experience, cash flow analysis, sensitivity analysis, stress testing, leverage and liquidity analysis, collateral and guarantor evaluation, risk ratings, debt service capacity assessment, collateral valuation, loan structuring and risk mitigations.

● Demonstrated experience exercising credit judgment and making or presenting recommendations on complex transactions, policy exceptions, restructuring and other significant amendments and modifications.

● Prior leadership experience with a minimum of three (3) years managing direct reports.

● Successful incumbent will possess strong underwriting, credit risk management and impact area expertise, have excellent written and verbal communication skills, strong management/coaching skills, superior process management and operational effectiveness skills, strong decision-making skills and are a result-oriented team player.

● Ability to maintain big picture focus while attending detailed work and providing thorough documentation.

● Demonstrated ability to work productively and accurately in a fast-paced environment with multiple projects and stringent deadlines.

● Strong proficiency in a PC environment using Google, Microsoft Office, Adobe Acrobat, and Salesforce and other loan origination systems is required. The ability to learn and adapt to a changing IT environment is required.

● Demonstrates professionalism, diplomacy and composure and is flexible and able to adapt to a variety of situations.

● Excellent communication and collaboration skills with team members across all levels of the organization.

● Strong analytical, loan compliance, risk management, sound judgement, manage ambiguity, complexity and ability to manage underwriting and credit risk to manage organizational financial exposure.

● Candidates should have demonstrated strong commitment to the Momentus mission.

● Previous experience with Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) is a plus.

Benefits

The salary range for this position is $118,536 – $182,000 and may be eligible for an annual discretionary incentive.

  • Structure A: $118,536 - $158,246 All locations except Structures B and C
  • Structure B: $131,707- $175,829 Washington, D.C.; Maryland; Virginia (DMV); non-Bay Area California markets; and Massachusetts
  • Structure C: $144,482- $182,000 New York; New Jersey; and the California Bay Area

All employees must be legally authorized to work in the United States. The company will not sponsor applicants for work visas.

title: Mental Health/Disability Specialist
description:
Child Start, Inc. is currently seeking a Mental Health/Disability Specialist to join our team. As a Mental Health/Disability Specialist, you will collaborate with classroom staff in identifying children in need of individualized developmental and behavioral services. You will recommend and demonstrate strategies to help children adapt and succeed in the classroom and at home. Additionally, you will refer children for additional evaluation by partner agencies for Part B and Part C services and mental health consultation. You will document and track screenings, individualized services, and referrals in our child-tracking software.

In this role, you will provide direct support to children and families as needed through Program Intervention Plans. You will also work with our Mental Health and Disabilities Coordinator to recommend referrals to partner agencies and provide assistance with Individual Education Plans (IEP) or Individual Family Service Plans (IFSP).

  • Observe children in classrooms and home settings to help classroom staff identify children with developmental and behavioral needs; attend month Multidisciplinary Case Reviews
  • Recommend strategies to help children with identified concerns adapts more successfully to classroom environment; collaborate with Teachers and Coaches to develop Program Intervention Plans (PIP) and Behavior Safety Plans (BSP) to provide direct support for children; collaborate with Site Supervisor to lead PIP and BSP meeting with parents and classroom staff; demonstrate and mentor teachers in using these strategies
  • Support classroom staff in identifying and implementing IEP/IFSP recommendations
  • Work with contracted Mental health Consultants on-site to implement social-emotional and behavioral recommendations
  • Monitor required developmental and behavioral screenings; train and support classroom staff in using screening tools and complete screenings in a timely manner as defined by HS performance standards
  • Identify potential concerns from screenings; initiate referral to CAET for review and recommendations; assist classroom staff in completing paperwork for referrals for developmental/speech evaluations and mental consultation
  • Support staff in communicating with parents the results of children’s developmental and behavioral screenings and any concerns that are identified; assist parents in communicating their concerns for their children with site staff; when appropriate attend home visits with Family Services Staff and/or Teacher to observe children and provide support to families
  • Encourage families to pursue referrals for developmental/speech evaluation and services as well as mental/behavioral health consultation and services; monitor progress of referrals; link parents to community support services as needed
  • Serve as a collaborative team member with the entire MHDB team; share duties with team members such as monitoring health checklist for MHDB requirements and attending Health Literacy events
  • Take direction and supervision from assigned Mental Health & Disability Coordinator while recognizing responsibility to the assigned Site Supervisor(s) for helping the entire center(s) achieve success with children in attendance.

Requirements
