About Catalyst Metals

Catalyst Metals Limited owns and operates the Plutonic Gold Mine in the Eastern Gascoyne region of Western Australia. The operation is undergoing continued underground growth, with multiple mining areas progressing from development into production.

Catalyst is focused on building a long-life gold business supported by disciplined technical planning and strong operational execution.

Catalyst Metals Limited is listed on the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX code: CYL).

Catalyst Metals Ltd is an equal opportunity employer and encourages applications from people who identify as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander.

About the Role

With more than 15 years of mine life ahead of us, there’s never been a better time to join our underground team. We take pride in the ground we work in – competent rock, a strong safety culture and a modern Sandvik fleet that sets you up for success.

As we grow across the belt, our satellite operations are creating opportunities for exposure to different ore bodies and mining environments, including upcoming narrow vein and paste-fill operations. This provides variety in your day-to-day work and the chance to broaden your underground capability across multiple styles of mining.

Backed by long-term job security and genuine progression pathways, this is a place where you can build a sustainable underground career while continuing to develop your skills.

As a Mining Supervisor, you'll play a key role in leading crews, delivering safe and productive outcomes, and supporting the continued growth of our underground operations.

This opportunity offers genuine variety. You may work as Shift Boss / Shift Supervisor at our main underground operation, or across our satellite deposits where you'll be part of a smaller, tight-knit team and take a more hands-on approach to leadership. In these environments, you'll guide your crew, fulfil your statutory responsibilities, and step in where needed to keep operations moving safely and efficiently.

You'll have the opportunity to influence how we operate, mentor developing team members and help build capable, high-performing crews. Backed by long-term job security and genuine progression pathways, this is an opportunity to develop your leadership capability within a growing Australian gold producer.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and coordinate your crew of up to 15 people to achieve production and development targets using Sandvik development and production fleet
  • Fulfil Section 26 statutory responsibilities in accordance with legislative requirements
  • Promote and maintain a strong safety culture across all underground activities
  • Monitor and coordinate daily underground mining activities to ensure operational efficiency
  • Ensure compliance with mining plans, site procedures and legislative requirements
  • Support, mentor and develop underground operators and team members
  • Work collaboratively with Technical Services, Maintenance and other key stakeholders
  • Drive accountability, performance and continuous improvement within your team

Requirements

About You

To be successful in this role, you will have:

  • WA Underground Supervisor's Certificate of Competency (Section 26 Statutory Qualification)
  • Proven experience in a similar underground mining supervisory role
  • Sound knowledge of the Mine Safety and Inspection Act and Regulations
  • Strong communication and leadership skills with the ability to engage across all levels
  • Well-developed organisational skills and a proactive approach
  • Strong commitment to safety and team performance
  • Current WA C-Class Driver's Licence
  • Current Dangerous Goods Security Card (DGSC)
  • National Police Clearance (or ability to obtain)

Desirable:

  • First Aid Certificate
  • Experience working across multiple underground mining operations or satellite deposits
  • Experience leading teams in both production and development environments

Benefits

Why Catalyst?

FIFO isn’t for everyone — it requires commitment and time away from home. That’s why we place strong emphasis on creating a supportive team culture, approachable leadership and an environment where people work hard, back each other in, and still find time to have a laugh and enjoy what site has to offer.

  • Short, walkable commute from camp to site with your own permanent room
  • Exposure to a growing and expanding underground operation
  • Opportunity to contribute beyond your core role and influence how we operate

title: Artiste en éclairage / Lighting Artist - Feature Animation (short-term)
description:
NOTRE HISTOIRE

Depuis plus de 35 ans, Bardel Entertainment est le chef de file de l'industrie de l'animation grâce à son engagement inébranlable en matière de qualité, de créativité et d'innovation. Nous sommes un studio internationalement reconnu, lauréat d'un Emmy Award® - dans deux villes canadiennes de premier plan, Vancouver et Montreal - et la force créatrice derrière des succès d'audience tels que Le Prince Dragon, Rick and Morty, Teen Titans Go ! et Diary of a Wimpy Kid.

OUR STORY

For more than 35 years, Bardel Entertainment has led the animation industry through unwavering commitment to quality, creativity, and innovation. We are an internationally recognized, Emmy Award®-winning studio – in two prominent Canadian cities, Vancouver and Montreal – and the creative force behind top audience hits such as The Dragon Prince, Rick and Morty, Teen Titans Go!, and Diary of a Wimpy Kid.

Requirements

En tant qu'artiste en lighting, vous jouerez un rôle essentiel pour donner vie à nos mondes animés. Vous serez responsable du lighting et l’ombrages des scènes, des personnages et des environnements afin d'obtenir l'esthétique visuelle, l'ambiance et l'impact narratif souhaités pour notre projet d'animation. Vous collaborerez avec les équipes créatives et techniques afin de garantir que nos projets répondent aux normes de qualité les plus strictes.

Ce que vous ferez :

  • Utilisez votre expertise pour concevoir, développer et exécuter des configurations de lighting complexes et des matériaux pour les personnages, les accessoires et les environnements, en veillant à ce qu'ils répondent à la vision créative du projet.
  • Collaborer avec d'autres services pour optimiser les scènes en vue du rendu, en veillant à l'efficacité tout en maintenant la qualité visuelle.
  • Travailler en collaboration avec le superviseur/artiste principal de lighting et les autres départements pour maintenir la continuité de lighting et de l'ombrage sur l'ensemble du projet, notamment en résolvant les problèmes créatifs et techniques.
  • Identifier et résoudre les problèmes techniques liés au lighting et au rendu et mettre en œuvre des solutions créatives pour les surmonter.
  • Contribuer au développement et à l'amélioration du pipeline lighting, des outils et des flux de travail afin d'accroître l'efficacité et la qualité.
  • Gérer les tâches de rendu, y compris la mise en place de passes de rendu, la gestion des ressources de la ferme de rendu et la garantie de temps de rendu efficaces.
  • Effectuer des contrôles de qualité rigoureux pour s'assurer que les prises de vue finales respectent les normes visuelles et techniques du projet.

Ce que vous apporterez :

  • Au moins 5 ans d'expérience ou plus en tant que artiste lighting dans l'industrie de l'animation ou des effets visuels.
  • Maîtrise des logiciels 3D standard de l'industrie (p. ex., Maya, Houdini).
  • Maîtrise de Katana, y compris le travail avec des modèles dans un pipeline.
  • Solide compréhension de la théorie des couleurs, de la composition et des principes cinématographiques.
  • Solide connaissance des langages d'ombrage (par exemple, RenderMan, Arnold).
  • Familiarité avec les logiciels de composition (par exemple, Nuke).
  • Solides compétences en matière de résolution de problèmes et capacité à travailler efficacement dans des délais serrés.
  • Excellentes aptitudes à la communication et au travail d'équipe.
  • Une passion pour la narration et un sens artistique développé.
  • Fournir des conseils et un soutien aux artistes lighting débutants et aux autres membres de l'équipe, en favorisant un environnement d'apprentissage collaboratif.

Emplacement: Quebec, Canada

___________________________________________________________________________________________

As a Lighting Artist, you will play a crucial role in bringing our animated worlds to life. You will be responsible for lighting and shading scenes, characters, and environments to achieve the desired visual aesthetic, mood, and storytelling impact of our animated project. You will collaborate closely with our creative and technical teams to ensure that our projects meet the highest quality standards.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Use your expertise to design, develop, and execute complex lighting setups, and materials for characters, props, and environments, ensuring they meet the creative vision of the project.
  • Collaborate with other departments to optimize scenes for rendering, ensuring efficiency while maintaining visual quality.
  • Work closely with the Lighting Supervisor/Lead, and other departments to maintain continuity of lighting and shading across the project, including solving creative and technical challenges.
  • Identify and troubleshoot technical issues related to lighting and rendering and implement creative solutions to overcome them.
  • Contribute to the development and improvement of the lighting pipeline, tools, and workflows to enhance efficiency and quality.
  • Manage rendering tasks, including setting up render passes, managing render farm resources, and ensuring efficient render times.
  • Conduct rigorous quality control checks to ensure that final shots meet the project's visual and technical standards.

What you’ll bring:

  • 5+ years experience as a Lighting Artist in the animation or visual effects industry.
  • Proficiency in industry-standard 3D software (e.g., Maya, Houdini).
  • Proficiency using Katana including working with templates in a pipeline.
  • Strong understanding of colour theory, composition, and cinematography principles.
  • Strong knowledge of shading languages (e.g., RenderMan, Arnold).
  • Familiarity with compositing software (e.g., Nuke).
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work efficiently under tight deadlines.
  • Excellent communication and teamwork skills.
  • A passion for storytelling and a strong artistic eye.
  • Provide guidance and support to junior lighting artists and other team members, fostering a collaborative learning environment.

Location: Quebec, Canada

title: M26333 - GRC Specialist (Governance, Risk and Compliance) (Locally recruited)
description:
CIMMYT is a cutting edge, non-profit, international organization dedicated to solving tomorrow's problems today. It is entrusted with fostering improved quantity, quality, and dependability of production systems and basic cereals such as maize, wheat, triticale, sorghum, millets, and associated crops through applied agricultural science, particularly in the Global South, through building strong partnerships. This combination enhances the livelihood trajectories and resilience of millions of resource-poor farmers, while working towards a more productive, inclusive, and resilient agrifood system within planetary boundaries.

For more information, visit cimmyt.org.

The GRC Specialist will serve as the internal subject-matter expert for governance, risk, and compliance across CIMMYT's enterprise application ecosystem (Dynamics 365 F&O, HR and Customer Engagement, Power Platform, ICERTIS Contract Intelligence, and Sapience HR), responsible for operating a single cross-platform GRC framework covering access control and segregation of duties, licensing and entitlement governance, data privacy, and audit readiness, under the supervision of the ERP Program Manager and in coordination with the CIMMYT ERP team, KMIT, and control and process owners across the institution.

  • Own and operate the full-lifecycle Access Management procedure (request, approval, provisioning, modification, recertification, revocation), and close gaps against each platform.
  • Maintain the privileged access elevation model (justification, approval, duration limits, session logging, post-use review) and the required log set, retention, and monitoring per platform.
  • Maintain the consolidated cross-platform segregation-of-duties (SoD) conflict matrix, run riskranked assessments, agree remediation or mitigating controls with process owners, and operate recurring SoD reporting.
  • Periodically review all accounts (active, dormant, duplicate, generic, shared, service, external), remediate orphaned accounts, and reconcile reclaimed accounts to license entitlement.
  • Maintain an entitlement register per platform, reconcile licenses against actual usage and quantify the gap, assess how security role design drives license tier, and operate request, approval, and reclamation controls so reclaimed accounts convert into recovered cost.
  • Maintain the data inventory and processing record, define and apply retention and disposal schedules, and enable data subject request handling within statutory timeframes.
  • Maintain and test the IT general controls (ITGC) matrix (access, change management, program development, computer operations) across all platforms; report deficiencies, require appropriate corrective actions from process and control owners, challenge inadequate or delayed remediation responses, and track remediation to closure.
  • Keep the evidence base continuously audit-ready, run readiness assessments before scheduled audits, act as coordination point during internal and external audit fieldwork, and track prior findings to closure.
  • Maintain the GRC policy and procedures set with owners and review cycles, the ERP/IT risk register on the institutional scale, and automated key risk and control indicators reporting breaches as they occur.
  • Assess interface controls (completeness, reconciliation, failure alerting, connector privileges) and the control environment of vendors with system or data access, including KMIT, reviewing assurance reports, contractual security, breach notification and audit rights, and relevant service levels.
  • Operate the exception register with expiry dates, contribute to change advisory and incident root-cause analysis, and train control owners on their obligations.
  • Deliver monthly progress reports and the quarterly GRC dashboard to the ERP Program Manager and governance bodies, escalating material findings directly.
  • Perform other related tasks within the job level as may be requested by the immediate supervisor.

Requirements

Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in IT GRC or IT audit, of which at least 3 on enterprise application platforms; ITGC design, testing, and remediation experience in an audited environment.
  • Hands-on experience with the Dynamics 365 security model (F&O roles, duties, and privileges; CE role-based security) and practical ERP SoD design or assessment.
  • Experience with Power Platform governance (environments, DLP policies, Dataverse security) and license reconciliation.
  • Working knowledge of data protection law and of ISO 27001, NIST CSF, or COBIT.
  • Experience preferred; CISA, CRISC, CISM, or CIPP certification an advantage; experience with ICERTIS or a comparable CLM platform, HRIS governance, a GRC tool (Pathlock, Fastpath, SAP GRC, ServiceNow IRM), or in multi-jurisdiction environments an advantage.
  • Strong analytical skills and proficiency with reporting and dashboard tools; Power BI or equivalent an advantage.
  • Full professional proficiency in English.
  • Familiarity with ticketing tools and D365 administration highly desirable.
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills without direct line authority, with the ability to interact professionally with internal clients across IT, Finance, HR, Legal, and vendor teams.

Benefits

CIMMYT offers an attractive remuneration package and support for continuous professional development. In addition to the provisions of the Mexican Labor Law our package of benefits includes year-end bonus (40 days), vacation premium (56%), life and medical insurance, supermarket coupons, savings fund, social Mexican benefits (IMSS, SAR / Infonavit).

Please note only short-listed candidates will be contacted.

Foreign national candidates must have legal documents to work in Mexico.

This position will remain open until filled.

CIMMYT is an equal opportunity employer. It fosters a multicultural work environment that values gender equality, teamwork, and respect for diversity.

title: RfP: Aviation EU External Evaluation
description:

Reports to: Senior Head of Network Learning and Innovation

Preferred timezone: Based in Europe

Budget: € 30,000 - 39,000 (inclusive of all taxes, fees and expenses)

Contract: Fixed-term assignment, Oct 2026 - March 2027 (final dates subject to contracting).

About Climate Catalyst

Climate Catalyst is a non-profit dedicated to galvanising the collective power of business, investors, and civil society to influence and accelerate policy change in Asia and Europe. We work to strengthen collaboration and mobilise new actors on pivotal climate challenges to build power and compel political leaders to act at the speed and scale needed to tackle the climate crisis.

Our Aviation programme aims to enable narrative change and private sector action to tackle aviation’s climate impacts in Europe. As the programme approaches its close in March 2027, an independent external evaluation will provide credible, externally validated evidence of what was achieved, assess the resilience of those achievements, and generate transferable learning for future work. The evaluation is not intended to inform ongoing programme delivery; its primary purpose is to support a rigorous and well-evidenced closure of the programme, including partner feedback and a detailed assessment of impact achieved.

Climate Catalyst is seeking proposals from qualified firms to design and deliver an independent end-term evaluation of its Aviation programme in Europe. This Request for Proposals sets out the background, scope, deliverables, qualifications, submission requirements and assessment criteria for the assignment. This is an open invitation to firms with demonstrated experience in impact evaluation, particularly for NGOs.

Purpose and Objectives

  • Assess evidence of impact across all current and past programme levers including narrative change and private sector action.
  • Capture and evaluate ecosystem coordination, narrative shifts, and influence-related changes, alongside more direct programme outputs and outcomes, as the Aviation programme is a systems-level programme.
  • Generate credible, independent evidence of results to support ongoing donor engagement, strengthen partner relationships, and validate the programme’s theory of change.
  • Build internal evaluation capacity within the Climate Catalyst team by making evaluation design, methods, and analytical reasoning transparent and participatory throughout the process, enabling staff to apply similar approaches independently in the future.

Requirements

The evaluation will specifically address:

  1. Measure and define the impact: What impact has the European Aviation programme had?
    • Did the programme contribute to real-world change, as defined by its impact ladders and OKRs? Did the programme deliver its intended outputs and outcomes? This includes how outputs and interventions have been perceived and valued by stakeholders, and (subject to discussion during proposal review), what contribution the programme has made to emissions reduction pathways in the aviation sector.
    • To what extent has the Aviation programme contributed to shifts in the EU/UK policy landscape for sustainable aviation? To what extent do these shifts represent steps forward on ambition, or in mitigating the impact of rollbacks?
    • What evidence exists that the programme influenced the wider narrative around aviation within civil society, and among policymakers, media, and the public?
    • How has the private sector action work (targeting e-fuels companies, incumbent fuel makers, institutional investors and banks) shaped awareness, knowledge, and behaviour related to aviation decarbonisation and sustainable aviation fuels?
    • To what extent have civil society partners strengthened their capacity and confidence to advocate and communicate strategically on aviation climate issues?
  2. Assess evidence of strategy and tactic effectiveness: Which strategies and approaches worked well, and why?
    • Which activities proved most effective in influencing the European aviation policy environment or private sector knowledge/behaviour, and under what conditions?
    • What was the programme’s distinctive contribution compared to other actors working on tackling the climate impacts of aviation in Europe?
    • How could the durability of any programme achievements be enhanced?
    • What legacy has our programme activities been able to leave or unlock?
  3. Produce learning for future programmes: What would we do differently? What could or should others replicate?
    • Which assumptions in the theory of change proved most and least valid? What are the implications for future work related to those assumptions?
    • What does the programme’s experience reveal about the role of private sector action, strategic communications, research, strategy co-design, network building, and policy advocacy in driving change?
    • How did the programme adapt its strategy in response to shifts in the political and wider external environment?
    • What should the programme team do differently, and what are the transferable lessons for other programmes?

Scope of Work

  • Co-design the evaluation framework with Climate Catalyst, including a working session that explains the rationale behind methodological choices.
  • Gather and synthesise qualitative and quantitative evidence of impact, including from individuals and organisations engaging with our programme outputs. This should include synthesis of what the programme started, contributed to, delivered and achieved, including an assessment of policy resilience and longevity.
  • Conduct a ‘listening report’: structured engagement with programme partners and stakeholders (industry, financial institutions, civil society, researchers, philanthropies) to capture perspectives on programme relevance, effectiveness, and influence. This should gather evidence of what Climate Catalyst achieved and how it was perceived by those it worked with, to be used in communications materials about the programme.
  • Assess where the policy landscape remains contested at programme Close: the evaluation should assess the extent to which the programme has increased the likelihood of positive policy developments, or contributed to mitigating worse outcomes, and whether the right actors are in place to continue the work.
  • Produce a final report summarising evidence of impact of the Aviation programme.

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Demonstrated experience in programme evaluation in advocacy, policy influence, or civil society contexts, ideally in climate or energy transition.
  • Strong mixed methods research skills, including stakeholder interviewing, and experience with contribution analysis or similar approaches to attributing policy influence.
  • Ability to assess the resilience and longevity of policy outcomes, not just whether change occurred, but how durable it is.
  • Familiarity with theory of change approaches and the ability to interrogate assumptions critically and constructively.
  • Experience assessing narrative change, eg.media analysis and social listening, is desirable.
  • Excellent written English and ability to translate complex findings; ability to produce clear, credible, evidence-based reports for donor and partner audiences.
  • Ability to work in a participatory and capacity-building oriented way, making methods and reasoning transparent to internal teams, not just producing outputs.
  • Ability to assess and provide estimation or quantification of the emission reduction and/or climate impact of the programme is desired but not required.

Benefits

Compensation + Benefits

  • The budget for this assignment is € 30,000-39,000, inclusive of all taxes, fees and expenses.

Proposal Requirements

To be considered, please submit the following:

  1. Technical Proposal (maximum 4 pages)
      1. Demonstrate understanding of the assignment and proposed evaluation approach and methodology
      2. Include workplan and timeline mapped to the timeline and deliverables indicated in this Request for Proposals
      3. Outline how the firm will work in a participatory, capacity-building way with the Climate Catalyst team.
  2. Team information
      1. A short profile of the proposed team composition, including legal status and registration. Include CVs of lead personnel and their roles on the assignment.
      2. At least two examples of comparable assignments and two client references
  3. Financial proposal
      1. All-inclusive budget within the stated ceiling

How proposals will be assessed

Proposals will be evaluated on a combined technical and financial basis using the weighting below. Shortlisted firms will be invited to interview before a final decision is made.

Procurement Timeline

RfP issued: August 10, 2026

Proposal submission deadline: August 31, 2026

Interviews with shortlisted firms: w/o September 7, 2026

title: Assistant Research Associate-Roster
description:

This combination enhances the livelihood trajectories and resilience of millions of resource-poor farmers, while working towards a more productive, inclusive, and resilient agrifood system within planetary boundaries. CIMMYT is a core CGIAR Research Center, a global research partnership for a food-secure future, dedicated to reducing poverty, enhancing food and nutrition security and improving natural resources.

For more information, visit cimmyt.org.

CIMMYT is building a Roster of qualified professionals to be considered for future opportunities in various locations and areas of expertise.

What is a Roster?

A roster is a pool of pre-assessed, qualified candidates who may be contacted when a relevant position becomes available. This approach allows us to respond more efficiently to hiring needs and significantly shorten recruitment timelines when vacancies arise.

CIMMYT has opened a call for applications for Project Management related positions such as:

Assistant Research Associate roles in CIMMYT play a crucial part in monitoring progress, evaluating outcomes, and adapting strategies to meet evolving needs. The focus is on delivering impactful, science-based solutions that address global challenges in food security, climate resilience, and rural livelihoods.

The location of the related positions will be in any of the countries where CIMMYT operates/multiple locations.

In addition to the provisions of the Mexican Labor Law our package of benefits includes year-end bonus (40 days), vacation premium (56%), life and medical insurance, supermarket coupons, savings fund, social Mexican benefits (IMSS, SAR / Infonavit).

title: 2027 Associate Position at Close Concerns
description:
Close Concerns, a healthcare information company that advocates for people with diabetes and obesity, seeks undergraduate applicants for its prestigious two-year Associate Program, based in San Francisco.

  • The Associate Program provides new college graduates unparalleled exposure to the real worlds of healthcare and business, significant work experience and responsibility, national and international travel, and extensive support for graduate school applications.
  • For candidates considering work experience before post-graduate studies - such as medical school – this Program is an outstanding way to enhance your skills and knowledge, interact with healthcare leaders (clinical, scientific, and business), and use a different part of your brain, all the while improving your chances of being admitted to a top graduate program.

Our organization, led by Kelly Close, has a meaningful social purpose: improving life for people with diabetes and obesity, two of the most pervasive public health problems of our time. This is a mission that everyone here takes to heart - if you feel that you can share it, please apply.

-----------------------------------------------------

The Close Concerns Associate Program

Close Concerns, founded in 2002, is a healthcare information company focused on diabetes, pre-diabetes, and obesity, dedicated to improving patient, clinical, and system outcomes.

We do this by educating physicians, researchers, business leaders, policy makers, and manufacturers about the most important news and research in the field via an online publication. With thousands of subscribers at academic institutions, nonprofit organizations, drug and medical device companies, and government bodies, Closer Look (our premium subscription news service) is widely read and respected in the healthcare community.

Close Concerns Associates research and write our products, frequently by attending scientific conferences and interviewing experts, including world-class endocrinologists, cardiologists, as well as a range of other scientific and business leaders. Associates broaden their minds, sharpen their communication skills, and quickly become experts in all aspects of diabetes – such as therapies, medical devices, digital health, clinical research, public health, regulatory, and business issues. On occasion, Associates author and publish research papers in peer-reviewed journals or speak at major conferences. Most are excited by the significant level of responsibility they are given and their access to thought leaders, researchers, clinicians, and business executives.

Close Concerns provides ongoing support for graduate school admissions. Nearly all our Associates go on to attend a top ranked graduate program. One hundred percent of those who have applied to grad school have been accepted. Since 2007, over half have attended either Penn, Columbia, Harvard, UCSF or Yale (most for medical school). The specific work at Close Concerns and the reputation of the Associate Program help to create a much stronger application and turn applicants into better prepared and more compelling candidates. To support associates in the application process, Close Concerns provides customized and compelling reference letters, free consults with an excellent graduate school admissions advisor, and access to our alumni network – together with time off and some financial support for exams and exam prep (e.g., MCAT).

Typically, the Associate Program involves significant travel in the United States and internationally, which Associates find enriching. Our conferences have allowed our associates to travel to global destinations such as Florence, London, Madrid, Boston, Seattle, Chennai, Aspen, Austin, Barcelona, Berlin, Busan, Chicago, Keystone, Las Vegas, Los Angeles, Liverpool, Miami, New Orleans, New York City, Orlando, Paris, Washington DC, Stockholm, Rome, Chicago, San Diego, Lisbon, and Abu Dhabi. Our Associates typically travel 30% to 40% of the time and collect a lot of air miles!

Our organization is located in San Francisco – an exciting and beautiful city. Our compensation package is commensurate with living in San Francisco, and we provide support in finding nearby accommodation and offer excellent work benefits (including quality healthcare, 401(k), free public transportation pass, gym/yoga membership, a kitchen stocked with healthy foods, and a great team atmosphere).

-----------------------------------------------------
About You

The Associate position at Close Concerns is ideal for someone with a science or pre-medical background. If you have an additional interest in data analysis, computer science, public health, health policy, economics or business (in addition to science or pre-medical) this is considered a bonus! Strong critical thinking and strong writing skills are both essential.

Requirements for successful candidates:

  • Demonstrated academic excellence
  • Scientific background; research and/or data science experience is encouraged
  • Exceptionally strong writing, editing, and synthesizing skills
  • Strong critical thinking and analytic skills
  • Adaptable and flexible approach to work
  • High energy and ability to keep multiple projects moving simultaneously
  • Ability to work independently and to collaborate frequently within small teams
  • Reliability; commitment to schedules and deadlines
  • Two-year commitment to the position

We pride ourselves on our friendly and inclusive environment. Through our recruiting, we are committed to sustaining our diverse workplace.

-----------------------------------------------------
TO APPLY

This is a highly sought-after position. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and applicants are encouraged to apply early. The final deadline is November 30, 2026. Those who apply before October 15 may receive an in-person interview invitation early. The final round of interviews will be held in San Francisco January 7-9, 2027.

Please apply through Workable. Please do not apply through your school’s career portal – we will not receive these applications.

Close Concerns treats everyone equally and encourages candidates of all backgrounds and from all schools to apply. We are looking forward to hearing from you!

In addition to the question fields in our online application, please attach the following as a PDF document in the “Resume” field: Resume as PDF – please include undergraduate GPA, major, and graduation year.

Please email info@closeconcerns.com if you have any challenges with the application form.

-----------------------------------------------------
Testimonials

We are really proud of helping our Alumni of Close Concerns take another important step in their journey. Our alums have attended medical school and other graduate schools at UCSF, Stanford, the University of Pennsylvania, Harvard, Dartmouth, and many other outstanding institutions. Those that have delayed graduate school have done so many interesting things ranging from teaching high school biology to working with start-ups to founding their own start-ups, often funded by prestigious sources (e.g., Route 66 Ventures, Y Combinator, etc.)

Here are some reflections about the role from previous Associates:

“By the numbers, Close Concerns gave me the opportunity to attend nearly 50 conferences, plan nearly two dozen events, and conduct over a dozen interviews with clinical trialists, clinicians, and business leaders. The mentors I found through Close Concerns supported me in countless ways, and the connections I made through them led to impactful and valuable experiences. Through it all, I developed poise and perspective – qualities for which I find myself deeply grateful as a medical student today.”

- Elaine Young (Dartmouth College '22, Ohio State University College of Medicine '30)

"At Close Concerns, I absolutely loved the opportunity to scale a steep learning curve and gain deep expertise in the scientific, business, and policy aspects of the diabetes and obesity fields, all while working with some of the brightest, kindest people I've met. I savored being able to interview clinical trial leaders and pharmaceutical executives and ask pressing questions. My work at Close Concerns has shaped my interests in medical school and has enabled me to ask worthwhile research questions."

- Ashwin Chetty (Yale College '21, Yale School of Medicine '27)

"As my first position out of college, Close Concerns provided me an excellent opportunity to learn, travel, lead, and most importantly, spend time with truly great people. In modern public health, few issues rival the urgency of diabetes and obesity, so it was a great opportunity to work in that space and develop subject matter expertise."

- Albert Cai (University of Michigan '19, Senior Regulatory Affairs Specialist at Biolinq, Co-Founder of Harbor)

"Close Concerns was possibly the best gap year job I could imagine before heading to graduate school. I certainly wouldn’t be at Harvard Medical School without it. It was an amazing opportunity to dive headfirst into the inner workings of the pharmaceutical industry. The job provides a front row view, ranging from basic science research to clinical trials to market dynamics. It was an immersive learning experience that blossomed into a passion for diabetes and obesity that I carry with me each day in my clinical interactions. I also built incredible relationships with my colleagues that have transformed into lifelong friendships. I am forever grateful for the two years I spent there!”

- Claire Holleman (Amherst College ‘21, Harvard Medical School ‘27)

“Associates at Close Concerns have more independence and responsibility than almost any other graduates fresh out of college. The job is exciting, fast-paced, and the best testing ground I could imagine for learning how to become successful in any field. “

- Jenny Jin (Harvard College ’06, UCSF School of Medicine ’12, Resident, Orthopedic Surgeon, Brigham and Women’s Hospital, Boston, General Orthopedic Surgeon, Saint Alphonsus, Boise, Idaho)

“Simply put, I loved working at Close Concerns because I was able to work with incredibly bright, driven, and fun people all committed to working together to make an impact. The best part about Close Concerns is that you never leave the community. I even ended up co-founding

Adventris Pharmaceuticals with a fellow Close Concerns alum.”

- Jen Herbach (Amherst College ’07, Harvard Business School ’13, Co-Founder and CEO, Adventris Pharmaceuticals)

“While I certainly value the skills I learned at Close Concerns, I am most appreciative of the perspective I gained. The work gave me an exhaustive understanding of the many forces driving medical care and health policy – where those forces succeed and where they fall short. My experiences at Close Concerns have fueled my own passion to be persistent, resourceful, and dedicated in my own career.”

- Eric Chang (Pomona College '09, UCSF School of Medicine ’14, Radiation Oncologist, UCLA Medical Center, Los Angeles ‘18, University of Colorado School of Medicine Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation Resident ‘21)

“Being an associate at Close Concerns was the experience of a lifetime and one I think back to often. I got a unique insider look at the worlds of diabetes care, the pharmaceutical and medical device industries, and the healthcare system as a whole — all while traveling the world. Close Concerns was an amazing place to work, and my time there primed me well for a career in healthcare.”

- Manu Venkat (UCSF School of Medicine '19, Columbia University Resident '22, NYU Langone Gastroenterology Fellow)

Join us and contribute to strategic innovation, regulatory excellence, and digital transformation in the insurance industry.

Strategic Consulting & Client Advisory

  • Drive new product development, leveraging telematics, usage-based insurance (UBI), embedded insurance, and AI-driven pricing models.

title: Charge-Up Operator | Underground Gold Mining | FIFO from Perth 8:6 7:7
description:
Charge-Up Operator | Underground Gold Mining | FIFO from Perth 8:6 7:7

About Catalyst Metals

Catalyst Metals Limited owns and operates the Plutonic Gold Mine in the Eastern Gascoyne region of Western Australia. The operation is undergoing continued underground growth, with multiple mining areas progressing from development into production.

Catalyst is focused on building a long-life gold business supported by disciplined technical planning and strong operational execution.

Catalyst Metals Limited is listed on the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX code: CYL).

Catalyst Metals Ltd is an equal opportunity employer and encourages applications from people who identify as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander.

About the Role

We take pride in the ground we work in – competent rock, a strong safety culture and a modern Sandvik fleet that sets you up for success. You’ll find a supportive team environment with real pathways for development, working in technically challenging conditions that build depth in your skills and exposure to precision underground mining.

As production ramps up across our underground operation, Charge-Up Operators play a critical role in safely delivering high-quality blasting outcomes that drive consistent production performance.

Working in modern underground conditions with a strong safety culture and well-supported blasting systems, you’ll be responsible for charging development headings and stopes to design specifications. Accuracy, discipline and strict adherence to procedures are essential, as your work directly influences fragmentation, dilution control and downstream productivity.

This is a role for operators who take pride in doing things properly, understand the importance of controlled blasting, and want to be part of a team where safety and precision come first.

Key Responsibilities

  • Safely transport, handle and charge explosives in underground environments
  • Load blast holes to design specifications in development and production headings
  • Install and connect initiation systems in accordance with procedures
  • Conduct pre-charge inspections and verify ground conditions
  • Ensure compliance with all explosive handling regulations and site procedures
  • Collaborate closely with drillers, supervisors and blasting engineers
  • Maintain accurate records of explosive usage and blast loading
  • Support safe blast clearance and firing procedures

Requirements

About You

To be successful in this role, you will have:

  • Proven experience in underground charge-up or blasting operations
  • Strong commitment to safety, procedures and risk awareness
  • Ability to work accurately in high-risk environments requiring attention to detail
  • Current Shotfirer's Licence or recognised explosives handling certification
  • Current Dangerous Goods Security Card
  • Ability to follow procedures and work to plan
  • Current Manual C-Class Driver’s Licence

Benefits

Why Catalyst?

FIFO isn’t for everyone — it requires commitment and time away from home. That’s why we place strong emphasis on creating a supportive team culture, approachable leadership and an environment where people work hard, back each other in, and still find time to have a laugh and enjoy what site has to offer.

We offer:

  • 8:6 7:7 roster promoting genuine work-life balance
  • Health insurance eligibility
  • Salary sacrifice options available including novating leasing, airport car parking and more
  • Exposure to a growing and expanding underground operation
  • Opportunity to contribute beyond your core role and influence how we operate
  • Supportive and collaborative site leadership team
  • Ongoing development and internal progression opportunities

This role offers genuine development potential for someone looking to build their career within a growing Australian mining business.

If you’re ready to take the next step in your career, we’d love to hear from you. Applications are currently being accepted, so apply now.

title: Head of HR
description:
At Charterhouse, we don’t just deliver technology—we enable transformation. With over 30 years of experience, we are a trusted provider of integrated IT and communications solutions, helping organisations connect, collaborate, and secure their operations. Our team of 200 passionate professionals work across the UK and internationally, delivering innovative solutions in Enterprise Networking, Collaboration Spaces, Cyber Security, UC, AI and mobile

We’re proud of our client-centric approach, our strategic partnerships with world-class vendors, and our commitment to sustainability and community impact. Our values—Be Your Best Self, Own it, Love What You Do, Do the Right Thing —are at the heart of everything we do.

The Role

The head of HR is responsible for ensuring that all HR services and operations are aligned to and deliver the strategic business objectives for the Company in a smooth and efficient way.

Key Responsibilities

· Oversee and deliver efficient and structured HR operations, including recruitment, performance management, onboarding, offboarding, payroll, and benefits administration.

· Advise on and manage complex employee relations issues ensuring compliance with UK employment law, GDPR and organisational policies.

· Provide HR support and guidance to managers and employees throughout the employment life cycle.

· Drive process improvements ensuring HR systems and processes are efficient and fit for purpose.

· Develop review and implement HR policies procedures and guidance to ensure they are up to date and compliant with the latest UK employment law.

· Manage compensation and benefits and lead on annual pay review process including benchmarking of roles.

· Develop HR initiatives that drive employee engagement, productivity, and organisational success.

· Monitor and analyse HR metrics and trends to identify areas for improvement and recommend strategies to enhance HR effectiveness.

· Drive talent acquisition efforts, partnering with hiring managers to attract and onboard top talent while ensuring adherence to equal employment opportunity principles.

· Oversee performance management processes, including goal setting, performance evaluations, and career development plans, to drive employee growth and productivity.

· Develop and deliver HR training programs tailored to enhance the skills and capabilities of managers and employees.

· Build relationships with external HR vendors, consultants, and professional networks to leverage expertise and resources.

Requirements

What You Bring

· Proven experience as a Head of HR or similar leadership role, overseeing HR within the UK.

· Proven track record of delivery efficient and organised best practice solutions

· Successfully managing employee relations issues and fostering a positive work environment within the UK.

· Experience of leading a small HR team.

· Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and manage multiple priorities.

· In-depth knowledge of HR best practices, UK employment laws, and regulations.

· Strong understanding of talent acquisition, employee engagement, performance management, and employee relations within the UK context.

· Resilient and outcome orientated.

· Demonstrated ability to develop and implement HR strategies, policies, and programmes aligned with UK business objectives.

· Strong leadership and people management skills, with the ability to inspire and motivate teams.

· Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to effectively collaborate with stakeholders at all levels.

· Strategic thinking and problem-solving abilities to address complex HR challenges and drive initiatives.

· Proficiency in using HRIS systems, HR analytics, and other HR technology platforms.

· Understanding of data protection regulations and confidentiality requirements in handling employee information.

· Strong knowledge of compensation and benefits programs specific to the UK, including market trends and compliance considerations.

· Proficient in using MS Office applications, particularly Excel, for data analysis and reporting.

· Continuous learning mindset to stay updated with changes in UK HR practices, laws, and regulations.

Benefits

Join us, and your benefits and perks will include private healthcare, Medicash cashback, life assurance, workplace pension, cycle to work scheme, access to our employee assistance programme, savings discount, 20% EE discount that extends to your family and friends, a birthday gift voucher and day off, plus more.

title: scrum Master
description:

  • Excellent communication, facilitation, and interpersonal skills.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Ability to influence and drive change within teams and organizations.
  • Commitment to fostering a culture of continuous improvement and innovation.

title: Head of Partnerships
description:
Life @ AP+:

We are one connected team in pursuit of one inspiring purpose – to unite people and technology to power better experiences. Each of us has a part to play in making that happen. You’ll be encouraged to bring your big ideas forward and make a difference through your work. Taking steps forward in your career whilst still having room for fun, friendships, and flexibility in your daily life.

We’re driven by our core values: lead with heart, learn for tomorrow and live our legacy. A purpose like ours takes the inspired impact of an incredible team. Ready to change the game? We’re ready to help you do it.

The Purpose:

This is a senior commercial leadership role at the centre of how AP+ builds and grows strategic partnerships. As Head of Partnerships, you’ll set and lead the partnership strategy, build high-value, long-term relationships with key partners and stakeholders, and turn opportunity into sustainable commercial and customer value. You’ll operate across AP+ and with senior external stakeholders to shape significant proposals, lead complex negotiations and investment decisions, and ensure our partnerships deliver measurable outcomes aligned to AP+’s broader strategy.

Key Responsibilities the Role Owns:

  • Set the direction for AP+’s partnership strategy and translate organisational priorities into a clear portfolio of strategic partnership opportunities and plans.
  • Build, influence and steward senior-level relationships with key partners and stakeholders, positioning AP+ as a trusted, long-term strategic partner.
  • Identify, assess and prioritise opportunities based on strategic fit, business demand, commercial value and AP+’s capacity to deliver.
  • Lead significant commercial discussions, proposals and negotiations with senior customer and partner representatives, including contractual and commercial outcomes.
  • Shape investment appraisals and business cases, establish success measures and maintain a clear view of the value, performance and benefits delivered through partnerships.
  • Lead and develop a high-performing team while aligning partnership, sales and customer engagement activity across AP+ to strengthen customer loyalty and lifetime relationship value.

You’ll likely be a strong fit for this role if:

  • Deep Payments experience within a payment scheme or financial institution in areas such as Issuing, Acquiring, or Account to Account payments.
  • You’re an established senior leader with significant experience shaping strategic partnerships, business development and commercial strategy in complex organisations.
  • You have a strong track record of building credibility and influence with executive-level customers, partners and stakeholders, and of creating mutually valuable long-term relationships.
  • You’ve led complex commercial negotiations and significant proposals, with the judgement to balance strategic, customer, commercial and organisational considerations.
  • You can move comfortably between strategy and execution - assessing opportunities, developing investment cases, measuring benefits and ensuring partnerships translate into tangible outcomes.
  • You bring strong commercial acumen across partnership strategy, sales, investment appraisal, benefits management and performance measurement.
  • You’re an experienced people leader who can set direction, build capability and performance, and bring cross-functional teams together around shared commercial and customer outcomes.

What happens next:

At AP+, we believe in the power of passion, pride and purpose. Our team is driven by a shared mission to make a difference in the world of payments, and we're proud to work together towards this common goal.

If you’re a senior partnerships leader who can see where strategic relationships can create meaningful value and has the commercial leadership, influence and judgement to turn that opportunity into impact, we’d love to hear from you.

If you’re ready to be a game changer, please submit your application. The Talent Acquisition team will endeavour to review your application and notify you of the outcome within the next two weeks.

We want to remove all barriers to inclusion, so if you need advice or support with your application, we’re here to help. Please reach out to recruitment@auspayplus.com.au. We also encourage you to let us know your pronouns at any point during the recruitment process.

AP+ are not partnering with Recruitment agencies for this role.

title: DevOps Engineer (GovText)
description:
Assurity Trusted Solutions (ATS) is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Government Technology Agency (GovTech). As a Trusted Partner over the last decade, ATS offers a comprehensive suite of products and services ranging from infrastructure and operational services, authentication services, governance and assurance services as well as managed processes. In a dynamic digital and cyber landscape, where trust & collaboration are key, ATS continues to drive mutually beneficial business outcomes through collaboration with GovTech, government agencies and commercial partners to mitigate cyber risks and bolster security postures.

Who we are
GovText is a text related AI platform aims to avail a suite of reusable AI services to accelerate the incorporation of AI into WOG or agency-specific systems and applications. We are part of the GovTech's Data and Artificial Intelligence Platforms team. Where the mission is to deliver Data and AI assets for policy making, service delivery and operations across WOG.

What you will be working on

You will work on both small and large scale projects, building and maintaining and deployment of the infrastructure behind them. With a mix of on-premises and cloud infrastructure

  • Manage the development, deployment, orchestration and maintenance of application services for our products
  • Providing DevOps architecture implementation and operational support
  • Architecture and planning for on-premises and cloud deployments (Private and Public cloud)
  • Developing and managing processes, automation, best practices, documentation
  • Development and operation of continuous integration and deployment pipelines.

What it is like working here
We build products that serve a variety of agency users, who use them to solve highly meaningful problems pertinent to our society, from transportation, to education, to healthcare. The public sector is full of opportunities where even the simplest software can have a big impact on people’s lives. We are here to improve how we live as a society through what we can offer as a government.

  • Rapid Prototyping - Instead of spending too much time debating ideas we prefer testing them. This identifies potential problems quickly, and more importantly, conveys what is possible to others easily.
  • Reliable Productization - To scale an idea, a prototype or a Minimum Viable Product to a software product, we scrutinize and commit to its usability, reliability, scalability and maintainability.
  • Ownership - In addition to technical responsibilities, this means having ideas on how things should be done and taking responsibility for seeing them through. Building something that you believe in is the best way to build something good.
  • Continuous Learning - Working on new ideas often means not fully understanding what you are working on. Taking time to learn new architectures, frameworks, technologies, and even languages is not just encouraged but essential.

Requirements

We have products that resides in both on-premises and cloud infrastructure. Having that breadth of knowledge in government IT infrastructure and experience in government networks will help. A disciplined approach and strong problem-solving instincts are fundamental to succeed. Your aptitude for completing the tasks and attitude to continuous learning are more valued than any formal certification. To succeed, you will need to possess some of the following:

  • Excellent problem solving and methodical troubleshooting skills
  • Experience with on-premise deployments, government application and networking infrastructure/routing
  • Strong knowledge and experience in setup of infrastructure services e.g. Elasticsearch, Openshift, MongoDB, Postgresql
  • Knowledge and experience working with air-gapped on-premise deployments would be a good plus
  • Cloud computing deployment and management experience in AWS, Azure and some GCP knowledge
  • Strong scripting skills e.g. Python, Bash, JavaScript
  • Strong understanding of virtualization and networking concepts
  • Experience with patch maintenance, regression testing and security incident response
  • Experience with interactive workloads, machine learning toolkits and how they integrate with cloud computing e.g. Jupyterhub
  • Experience with highly scalable distributed systems
  • Breadth of knowledge - OS, networking, distributed computing, cloud computing, authentication, security, monitoring services and capacity planning

Join us and discover a meaningful and exciting career with Assurity Trusted Solutions!

The remuneration package will commensurate with your qualifications and experience. Interested applicants, please click "Apply Now".

We thank you for your interest and please note that only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

By submitting your application, you agree that your personal data may be collected, used and disclosed by Assurity Trusted Solutions Pte. Ltd. (ATS), GovTech and their service providers and agents in accordance with ATS’s privacy statement which can be found at: or such other successor site.

Benefits

Our employee benefits are based on a total rewards approach, offering a holistic and market-competitive suite of perks. These include leave benefits to meet your work-life needs and employee wellness programmes.

We champion flexible work arrangements (subject to your job role) and trust that you will manage your own time to deliver your best, wherever you are, and whatever works best for you.

title: Senior Self-Supervision Officer -KSA

title: Workshop Foreman
description:
MEKA24 is the automotive service, maintenance, and repair division of AUTO24, one of Africa’s fastest-growing used-car platforms. As the business continues to grow, the workshop plays a central role in delivering reliable vehicle preparation, servicing, and repair standards that support both operational performance and customer confidence.

This role is a key leadership position within the workshop. As Workshop Foreman, you will help drive high technical standards, strong team performance, and disciplined day-to-day execution across servicing, diagnostics, repairs, and vehicle reconditioning. You will work closely with technicians and cross-functional teams to keep work moving efficiently, maintain quality, and support continuous improvement as the business scales.

Responsibilities

  • Supervise, support, and motivate workshop technicians and assistants.
  • Allocate daily jobs based on technician skills, priorities, and available capacity.
  • Monitor workshop productivity, efficiency, turnaround times, and work in progress.
  • Conduct quality-control inspections before vehicles are released.
  • Assist technicians with complex diagnostics, repairs, and technical issues.
  • Ensure services and repairs are completed correctly and to manufacturer standards.
  • Review job cards and verify labour, parts, and repair information are accurately recorded.
  • Coordinate with the parts team to ensure required parts are ordered and available on time.
  • Identify additional repair or maintenance needs during vehicle inspections.
  • Provide accurate technical feedback to service, sales, and operations teams.
  • Reduce repeat repairs, comebacks, and unnecessary parts or labour costs.
  • Maintain workshop equipment, tools, cleanliness, and operational discipline.
  • Enforce health, safety, and environmental procedures.
  • Support recruitment, onboarding, coaching, and performance management of technicians.
  • Help implement efficient workshop processes as MEKA24 grows in South Africa.

Requirements

  • Qualified motor mechanic with 3-5 years of workshop leadership experience in an automotive workshop.
  • Strong experience in used-car reconditioning, general vehicle service, and maintenance.
  • Proven ability to diagnose complex mechanical and technical faults using diagnostic scanners and manufacturer diagnostic platforms.
  • Experience managing technician productivity, workflow, and quality standards in a busy workshop environment.
  • Knowledge of manufacturer procedures for vehicle servicing and repairs.
  • Experience using job card systems and parts ordering systems to maintain accurate repair, labour, and parts records.
  • Experience working cross-functionally with service advisors, parts, sales, operations, and used-car purchase and sales teams.
  • Experience enforcing safety standards in an automotive workshop.
  • Experience working in the South African Johannesburg market.
  • Eligible to work in South Africa.

title: AI & Data Analytics Lead
description:
We are looking for an AI & Data Analytics Lead to lead the company’s use of Artificial Intelligence, data, analytics, automation, and business intelligence.

This is a hands-on role for someone who sees AI as a fundamental part of how a modern company should operate—not simply as another technology or tool. The goal of this role is to identify opportunities across the organization where AI can improve how we analyze data, make decisions, automate processes, build reporting, work in Excel, interact with systems, and operate the business.

The ideal candidate combines strong data and BI skills with a deep understanding of modern AI tools and capabilities. You should be someone who naturally asks:

“Why are we doing this manually, and how can AI make this better?”

You will work across Finance, Operations, Marketing, Product, Technology, and other areas of the business to identify opportunities, build solutions, automate workflows, and create a more AI-enabled organization.

Key Responsibilities

AI Strategy, Implementation & Automation

· Lead the company’s practical adoption and implementation of AI across business functions.

· Identify opportunities where AI can eliminate manual work, improve decision-making, increase productivity, reduce errors, and create new capabilities.

· Evaluate emerging AI technologies, tools, platforms, and models and determine how they can be applied to the business.

· Build and implement AI-powered workflows rather than simply recommending AI tools.

· Integrate AI into existing business processes, systems, reporting, analytics, and workflows.

· Develop AI solutions that allow employees to interact with company data using natural language.

· Use AI to automate recurring analysis, reporting, research, data preparation, reconciliation, forecasting, and other manual processes.

· Identify opportunities to use AI for anomaly detection, trend identification, forecasting, classification, summarization, and predictive analytics.

· Develop repeatable AI solutions that can scale across departments.

· Establish best practices for responsible and secure use of AI with company data.

· Stay current with rapidly evolving AI capabilities and continuously identify new opportunities to apply them.

AI + Excel

· Transform how the company uses Excel by integrating AI into Excel-based analysis and workflows.

· Develop AI-enabled Excel solutions that automate analysis, reporting, data manipulation, modeling, and repetitive tasks.

· Connect Excel to Snowflake, APIs, BI platforms, and other data sources.

· Leverage tools such as Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, APIs, Power Query, Power Pivot, VBA, Office Scripts, and other emerging technologies where appropriate.

· Build workflows where users can ask questions of data and receive meaningful analysis without manually manipulating large datasets.

· Automate recurring Excel reporting and eliminate unnecessary spreadsheet-based manual processes.

· Identify opportunities to replace complex manual Excel processes with AI-enabled or automated solutions.

AI + Data & Business Intelligence

· Use AI to fundamentally improve how the company accesses, analyzes, and understands its data.

· Work extensively with Snowflake as a core data platform.

· Write and optimize SQL queries and develop data models and datasets for analytics.

· Use Tableau and other BI tools to develop dashboards and reporting.

· Incorporate AI into dashboards and analytics so users can more easily understand and interact with information.

· Develop natural-language or AI-assisted interfaces to company data where appropriate.

· Use AI to identify trends, outliers, relationships, and insights that may not be obvious through traditional reporting.

· Improve data quality and identify inconsistencies using automated and AI-assisted processes.

· Partner with Technology and Engineering to improve data pipelines, integrations, APIs, and the overall data environment.

Business Analytics & Decision Support

· Partner with leadership and business teams to identify high-value analytical and AI opportunities.

· Translate business problems into data- and AI-driven solutions.

· Develop KPIs, dashboards, analytical models, forecasts, and decision-support tools.

· Use AI to accelerate and improve forecasting, scenario analysis, budgeting, financial analysis, and business planning.

· Create tools that allow leadership and business users to quickly answer questions using company data.

· Move reporting from static historical information toward automated, predictive, and actionable intelligence.

Process Automation

· Identify manual and repetitive processes throughout the organization that can be automated using AI, APIs, workflow tools, or traditional automation.

· Build automated workflows that connect data, applications, and AI models.

· Look beyond the existing process and determine whether AI can eliminate the process entirely or fundamentally redesign it.

· Measure the time, cost, and efficiency improvements generated by AI initiatives.

· Create scalable solutions rather than one-off experiments.

Requirements

What We’re Looking For

· 5+ years of experience in Data Analytics, Business Intelligence, Data Science, AI, Automation, or a related field.

· Strong hands-on experience with AI and generative AI tools and a demonstrated ability to apply them to real business problems.

· Strong experience with Snowflake and SQL.

· Strong experience with Tableau or another enterprise BI platform.

· Advanced Excel skills, including Power Query, Power Pivot, data modeling, and automation.

· Experience integrating AI with Excel, APIs, databases, BI tools, and business applications.

· Ability to build practical AI solutions—not just experiment with ChatGPT or other AI tools.

· Strong understanding of data structures, data modeling, analytics, and business intelligence.

· Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to look at an existing process and identify how technology and AI can fundamentally improve it.

· Ability to communicate complex technical concepts to non-technical users.

· Comfortable working independently and taking projects from idea through implementation.

· Strong business acumen and curiosity about how the entire business operates.

Technical Skills

Required:

· Generative AI / LLMs

· AI workflow design and implementation

· Snowflake

· SQL

· Tableau

· Advanced Excel

· Power Query / Power Pivot

· Data modeling

· Data visualization

· Automation

Strongly Preferred:

· Python

· APIs

· Office Scripts / VBA

· Microsoft Copilot

· OpenAI / ChatGPT APIs

· Claude / Gemini or similar LLM platforms

· dbt

· Data pipelines / ETL

· AI agents and agentic workflows

· Machine learning / predictive analytics

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is not simply a BI analyst who knows how to use ChatGPT.

You are someone who understands data, technology, and business—and who sees AI as a tool that can fundamentally change how a company operates.

You are constantly looking for ways to:

· Automate instead of manually perform.

· Predict instead of simply report.

· Ask AI instead of manually search.

· Build instead of repeatedly analyze.

· Connect systems instead of move data between them.

· Give employees answers instead of making them build reports.

· Eliminate processes instead of making inefficient processes slightly faster.

You should be excited by the opportunity to take an existing process, understand how it works, and ask:

“What would this look like if we built it today with AI?”

What Success Looks Like

Within the first year, this person should help establish an AI-first analytics and automation culture across the organization.

Success will include:

· AI is being used across Finance, Operations, Marketing, Product, and other business functions.

· Significant manual reporting and analysis has been automated.

· Employees can interact with company data more naturally and efficiently.

· Excel-based processes have been transformed through AI and automation.

· Snowflake and Tableau provide a scalable foundation for analytics.

· AI is integrated into reporting, forecasting, analysis, and decision-making.

· New AI-powered workflows and tools are continuously being developed.

· Leadership has faster access to better information.

· The company is using AI not just to work faster, but to work differently and better.

·

Benefits

Competitive Compensation, Medical, Dental, Vision, & 401K with Company Match!

Excellent project management and organizational skills.

Experience working with Data governance

title: INTERNAL LEADERSHIP OPPORTUNITY: Sanctuary Leader
description:
INTERNAL LEADERSHIP OPPORTUNITY: Sanctuary Leader

Help clinicians feel supported, known, and inspired in their work.

  • Opportunity: Internal Chatterboxes SLP
  • Reports to: Clinical Director
  • Clinical Commitment: 25 Billable Hours/Per Week + 5 Days Per Week (M-F)
  • Step into a salaried leadership role while continuing to remain connected to clinical practice.

The Opportunity

The Sanctuary Leader is a culture stabilizer, clinical mentor, and steady, visible presence for a group of our clinicians. This leader helps create connection and psychological safety, strengthens clinical practice, and brings warmth, clarity, accountability, and follow-through to the everyday clinician experience.

This is a player-coach role. The Sanctuary Leader remains actively engaged in clinical work while serving as a trusted bridge among clinicians, the Clinical Director, the Founder, and the broader leadership team.

What You Will Do

  • Clinical mentorship and excellence
  • Maintain an active caseload of approximately 25 billable clinical hours per week so your leadership remains clinically grounded and relatable.
  • Provide ongoing mentorship and consultation across the career span, including support for Clinical Fellows, CF mentors, SLPA supervisors, new clinicians, and seasoned SLPs.
  • Help clinicians think through complex or stuck cases in a safe, judgment-free space while reinforcing sound clinical judgment and professional accountability.
  • Guide clinicians with documentation and compliance, including progress notes, evaluation reports, IEP/IFSP goals, eligibility decisions, assessment selection, and productivity expectations.
  • Share evidence-based resources, therapy materials, research, approaches, and continuing education opportunities while ensuring diverse voices and perspectives are represented.
  • Connect clinicians with colleagues who hold relevant specialty expertise across Chatterboxes.
  • Support ethical practice, scope of competence, and sustainable workload; elevate clinical or wellness concerns to the appropriate leader when needed.

Culture and Team leadership

  • Create a consistent, warm team presence through approachable Slack support, casual touchpoints, recognition, invitations to connect, and prepared co-facilitation of team meetings.
  • Model Chatterboxes values through everyday professionalism, respect, care, reliability, and communication.
  • Serve as a calm communication bridge: bring patterns and concerns to leadership with context, then translate responses back to clinicians clearly and without speculation or escalation.
  • Help change feel contained and understandable by explaining what is happening, why it matters, what it means for clinicians, and where support lives.
  • Represent the full organization consistently, including when you may personally have approached a decision differently.
  • Maintain healthy leadership boundaries by connecting clinicians to the right support rather than becoming the resource for everything.
  • Clinician growth and accountability
  • Hold a monthly 1:1 with each clinician in your Sanctuary and provide responsive support between meetings.
  • Compile and analyze monthly review forms to document progress, contributions, strengths, and clinical efforts that may support merit-based increases.
  • Evaluate clinical performance on an ongoing basis and document concerns clearly and promptly when they arise.
  • Partner with the Clinical Director on annual reviews and biannual merit-based compensation reviews by contributing grounded observations and team insights.
  • Redirect compensation and financial questions to the formal review process, Head of Operations, or Chatterboxes' Financial Empowerment benefit, as appropriate.

Internal Application Process

Interested internal candidates should apply through Workable during the five-business-day application window. Candidates who meet the initial criteria will be invited to complete a brief written leadership project, followed by leadership interviews.

Ready to help shape the next chapter of Sanctuary Leadership?

Submit your application by Monday, 8/31/26. Any related questions may be directed to Devin!

Requirements

Who We Are Looking For:

🩵 A current Chatterboxes SLP who is clinically grounded and genuinely enjoys helping other clinicians grow.

🩵 Warm and relational, with the courage to pair support with clear accountability.

🩵 Steady under pressure and able to bring calm, context, and clarity to uncertainty.

🩵 A strong listener and communicator who can synthesize information and communicate it thoughtfully.

🩵 Trusted by peers because of how you consistently show up - not simply because of tenure.

🩵 Comfortable with boundaries and able to recognize what belongs within your role and what should be elevated or redirected.

🩵 Open to feedback, self-reflection, and continued growth as a leader.

🩵 Proactive without overstepping; dependable with follow-through.

🩵 Excited about the Chatterboxes vision and willing to help carry it forward consistently.

Support and Partnership

The Sanctuary Leader reports to the Clinical Director and collaborates closely with the Sanctuary Leadership Team, Head of Operations, Founder, and Chatterboxes Leadership Coach. The role is strongest when questions are brought to the appropriate leader, established processes are trusted, and emotional support needs are directed toward appropriate professional resources.

Benefits

Benefits of the Role

  • Step into a salaried leadership role while continuing to remain connected to clinical practice.
  • Expand your impact beyond direct services by leveraging your clinical knowledge and experience to mentor, guide, and strengthen fellow SLPs.
  • Learn alongside and receive support from Chatterboxes’ leadership team, including Megan, Devin, Clinical Director, Jen H, Head of Operations; Jen E, Leadership Coach; and Danielle, Sanctuary Leader.
  • Build your confidence, judgment, communication skills, and effectiveness as a people leader with the support of experienced leaders and coaches.
  • Level up your career by developing transferable skills in mentorship, team leadership, performance development, communication, and organizational strategy.

Play an important role in shaping the clinician experience and carrying the Chatterboxes Sanctuary vision forward!“Leadership isn’t about having all the answers. It’s about helping others feel supported enough to discover what’s possible.”
