title: National Head of Distance Education
description:
About CEM

Christian Education Ministries (CEM) is a protestant non-denominational, Christian Education organisation, whose mission is to develop each and every student to be equipped spiritually, academically, socially and physically to flourish into their full potential, and be a positive influence on the world around them. CEM is wholeheartedly committed to excellence in education so that students are “well known, well loved, and well taught” by dedicated trained Christian staff.

CEM is a growing network, with 16 schools (including the Australian Christian College schools) in 5 states. Five of our schools operate a Distance Education (DE) Program with a combined enrolment of over 3000 students.

We are seeking a suitably qualified candidate to join our team as the National Head of DE. This is a new role in our organisation and the successful candidate would support our DE teams and programs across the country.

About the Role

The key function of the National Head of DE is to ensure that our DE schools are growing (through new growth and increased retention) and that our DE schools are providing a quality experience for students and parents. The National Head of DE will work closely with all of the DE Leadership Teams, and where relevant, School Principals. You will also be working as a part of the CEM Education Services Team.

Key Job Functions:

  1. DE Leadership through the CEM Vision and the CEM Way
    1. Provide strategic leadership in DE according to the CEM Vision and the CEM Way.
    2. Meet regularly with the DE Leadership Teams and develop their capacity to lead and manage.
  2. DE Growth & Development
    1. Lead initiatives to grow the Distance Education schools in their state & national context.
    2. Identify & build new markets & sub-markets that could benefit from DE.
    3. Improve retention of existing DE customers.
  3. DE Quality Experience
    1. Ensure that DE customers receive the highest quality of service that CEM aspires to throughout its organisation.
  4. Other Projects as determined, identified, or directed by the Assistant CEO.

This full time role commences January 2027.

Requirements

You will be a highly capable and collaborative Christian education leader with:

  • A committed Christian faith and active involvement in the church.
  • A strong alignment with the CEM Vision, mission and CEM Way values.
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in education, with postgraduate qualifications in leadership or education highly regarded.
  • Current or recent teacher registration in an Australian state or territory.
  • Significant leadership experience within a school or education environment.
  • Experience in Distance Education, online learning or flexible learning environments, highly regarded.
  • Demonstrated ability to provide strategic leadership and develop the capacity of leadership teams.
  • A proven ability to lead growth, innovation and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Strong commercial and strategic thinking, including the ability to identify new markets and improve enrolment retention.
  • A strong commitment to delivering an excellent experience for students and families.
  • Excellent interpersonal, communication and influencing skills, with the ability to build effective relationships across multiple schools and states.
  • The ability to analyse data, identify trends and translate insights into practical action.
  • Strong organisational and project-management skills, with the ability to manage competing national priorities.
  • A willingness and capacity to travel regularly to CEM schools across Australia.
  • A current Working with Children Check or the ability to obtain the relevant clearances.

Benefits

CEM employees can access a range of staff benefits, including:

  • WHEREFIT health & wellbeing benefits program with 15-50% off leading brands
  • Competitive salary, salary sacrificing & packaging options.
  • Grow in your faith, skills and experience.
  • EAP program
  • Being part of an authentic faith community that shares regular bible devotions and prayer.

title: Supervisor - Entertainment & Events - Props

description:

This role is a practical, workshop-led position requiring a highly skilled all-rounder who can diagnose, repair, and maintain a wide range of assets - from electric show vehicles and mechanical props to the on-board playback systems and scenic elements - ensuring safe, reliable, and show-ready operation at all times.

The Supervisor will lead by example as a “roll up your sleeves” problem solver, supporting daily operations, troubleshooting issues in real time, and maintaining the highest standards of safety, functionality, and visual quality.

Key Functional Tasks:

Show Props & Scenic Maintenance

  • Maintain, repair, and refurbish all hand props, scenic elements, and show set pieces
  • Carry out practical repairs including:
  • Gluing, bonding, and structural fixes
  • Fiberglass repairs and touch-ups
  • Painting and finishing
  • Basic carpentry and fabrication
  • Ensure all props remain show-quality and on-brand

Show Vehicles (EV Fleet) Maintenance

  • Oversee maintenance of electric show vehicles including:

o Tires, brakes, steering, and mechanical systems

o Battery systems and charging infrastructure

o Safety features (horns, lights, warning systems)

  • Perform routine inspections and preventative maintenance
  • Liaise with specialist vendors when required, but own first-line diagnosis and fixes

Technical Playback & Embedded Systems

  • Maintain and troubleshoot show playback systems, including:

o iPads / tablets

o Tascam / solid-state playback devices

o Basic audio signal paths and connections

  • Diagnose and resolve issues related to:

o Cabling, connectors, and power supply

o Playback reliability and triggering systems

Workshop & Fabrication

  • Operate as a practical workshop lead, maintaining tools, equipment, and workspace
  • Support fabrication and modification of props and show elements as required
  • Manage safe use of tools (hand tools, power tools, soldering equipment, etc.)

Operational Support

  • Attend rehearsals, technical run-throughs, and live performances as required to observe how hand props are used in practice
  • Identify potential wear, damage risks, or handling issues arising from performer use and staging
  • Implement practical solutions to improve prop durability and longevity, including reinforcement, protective finishes, and handling adjustments
  • Develop and introduce appropriate on-stage and backstage storage solutions to protect props during use and between performances
  • Provide on-the-spot troubleshooting and emergency repairs during rehearsals and live operations as required

  • Coordinate prop preparation, installation, removal, and storage for shows and special events

Daily excellence

  • Ensure all props are maintained to required artistic, operational, and safety standards.

Requirements

Knowledge & Experience;

Minimum 3–5 years’ hands-on experience in:

  • Theme parks, live entertainment, events, or similar environments

Strong practical experience across multiple disciplines:

  • Mechanical repair
  • Basic electrical systems
  • Scenic/prop fabrication
  • Technical troubleshooting

Experience working with:

  • Show props and scenic elements
  • Vehicles or moving assets (preferred)
  • Playback or show control systems (basic level)

Understanding of live entertainment production processes and backstage operations.

Ability to work flexible schedules including nights, weekends, and holidays.

Education & Certifications:

Strong problem-solving mindset – able to diagnose and fix issues quickly

Confident with tools and hands-on repair work

Practical knowledge of:

Calm under pressure during live operations

High attention to detail and safety

· Analyzing the competitive landscape for potential investments

· Tracking progress of portfolio companies post investment

· Working on investment updates and valuations for quarterly and annual reports

· Coordinating due diligence processes

· Supporting and leading negotiation of terms for new investments

· Contributing to knowledge management and translation of project and programmatic data

· Tracking fund deal flow and coordinating reports and summaries for weekly team meetings

· Compiling impact data for portfolio companies

· Providing organizational support as needed

Requirements

Professional Skills, Education and Experience

· Completion of a bachelor’s degree in a relevant field, plus a graduate degree or relevant level of experience

· 5+ years of work experience in a position providing extensive exposure to investing into companies

· Experience developing financial models and conducting sensitivity analysis

· Investment experience in the health, food, co-op or social entrepreneurship sectors

· Demonstrated experience in preparing and negotiating complex transactions and balancing the programmatic needs of community-based organizations with sound underwriting judgment and risk mitigation

· Familiarity with one or more of Capital Impact’s five core geographies

· Ability to generate deal flow using own contacts and experience

· Demonstrated interest in and experience in impact investing

· Exposure to boards of directors as a member or observer

· Experience leading the due diligence process for potential investments

· Ability to interact with bankers, investors and others

· Highly skilled in writing investment summaries, investment memos, preparing PowerPoint presentations and related word-processing and spreadsheet skills

· Comfort working in an environment with little supervision

· Strong communication and presentation skills

· Strong attention to detail, analytical, critical thinking and organization skills

· Strong written and verbal communication skills

· Demonstrated ability to take initiative and leverage knowledge and resources to solve problems

· Experience prioritizing and managing multiple projects, assignments and meeting tight deadlines

· Passion for community and economic development, impact investing, and social justice

· Advanced user of Excel, Word, Power Point and Google Suite. Experience with Salesforce is a plus

title: Co-Founder & CTO - AI Catalyst Discovery Venture
description:
The Venture

Discovering a better catalyst still runs on trial and error: form a hypothesis, synthesise a few candidates, test, repeat, for years, at a cost measured in millions. Most of the search space is never touched. It is one of the slowest, most expensive bottlenecks between the chemicals industry and a lower-carbon future.

We're building the company to change that. Spun out of A*STAR, our platform closes the loop between computation and the lab: machine learning proposes catalyst compositions worth making, simulation screens them, and an automated experimental workflow validates the winners, feeding every result back to sharpen the next cycle. It reaches candidates a traditional programme never would, in a fraction of the time and cost.

The beachhead is CO₂ to methanol and green chemicals, where industry pull is real and the economics work. Most catalyst work is improving a recipe that already exists, and the incumbent supplier usually keeps that business. The opportunity is a new process with no incumbent catalyst, and an unusual number of those are arriving between now and 2030. The core discovery IP is being licensed from A*STAR, with the inventor on board as an advisor. What the venture needs now is a founding technical leader to own the science and build the company around it.

The Role

You'll be the founding CTO. You'll own everything from the discovery campaign to a catalyst a customer can actually run in their process, taking a validated workflow and turning it into the engine of a real business. You'll work alongside a commercial co-founder (CEO), a dedicated ATUM venture team, and the inventor-advisor.

Together, we'll:

  • Direct the catalysis: which chemistries we pursue, how we design the discovery campaigns, how we read the results
  • Own the licensed workflow and the automated experimental loop end to end
  • Take candidates from prediction to a manufacturable, deployable catalyst, not a paper
  • Build defensible IP the company owns, including new catalyst compositions worth patenting
  • Sit across the table from chemical customers and turn their process problems into targets we can solve
  • Build the lab foundation and the science team behind it

This is not a job. It's a founding journey where you share the risk, the upside, and the impact.

Requirements

  • Deep in heterogeneous materials, ideally catalysis: You hold a PhD in Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, or Materials Science, with roughly 8 to 15 years turning chemistry into things that run in the real world. Heterogeneous catalysis is the strongest fit, but we're open to adjacent ground: electrocatalysis, energy materials, nanomaterials, surface and interface chemistry. What matters is that you understand surfaces, synthesis and reactors.
  • Industry-tested: You've done this inside a chemicals, catalyst or materials company's R&D, or a deep-tech startup. You know why a promising result dies at scale-up. You care whether a catalyst is manufacturable and deployable, not whether it makes a good paper.
  • Comfortable directing the AI, not running it: You won't write the models yourself, but you can steer a computation-and-ML-driven discovery loop and decide what to make and test next.
  • You've built physical capability before: A lab, a rig, a pilot line, a testing setup. Ideally on a budget that forced hard choices about what to buy, build or outsource.
  • A builder, not a career scientist: You want to run a company, not hold a senior title inside someone else's. You're ready to leave a stable role, take equity over salary, and own the outcome, and you're energised by conservative industrial buyers rather than put off by them.

Benefits

Why Build With Us

  • A hard problem worth owning: A real scientific and commercial challenge with a clear prize, and the science is yours to lead.
  • A de-risked starting point: A validated workflow with industry programmes behind it, a licence from A*STAR, an inventor handing over the know-how, and real industry pull. Not a blank page.
  • Founder-led: You're a co-founder with a C-level seat and meaningful founding equity, not an employee.
  • Funding-ready: ATUM backs the build with pre-seed capital and grant access, plus follow-on support from our investor network.
  • Hands-on partners: We're in the trenches on product, hiring, and fundraising, not just on the cap table.

Based in Singapore, where the lab and the A*STAR relationship sit. If you're not here, we sponsor and support EntrePass applications.

This is a from-zero build with real risk, and compensation is equity rather than salary until we raise. If what you want is a stable senior R&D role, this isn't it. If you want to own the science and build the company, read on.

title: Latin America Economist
description:
Capital Economics is one of the world’s leading independent economic research companies. We provide country and regional research on most of the major developed and emerging economies. We also provide overview services covering the global economy and financial markets, and have dedicated services providing research on commodities and on the property sector.

Founded in 1999, we have gained an enviable reputation for original and insightful research and have built up a wide and distinguished client base. We produce publications for world-wide distribution and offer support to clients in their respective time-zones through our offices in London, Toronto and Singapore.

Overall, more than 1,500 institutions subscribe to our publications. The majority are in the financial sector, including some of the world’s largest investment banks and wealth managers. We also have a growing number of corporate clients, as well as many relationships with governments and central banks, both in developed and emerging economies.

The role

A macroeconomist working within our highly-regarded Latin America team, reporting to the Senior Emerging Markets economist. This person will possess strong analytical skills, be willing to challenge the consensus and have the ability to express themselves with clarity and concision. You will have an opportunity to contribute across the range of our work on Latin America and emerging markets more broadly

  • Contribute to our views and generate forecasts for key Latin American economies and their financial markets. Try to identify where consensus expectations are wrong.
  • Produce frequent high-quality written economic analysis for our clients. This ranges from short notes published immediately after an event to longer, more detailed publications on issues that are likely to influence an economy over a number of years
  • As your expertise grows, you would present these views directly to clients, whether in person, on the telephone or conference calls, or at seminars. You would also be encouraged to build your own profile, including through media appearances.

Requirements

  • A strong academic background with, at least, a good undergraduate degree in economics or a related discipline.
  • At least two years’ experience analysing macroeconomic issues within the public sector, a financial institution or a research organisation. Previous experience covering Latin America would be an advantage but is not essential.
  • The ability to communicate in an engaging and authoritative manner. You will be expected to contribute to internal debates and present the company's views to external parties, including clients and the media. The hiring process involves delivering a presentation.
  • Above all, strong writing skills. Most of our output is written, so the ability to structure a written argument in English and express it clearly and concisely is a must. The hiring process includes a writing assessment.

title: Senior Backend Engineer - Core Java & Systems Integration
description:
About Clear Labs

Clear Labs harnesses the power of next-generation sequencing (NGS) to simplify complex diagnostics for clinical and applied markets. By creating a fully automated platform that brings together DNA sequencing, robotics, and cloud-based analytics, Clear Labs democratizes genomics applications to deliver clarity. Our turnkey platform accelerates outcomes and improves accuracy from food-borne pathogens to infectious diseases.

The Opportunity

We are looking for a hands-on Senior Backend Software Engineer to join our lean, high-impact engineering team as a core platform owner. This role is a critical replacement for a key team member and focuses exclusively on the "connective tissue" of our platform—architecting robust Java backend services and low-latency integration bridges between physical lab automation hardware and our cloud ecosystem.

This is an opportunity for a purist backend systems engineer. You will own the deterministic state machine that ensures our physical robotics and cloud orchestration layers operate in perfect synchronization.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Core JVM Service Development: Own, develop, and maintain a distributed matrix of 30+ microservices using Java and Spring Boot.
  • Systems Integration: Analyze, design, and build bulletproof, replay-safe API integrations between Clear Labs, external bioinformatics analysis pipelines, and clinical middleware (LIMS/EHR).
  • State Orchestration & Messaging: Drive architectural resilience using Domain-Driven Design (DDD) principles, leveraging Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), RabbitMQ, and GCP Cloud Pub/Sub for asynchronous event streaming.
  • Data & Performance Engineering: Optimize and harden existing transactional database services (MySQL, Redis) for extreme reliability under high concurrency and massive data scale.
  • On-Market Tier Support: Act as the high-level technical lead for production escalations, triaging and troubleshooting deep infrastructure bugs within our grid service layers.
  • Compliance & Hardening: Implement technical security controls as we advance toward SOC2 and ISO 27001 compliance standards.

Requirements

Position Requirements

  • Legal Invariant: Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Clear Labs does not provide employment-based visa sponsorship now or in the future.
  • Location Invariant: Able to commute daily to our San Carlos, CA headquarters for a 100% on-site schedule.
  • Experience: 5+ years of professional backend software development experience in a production environment.
  • Core Language: Elite proficiency in Java and the Spring Boot ecosystem (Dependency Injection, Spring Data, Transaction Management).
  • Infrastructure & Messaging: Hands-on experience operating containerized workloads on cloud infrastructure (strictly GCP/GKE preferred) utilizing message brokers like RabbitMQ or Cloud Pub/Sub.
  • Databases: Deep knowledge of relational databases (MySQL), including schema design, constraint invariants, query tuning, and indexing strategies.
  • Testing Philosophy: A strict affinity for writing comprehensive unit and integration tests (JUnit, Mockito, TestContainers) as a mandatory definition of "done."

Nice to Have

  • Prior experience building LIMS or EHR data integrations (HL7, FHIR).
  • Familiarity with cybersecurity frameworks (SOC2/ISO 27001 control mapping).
  • Experience writing automation scripts in Python or TypeScript.

Physical Requirements

  • Able to sit or stand at a computer for extended periods and use monitors and related hardware comfortably.

Benefits

  • Salary range: $121,500–$150,000

  • Employer-Sponsored Basic Life/AD&D, 60% Short-Term/Long-Term Disability
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

title: IRS26312 Dryland Crops Director
description:

Build Strategic Partnerships and Mobilize Resources:

  • Build Strategic Partnerships: Strengthen collaboration scientific integration with research institutions, national agricultural systems, governments, development partners, foundations, and private-sector actors to accelerate innovation and sustainable impact across dryland agricultural systems.

  • Secure Resources for Long-Term Impact: Lead resource mobilization efforts and cultivate investor confidence in scientific excellence and delivery to secure the investments required to enhance CIMMYT’s reach, impact, and long-term sustainability.

  • Strong experience in building strategic partnerships and mobilizing resources from bilateral and multilateral donors, foundations, governments, and other development partners, ideally within complex international agricultural systems.
  • Deep understanding of agricultural development challenges and opportunities in low- and middle-income countries, particularly within dryland production systems.
  • Exceptional communication, stakeholder engagement, and influencing skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships and represent the organization effectively across diverse international environments.
  • A collaborative and empowering leadership style, with a demonstrated ability to lead diverse teams, build organizational capability, foster equitable partnerships, and deliver impact through networks.

Benefits

Our Commitment to You:

title: Founder (CEO) - Elemental Sensing for AI Data Center Cooling
description:
Who We Are

ATUM is a Singapore deep-tech venture builder and investor. We build companies from breakthrough, IP-backed research, bringing capital, operational muscle, and partners from industry, VC, and government into every build. We've built and backed 15 ventures, and we invest in fast-scaling deep-tech with real fundamentals, not hype.

The Venture

Liquid cooling is fast becoming the backbone of the AI data center, and the coolant running through it is now mission-critical. Yet the fluid is still watched the way it was decades ago: a sample sent to a lab, once a quarter, or after something has already failed. Corrosion doesn't creep evenly either. It jumps when a loop gets topped up with the wrong fluid or an inhibitor runs down, and quarterly sampling finds the damage months later with no way to trace the cause.

We're building the company to change that.

The core is an inline coolant-monitoring platform, developed at NTU, that uses laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy to read the coolant in real time, identifying and quantifying the dissolved metals that signal corrosion, down to which component is degrading and how fast. The optical monitors entering the market today read the fluid indirectly; this one measures the metals directly, which they cannot.

The first market is coolant monitoring for data center operators, where a reliability gap is opening fast as the industry shifts to direct liquid cooling and no inline elemental product yet exists. A corporate partner in data centre cooling is already engaged. The science works and the technology is early. It's a platform-led deep-tech company at the centre of the AI infrastructure build-out, with a clear path to category leadership.

The Role

You'll be the founding CEO. You own the commercial side of the business: who buys this, what they pay for it, how it gets sold, and how the company gets funded.

Your founding CTO is already in place. He spent four years in US designing optical sensing hardware for consumer products shipped in the tens of millions, and led national-scale hardware deployment for the Singapore government. A laser and photonics specialist from another ATUM venture is advising on the optical build. The NTU inventors stay on as technical advisors, alongside a dedicated ATUM venture team.

Together, we'll:

  • Turn early operator interest into paid pilots, then into repeatable contracts
  • Set the product positioning and pricing, and build the business case that gets a data center operator to approve the spend
  • Raise pre-seed and seed capital alongside the CTO and ATUM
  • Open up the channels: colocation and hyperscale operators, cooling OEMs, and their service partners

This is not a job. It's a founding journey where you share the risk, the upside, and the impact.

Requirements

  • B2B sales track record: You've sold technical products or infrastructure to industrial, data center, energy, or process customers. Long sales cycles, several people in the room, and you carried the number.
  • New product sales: You've sold something new, something the customer wasn't buying before, and built the business case to get it approved internally.
  • Comfortable with hardware: You understand pilots, deployment costs, service models, and what it takes to go from one site to fifty. You can hold your own with engineers without being one.
  • Resilient & ready: You have the runway to commit full-time, and you know building deep-tech hardware takes grit, iteration, and patience. You don't need to be Singapore-based, though you'll need to be here often.

Bonus

  • Existing relationships with data centre operators, colocation providers, or cooling OEMs. Not required, but it would help.

Benefits

Why Build With Us

  • A real starting point: Working science, a corporate partner engaged, and a CTO already building. Not a blank page.
  • Founder-led: You're the CEO, with meaningful founding equity.
  • Straight talk on money: There's no salary at the start. ATUM funds the pre-seed and we have accelerated access to Singapore government grants, which together fund the early build. Salary comes when the seed round closes. You'll need runway to bridge that, and we'd rather say so now than three conversations in.
  • Funding-ready: ATUM backs the build with pre-seed capital and grant access, plus follow-on funding from our investor network.
  • Hands-on partners: We're in the trenches with you on product, GTM, and fundraising, not just on the cap table.
  • Domain access: Labs, technical experts, early adopters, and an ecosystem already engaged.

title: Underground Service Crew | 8:6 7:7 FIFO from Perth | Gold | Permanent Full Time
description:
About Catalyst Metals

Catalyst Metals Limited owns and operates the Plutonic Gold Mine in the Eastern Gascoyne region of Western Australia. The operation is undergoing continued underground growth, with multiple mining areas progressing from development into production.

Catalyst is focused on building a long-life gold business supported by disciplined technical planning and strong operational execution.

Catalyst Metals Limited is listed on the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX code: CYL).

Catalyst Metals Ltd is an equal opportunity employer and encourages applications from people who identify as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander.

About the Role

With more than 15 years of mine life ahead of us, there’s never been a better time to join our underground team. We take pride in the ground we work in – competent rock, a strong safety culture and a modern Sandvik fleet.

Backed by long-term job security and genuine progression pathways, this is a place where you can build a sustainable underground career while continuing to develop your skills.

As an Underground Service Crew Operator, you'll play a critical role in supporting safe and productive underground gold mining operations. Working alongside experienced development and production crews, you'll be responsible for installing and maintaining the essential underground services and infrastructure that keep our operations moving safely and efficiently.

This opportunity offers genuine variety. From ventilation installations and service extensions through to cable bolting, infrastructure maintenance and supporting production activities, you'll be exposed to a broad range of underground mining tasks while working across our growing operations.

As Catalyst continues to expand, you'll have the opportunity to develop your skills, mentor less experienced team members and contribute to the success of a growing Australian gold producer. Backed by long-term job security and ongoing investment across the Plutonic Gold Belt, this is an excellent opportunity to build your future with a company focused on growth.

Key Responsibilities

· Scope, plan and execute underground service crew activities

· Install and maintain underground services and ventilation in development and production headings

· Install, remove and maintain secondary ventilation fans

· Install cable bolts in accordance with ground support plans

· Assist Jumbo Operators and Charge-up Operators as required

· Operate underground dump trucks and other mobile equipment when required

· Complete thorough pre-start inspections and report equipment defects promptly

· Assist electricians with the installation of high-voltage cables

· Construct ventilation walls and associated infrastructure

· Operate equipment in accordance with manufacturers' specifications and site procedures

· Mentor and support the development of Service Crew team members

· Maintain high standards of safety, housekeeping and compliance across all underground work areas

Requirements

About You

To be successful in this role, you will have:

· Previous underground Service Crew experience within a hard rock mining environment

· Experience installing and maintaining underground services and ventilation

· Cable bolting experience

· Strong commitment to safety and safe work practices

· Ability to work effectively both independently and within a team environment

· Strong organisational and problem-solving skills

· Ability to adapt to a variety of underground tasks and priorities

· Current WA C-Class Driver's Licence

· Current Dangerous Goods Security Card (DGSC)

· National Police Clearance (or ability to obtain)

Desirable:

· Underground gold mining experience

· Experience assisting Jumbo and Charge-up crews

· Underground truck operating experience

· HR Driver's Licence

· Working at Heights certification

· First Aid Certificate

· Experience mentoring and training underground operators

Benefits

Why Catalyst?

FIFO isn’t for everyone — it requires commitment and time away from home. That’s why we place strong emphasis on creating a supportive team culture, approachable leadership and an environment where people work hard, back each other in, and still find time to have a laugh and enjoy what site has to offer.

We offer:

  • 8:6 / 7:7 roster promoting genuine work-life balance
  • Health insurance eligibility
  • Salary sacrifice options including novated lease, airport car parking and more
  • Short commute from camp to site with own private room
  • Fully equipped gym, swimming pool, multipurpose sports court and more
  • Exposure to a growing and expanding underground operation
  • Opportunity to contribute beyond your core role and influence how we operate
  • Supportive and collaborative site leadership team
  • Ongoing development and internal progression opportunities

This role offers genuine development potential for someone looking to build their career within a growing Australian mining business.

If you’re ready to take the next step in your career, we’d love to hear from you. Applications are currently being accepted, so apply now.

title: Executive Director, The Appellate Project at NYU School of Law
location: New York, New York, United States
description:
Position Title: Executive Director

Organization: TAP at NYU School of Law

Reports to: Executive Director, Center on Race, Inequality, and the Law at NYU School of Law

Position: Hybrid remote; candidates must be available to work in person approximately 2–3 days per month from the NYU School of Law in New York City

Location: Remote, NYC or DC preferred

Salary: $135,000-$150,000 annually + comprehensive benefits

About The Appellate Project

After seven years of operating as a standalone 501(c)(3), The Appellate Project (“TAP”) is excited to begin its next chapter as an initiative operating within the Center on Race, Inequality, and the Law at New York University School of Law. While TAP’s organizational structure is evolving, its mission remains the same: fostering emerging leaders as they work to build a more just, equitable, and representative appellate field through mentorship, professional development, community-building, and access to career pathways within the appellate profession.

At TAP, we believe our highest courts should reflect all of our communities. Since launching in 2019, TAP has supported more than 600 law students through its award-winning programming, providing access to mentorship, clerkship support, skill-building opportunities, and networking pathways within the appellate bar. TAP’s growing network includes judges, law clerks, attorneys, alumni, and legal leaders committed to expanding access to the appellate profession and strengthening a judiciary that better reflects the diversity and lived experiences of communities nationwide.

The Center on Race, Inequality, and the Law at NYU School of Law engages in research, advocacy, litigation, and public education to advance systemic change and address issues of race and inequality. Through this partnership, TAP is uniquely positioned to deepen its national impact while continuing to expand opportunities for future appellate advocates and legal leaders.

Learn more at The Appellate Project

The Role

The Appellate Project seeks an Executive Director to lead the organization into its next phase of growth, institutional development, and national impact. This is a pivotal leadership opportunity for a strategic, entrepreneurial, and equity-driven leader who will strengthen TAP’s organizational infrastructure, expand partnerships and fundraising efforts, and help shape the organization’s long-term vision and sustainability.

While TAP will operate within the Center on Race, Inequality, and the Law at NYU School of Law, the Executive Director will lead TAP’s strategic direction, programmatic growth, external partnerships, and community engagement.

Reporting to the Faculty Director of the Center on Race, Inequality, and the Law, the Executive Director will oversee TAP’s strategic and operational leadership, including program implementation, fundraising, partnerships, and organizational development. This individual will work closely with NYU leadership, funders, judges, alumni, law firms, volunteers, and strategic partners to strengthen TAP’s visibility, deepen partnerships, and expand opportunities for participants nationwide.

The Executive Director will also serve as a public representative and thought partner within the appellate and broader legal community. The ideal candidate is a collaborative and emotionally intelligent leader with strong strategic instincts, operational experience, fundraising acumen, and a demonstrated commitment to expanding access and representation within the legal profession.

Requirements

Key Impact Areas

Strategic Leadership & Organizational Direction

  • Lead the development and execution of TAP’s long-term strategic vision and organizational priorities
  • Guide TAP through its next phase of organizational growth and integration within the Center on Race, Inequality, and the Law at NYU School of Law
  • Translate mission and strategic priorities into actionable plans, measurable goals, and sustainable operational practices
  • Partner closely with NYU leadership and key stakeholders to strengthen organizational infrastructure and long-term sustainability
  • Foster a collaborative, inclusive, and accountability-driven organizational culture grounded in transparency, relationship-building, and mission alignment
  • Serve as a strategic thought partner on opportunities to strengthen TAP’s long-term impact, visibility, and influence within the appellate field

Program Leadership & Organizational Capacity

  • Oversee the design, implementation, and evaluation of TAP’s mentorship, clerkship support, alumni engagement, and professional development programming
  • Ensure programming remains innovative, participant-centered, equity-driven, and aligned with organizational priorities
  • Manage program operations, logistics, timelines, and participant engagement across virtual and in-person initiatives
  • Develop systems, processes, and operational structures that support effective program delivery and organizational growth
  • Supervise future staff, consultants, vendors, volunteers, mentors, and program partners

External Engagement & Network Leadership

  • Serve as TAP’s primary ambassador and public representative within the appellate and broader legal community
  • Cultivate and strengthen relationships with judges, law firms, alumni, funders, law schools, bar associations, and strategic partners
  • Represent TAP at conferences, convenings, panels, and external events
  • Build partnerships that expand opportunities for TAP participants and strengthen TAP’s national visibility and influence
  • Support communications, convenings, and thought leadership efforts that elevate TAP’s mission and impact
  • Engage diverse stakeholders with credibility, diplomacy, and a strong commitment to collaboration and relationship-building

Fundraising & Financial Sustainability

  • Lead the development and implementation of TAP’s fundraising and revenue strategy in partnership with Center leadership and NYU Law’s development team
  • Cultivate and steward relationships with individual donors, foundations, institutional partners, and philanthropic stakeholders
  • Support ongoing fundraising campaigns, donor engagement efforts, and development initiatives
  • Oversee programmatic budgets, grant reporting, and responsible financial stewardship
  • Help build a diversified and sustainable funding base to support TAP’s continued growth and impact

Impact, Evaluation & Systems

  • Develop evaluation frameworks and performance metrics to assess program effectiveness and organizational impact
  • Use participant feedback, data, and outcomes to strengthen programming and inform strategic decision-making
  • Track and report key organizational and programmatic indicators
  • Oversee technology platforms, CRM systems, and project management tools that support organizational operations and engagement

Qualifications and Leadership Profile

The ideal candidate will bring a demonstrated commitment to racial equity, representation, and expanding access within the legal profession, including an understanding of systemic barriers impacting historically underrepresented communities. They will be a collaborative and emotionally intelligent leader who is energized by mentorship, relationship-building, and mission-driven leadership.

Qualified candidates will possess:

  • At least 10 years of progressive leadership experience within nonprofit, legal, educational, advocacy, or other mission-driven organizations
  • Experience with fundraising, donor engagement, partnership development, and institutional relationship management
  • Strong strategic leadership and organizational management experience, including program development, operational oversight, and organizational growth
  • Experience leading within lean, dynamic, and evolving environments with the ability to manage multiple priorities effectively
  • Exceptional relationship-building and communication skills, with the ability to engage diverse stakeholders and serve as a compelling public representative
  • Strong project management, organizational planning, and operational problem-solving skills
  • Experience developing systems, evaluation frameworks, and organizational infrastructure that support long-term impact and sustainability

Additional qualifications include familiarity with CRM systems, project management platforms, and technology tools that support engagement and organizational operations. Familiarity with appellate law, judicial clerkships, legal pipelines, or legal advocacy work is preferred.

The ideal candidate will also demonstrate sound judgment, emotional intelligence, strategic flexibility, and a collaborative leadership style grounded in transparency, accountability, and relationship-building.

Additional Information About the Position

This is a full-time exempt position operating in a hybrid environment. While the role is primarily remote, the Executive Director will be expected to work in person approximately 2–3 days per month from the Center’s office on NYU Law’s campus in New York City. Candidates based in the Washington, DC metropolitan area will also be considered.

The role requires occasional evening and weekend commitments, as well as limited national travel to support programming, fundraising, partnerships, and external engagement efforts.

As TAP continues to grow, the Executive Director will play a central role in strengthening organizational systems, deepening partnerships, and ensuring the organization remains both mission-driven and operationally strong.

Benefits

Employees of New York University are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package, which includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, retirement plans, generous paid time off, tuition benefits, commuter benefits, and wellness resources. Additional information about NYU’s benefits offerings is available on the university’s careers and benefits website.

To Apply

The Appellate Project has retained the services of Charity Search Group to coordinate the search for this position. To apply, please complete this online application. If you have questions or need accommodations, please contact Kelly Stevens at kellystevens@charitysearchgroup.com ​or visit

Equal Opportunity Employer

The Appellate Project, housed at NYU School of Law, is committed to building an inclusive workplace and strongly encourages applications from individuals with diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. New York University is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, veteran status, marital status, citizenship status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law.

Research shows that individuals from historically underrepresented communities often hesitate to apply for roles unless they meet every qualification. If you are excited about this opportunity and believe you could thrive in this role, we encourage you to apply, even if your experience does not align perfectly with every listed qualification.
